## 27. Amendment: P9a build (2026-10-04)

What the P9a build (issue #24, PR "P9a: static publisher") found or settled against the plan and the issue, and why. P9a builds the `publish` role in both audiences (`publish [--audience public|owner] [--once]`), the static files of A§9.1 with their contracts, the dirty log, day versions and settled days, the Caddy routes (precompressed static files, the degraded stand-in, the owner site), the compose services, the 18 healthchecks, the owner canary in production, the web's static-first fetch chain and the `static` checks of `verify-prod`. The PR adds one hand-written and one generated migration, no runtime or dev dependency, no capture spec, egress host, registry row, audience or channel flag. **This section ticks no criterion**: the evidence column of the issue is filled in the PR, and the [agent-prod] checks wait for the deploy.

**What was built, in short.** `apps/server/src/publish/` (`write.ts` the only way to the file system, `plan.ts` the pure planner, `cycle.ts` the loop, `render/*` one module per file kind, `index.ts` and `main.ts`); `packages/contracts/src/static.ts` (web-importable: paths, the settled rule and the file contracts) with `static-owner.ts` and `status.ts` (server only); `packages/core/src/forecast-hold.ts` (the step-hold the web uses for a future `t` without the API); `load/dirty.ts`, `load/canary.ts` and the tail of `load/migrate.ts`; the migrations `20261107000001_p9a_publish.sql` and `20261107000002_views_publish.sql`; `deploy/web/{site,owner}.caddy`, `Caddyfile.owner`, `deploy/compose.yaml` (`publish`, `publish-owner`) and `deploy/compose.owner.yaml`; the web's `lib/data/{chain,static}.ts`. Architecture: A§4, A§6 "P9a reality", A§9.1 "P9a as built", A§9.3, A§11.1, A§11.3, A§11.4 and A§11.5. Runbook: `docs/runbooks/publisher.md`. Threat model 4.35: T-PUB-1 to T-PUB-3 (new), T-OWN-1, T-OWN-3, T-OWN-4, T-WEB-1, T-GEO-7 and T-DB-2.

**Deviations from the plan and the issue.**

| # | Plan or issue | What P9a does, and why |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | The loader gets `SELECT, INSERT` on `publish_dirty` (plan §9 C4) | **`INSERT` only** (and USAGE on the sequence). The loader never reads the log, so it gets no SELECT (least privilege; invariant 2, T-LOAD-3); `runMigrate` prunes rows older than 3 days as the owner role under the loader lock |
| 2 | The owner site: "`route` first: `basic_auth { … }`" (plan §4.6) | **`basic_auth` at the site level.** Measured on Caddy 2.11.4: a `basic_auth` inside a `route` does not gate the `handle` blocks (Caddy orders `handle` before `route`) and answered 200 without credentials. The 401 and every other error get `private, no-store` and `noindex, nofollow` through `handle_errors`, because error routes get no site `header`; the owner site fails closed because Caddy refuses to start without the imported credential file |
| 3 | `caddy-owner` as a compose profile or in `compose.yaml` | **An overlay file**, `deploy/compose.owner.yaml` (plan decision 2, A§11.1): the CI deploy job adds it with `-f`, production uses it only from P12a, so a missing owner secret can never stop the public Caddy |
| 4 | The files are listed, no contract for the warnings files | **A `WarningsFile` contract is added** (GeoJSON feature collection with `schemaVersion`, `generatedAt`, `day`, `attribution`), as is a status contract per family |
| 5 | The degraded stand-in on `/api/v1/snapshot*` through `handle_errors` | **Two mechanisms on the exact path `/api/v1/snapshot`:** an upstream 502, 503 or 504 response (the API answers 503 itself) is caught only by `handle_response` inside the proxy, a dead upstream only by `handle_errors 502 503 504`; the proxy of that path is its own, so no other API path changes (`copy_response` would drop the upstream's headers) and a site-wide `handle_errors` does not touch `file_server` 404s (KG-107). Both need `file_server { status 200 }` or the stand-in would carry the error's status |
| 6 | A future `t` through the static files | **API first, with the static `forecast/latest.json` as the degraded fallback**: the API holds the states, the file only the held values (no state), so a future `t` falls back to it only when the API is down or Caddy's stand-in answered |
| 7 | `registry_visible:<family>` = `{series id: [staleness_s, lic_display, lic_history_export]}` (plan §9 C10) | `{series id: [staleness_s, history_export]}`: a series in the family's series view has display by construction, so the flag adds nothing. The fingerprint also holds digests of the NL-4 reference rows and of the family's attribution rows (a changed attribution is reason `registry`, so a settled file stays a function of (day, version)) |
| 8 | The owner status like the public one | **No loader backlog in the owner status** (`backlogAgeS` null, no backlog-based `degraded`): the owner role cannot read the loader view (public-only), and widening that is not P9a's call (KG-219) |
| 9 | The e2e stand-in renders what production renders | **The web e2e stand-in (`apps/server/test/e2e/api.ts`) renders one settled day** (the newest), the other settled days stay 0 in `meta.dayVersions` and go to the API; the real Caddy and the full chain are exercised by the CI `e2e` and `deploy` jobs (KG-221) |
| 10 | `Health.loader.last_commit` as the newest `loaded_at` | Read by `lastCommit(tx, family, now)` with a one-hour range qualifier, which the `security_barrier` view pushes into the new `ingest_batch_loaded` index (an unbounded `max` is a sequential scan). It is the one value for `meta.latestFrom`, `status.json` and `Health.loader.last_commit` |
| 11 | Settled size "about 5 GB" for all static files | About 45 KB plain per snapshot, 3–4 GB a year, **an estimate that is not yet measured in production** (A§11.4) |

**Owner decisions of the plan (2026-10-04, binding for this PR).** The history window is a render-time exclusion, not a bump (plan §9 C5; dormant while every source keeps `history_export`: KG-114, KG-215); `rws_load` still has no DELETE anywhere; the pools are `rws_publish` 3 and `rws_owner_api` 2; `reconcileRollups` has no dirty hook (plan §9 C9: a rollup repair is a bug that raises an alert, KG-220); `static rerender` is [agent-prod] only (plan §9 C23).

**[U] list.** KG-210 (a dated warnings file is frozen), KG-211 (owner-mode presentation in the web is #25), KG-212 (the owner site is off in production until P12a, which also generates `owner_basic_auth`), KG-213 (the owner site mounts no basemap tiles), KG-214 (DE-6 Stand has no history before P9a), KG-215 (a no-history series is in no file but `latest.json`), KG-216 (the stand-in is a 404 before the first publish), KG-217 (the publisher heartbeat is liveness, not success), KG-218 (the precompressed sibling window), KG-219 (the owner status has no loader backlog), KG-220 (a rollup repair does not re-render frames), KG-221 (the e2e stand-in renders one settled day), KG-222 (the `static rerender` and `static lag` checks and the settled size wait for production). Updated: KG-202 (the owner `forecast/latest.json` is now written; the owner API is P9b), KG-114 (the static files carry the rule). Threat model 4.35, no new risk-register entry: a flood of dirty rows only costs re-renders, bounded to one settled day a cycle and a 35 s budget (T-PUB-2).

## 28. Amendment: P9b build (2026-10-05)

What the P9b build (issue #24, PR "P9b: API hardening", `Closes #24`) found or settled against the plan and the issue, and why. P9b makes `/api/v1` a bounded fallback behind the P9a static hot path: a DB-concurrency semaphore, a hardened LRU with precompressed variants, per-client token buckets keyed on a header Caddy sets from the TCP peer, strict and capped input, `v` and immutable answers, `POST /api/v1/beacon`, an `attribution` array on every answer, the owner API `api-owner`, the withheld, owner and channel canaries, an OpenAPI snapshot, the k6 load test in CI and the `verify-prod` sweeps. The PR adds one generated migration (`20261108000001_views_history.sql`), no runtime or dev dependency (k6 is a release binary checked by sha256 in `loadtest.yml`, a tool only), no capture spec, egress host, registry row, audience or channel flag. A§9.2, A§9.3, A§11.1 and the threat model (4.37, T-API-2 to T-API-5) carry the design; `docs/runbooks/api.md` the operation.

**What was built, in short.** `apps/server/src/api/`: `limiter.ts` (token buckets, key normalisation), `semaphore.ts`, `versions.ts` (day versions, immutability), `lru.ts` (the P4a LRU with lazily added zstd and gzip variants and `negotiate`), `channels.ts` (`ROUTES`, `rateClass`, `channelViews`), `answer.ts` (`bodySources`, `attributionOf`, `historyCapMs`), `beacon.ts`, and `routes.ts`, `health.ts`, `cache.ts`, `params.ts`, `data.ts`, `states.ts` changed to run one pipeline per family; `apps/server/src/attribution.ts` (moved from `publish/render/attribution.ts` and `dates.ts`, shared with the publisher); `app.ts` (`createApp({family, …})`) and `main.ts` (`api [--audience public|owner]`, `API_POOL`, `RWS_API_DB_CONCURRENCY`); `packages/contracts` (`api.ts` data and wire schemas through the `apiContracts` factory, `api-owner.ts` server only, `health.ts`, `openapi.ts`) with `openapi.json` and `openapi-owner.json` (`scripts/gen-openapi.ts`); `scripts/gen-views.ts` (`HISTORY_MIGRATION`) and the migration; `deploy/web/{site,owner}.caddy` (`X-Rws-Client`, `@beacon`, `Reporting-Endpoints`); `deploy/compose.owner.yaml` (`api-owner`, `owner_edge`); `deploy/tests/e2e/run.sh` and `api-sweep.mjs`; `.github/workflows/loadtest.yml`, `deploy/tests/loadtest/{k6.js,compose.loadtest.yaml}` and `scripts/seed-loadtest.ts` (with `apps/server/test/e2e/seed.ts` extracted from the e2e API); `scripts/verify-prod.ts` (`api sweep`, `settled sweep`); the publisher's `stations.json` (`schemaVersion` 2, `api` per series) and the web's schemas.

**Deviations from the plan and the issue.**

| # | Plan or issue | What P9b does, and why |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Build-prompt task 10: the owner API serves "settled snapshots and frames" | **`/frames` is deferred to #26**, as the issue's scope says. P9b registers its `heavy` rate class and lists it in `ROUTES` as `planned` (channel `api`), so the canary sweeps and the `verify-prod` sweep cover it the day #26 adds the handler (a test fails if a non-planned `api` route lacks a sweep). The owner view gets settled snapshots from owner `/snapshot` and no frames until #26 (KG-224) |
| 2 | Task 10: `api-owner` on "edge + db" in the compose file | **`api-owner` is in the overlay `deploy/compose.owner.yaml` and on its own networks `owner_edge`** (internal, shared only with `caddy-owner`) **and `owner_db` (internal, shared only with `db`; review F1: on the shared `db` network the public `api` could have opened `api-owner:8080`): the public `caddy` and `api` share no network with it (C15; A§11.1). Production starts the overlay only with P12a, so this release changes nothing on the VPS: no new healthchecks.io slug (like `api`, `api-owner` has the container's node healthcheck only), no bootstrap re-run (KG-226) |
| 3 | The plan's first draft: health stops caching errors | **Health keeps its 5 s error cache** (C5, so the watchdog still sees "down" on a real database error) and gains a last-good body: with no permit free it answers that body (at most 10 minutes old (longer than the watchdog's 5-minute look, review F4)) with `no-store` and `X-Stale: 1`, else 503 `busy` with `Retry-After: 2` |
| 4 | KG-114: a tripwire test only | **KG-114 is closed by the cap** (`historyCapMs`): an answer that holds a series without `history_export` is cached and sent for at most the time left of its history window, and is never immutable. `history-export.test.ts` stays as a registry tripwire |
| 5 | Forecast values: the history window "on every channel" | The observation views had it; the forecast value views and the Q2 functions did not. **The new migration `20261108000001_views_history.sql`** adds it (same columns and signatures, grants kept); the P8a bodies are frozen as `forecastValueV2` and `forecastAt(…, 'v2')`, so `20261106000002` regenerates byte for byte. Dormant while every source keeps `history_export` (KG-230) |
| 6 | C19: fail closed when a body source has no attribution row | **Fail closed on a source outside the family's source view** (`attribution_missing`, 503), not on a missing row: LU-3 is an owner source with no attribution text, so a row-based rule would make every owner body that names LU-3 a 503. A family source with no row gives no entry (KG-229) |
| 7 | C4: the health 503 body stays `{"status":"down","error":"unavailable"}` | **Every error body carries `attribution: []`** (owner decision 5 of the handoff, which wins over C4), the health 503 included: `{"status":"down","error":"unavailable","attribution":[]}`; the watchdog's strict parse follows |
| 8 | C6: the day versions are read inside the compute's transaction | **A short query of its own after the data read** (`readVersionTag`), compared with the in-memory versions now and with the versions the key was built from: simpler (the data read is `readStates`' own transaction), and a bump between the reads makes the answer not immutable, never wrongly immutable (KG-231) |
| 9 | C7: k6 with `--network host` | **k6 runs in a client network namespace (`ext`) with `--local-ips`**, one process on each of six public-looking addresses, because a host-originated request to a published port is masqueraded to the bridge gateway, which the limiter keys as `unknown-gw`. TLS is verified against the e2e root (`SSL_CERT_FILE`); the limiter is never disabled |
| 10 | C16: `settled sweep` | Returns **N/A** while no settled day is complete or none of the sampled files is served; the CI allow list requires PASS for `api sweep` only (`ci.yml`) |
| 11 | A§9.2: `GET /stations/{id}` | **Not built** (C23): not a P9b criterion; `ROUTES` lists it as planned (KG-225) |
| 12 | The plan's cache lifetime of an immutable answer | The LRU keeps the age-class TTL (at most 24 h), never a year; `immutable` is only a per-request header (C6). A§9.2 table: `/series/{id}/forecast` takes no `v` (`unknown_parameter`) |
| 13 | One OpenAPI document | **Two committed snapshots**, `openapi.json` and `openapi-owner.json` (the owner schemas with `audience`), both compared byte for byte; the owner API serves the second at its own `/openapi.json` |

**Decided during the build (plan §9, binding).** The limiter is off in `createApp` unless passed and the role always passes it (C1); the limiter's own monotonic clock; a peer in a private, loopback, unique-local or link-local range is `unknown-gw` with 100 times the buckets and logs `limiter_gateway_key` at most once a minute (C7), with a CI probe that the masked Caddy access log shows the runner's real prefixes and never a bridge gateway, and an [owner] check in production (KG-228); the beacon has a global bucket of 20/s, burst 100, beside the per-client 1/10 (C14); Caddy adds `@beacon` before the unchanged `@write` guard as an expression, not a `path` matcher (C3); `stations.json` is `schemaVersion` 2 with `api` on the static series metadata only (C18); `seed.ts` is not edited (C8): the new tests add their own rows, and `654321.987::real` renders `654322` (both are grepped).

## 29. Amendment: P10a build (2026-10-06)

What the P10a build (issue #25, PR "P10a: UI core", `Part of #25`) found or settled against the plan and the issue, and why. P10a is the web's classified map: the modes State, Δh and Q with their legend and palette, the river lines and the warning areas at `t`, the station panel with its basis, Δh, forecast band and credits, the live mode, the paged table, the multilingual label catalogue and the owner mode (banner, badges, owner schemas and labels), with the owner site, the CI end-to-end for it and Lighthouse. The PR changes no ingestion, database, migration, API route or `site.caddy`; it adds one dev dependency (`lighthouse` 13.5.0, the ADR-lite line is in the PR) and no capture spec, egress host, registry row, audience or channel flag. A§10 and the threat model (4.39, T-WEB-2, T-OWN-5, T-WEB-3) carry the design.

**What was built, in short.** `packages/core` (`./qc` and `./trend` subpaths: `QC`, `SUSPECT_BITS`, `deltaH`, `TREND_BAND`, re-exported by `classify.ts` and `crosswalk.ts`); `packages/contracts` (`sourceEntry` and the public `StaticSources` moved to `static.ts`, re-exported by `static-owner.ts`); `apps/web/src/lib` (`url/url.ts` mode and river, `data/contracts.ts` the per-site schema record, `data/chain.ts` and `data/api.ts` the loaders and hooks for sources, status mode, warnings, recent and rivers, `data/change.ts`, `data/warnings.ts`, `stationStates.ts`, `labels/`); `features/map/` (stations by mode, `rivers.ts`, `warnings.ts`, `icons.ts`, `popup.ts`); `features/legend/` (palette, legend, mode control, river chip); `features/station/` (basis label, panel, chart and its pure `chartModel.ts`, credits); `features/table/` (mode columns, paging); `features/owner/` (banner, badge, `contracts.ts`, `labels.gen.ts`, the lazy `index.ts`); `scripts/gen-web-labels.ts` with `check-i18n`; `deploy/web/owner.caddy` and `deploy/compose.owner.yaml` (tiles and rivers); the CI `e2e` job (owner Caddy, the artifact `e2e-test-results`), `deploy/tests/e2e/run.sh` (owner smoke) and `isolation.sh`; `apps/server/test/e2e/{api,public-seed,owner-seed}.ts`; and the Playwright projects and specs listed in CLAUDE.md.

**Deviations from the plan and the issue.**

| # | Plan or issue | What P10a does, and why |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | T12: a web-local owner schema for `sources.json` | **The owner record `OWNER_CONTRACTS`** (`features/owner/contracts.ts`, a lazy chunk) re-exports the owner family's schemas from `@rws/contracts/static-owner` and builds the owner API answers from `apiContracts` (C1: the public schemas refuse the owner canary's source id, and the owner API adds `audience`). `chain.ts` and `api.ts` take a `Contracts` record, public by default, and `hidden(source)` drops `CANARY-*` by source id on read. The public initial closure holds only `PUBLIC_CONTRACTS` |
| 2 | None | **`strictExecutionOrder`.** The owner chunk shares `@rws/contracts` with the page, so Rolldown put the schemas in a shared chunk that ran before `lib/zod.ts` set `jitless`: a CSP eval violation on every page. `build.rolldownOptions.output.strictExecutionOrder: true` in `apps/web/vite.config.ts` fixes it; the CSP is unchanged |
| 3 | T1: the default mode from `status.json` `classification.mode` | **By audience (C11):** the public `classification.mode` on the public site, `classification.owner.mode` on the owner site, with a narrow schema (the rest of the file ignored); `dh` is the `delta` mode, a failed read or none is `delta`, and the mode is undefined until the file has answered, so there is no state-to-delta flash |
| 4 | T1: Δh at any `t` | **`dh24` of `latest.json` at the current bucket, a second snapshot at t − 24 h otherwise, none after now.** Both values must exist, else null. The trend is core's `deltaH`. `/snapshot` is unchanged (KG-194 closed). After now the Δh mode shows hollow markers and "n.v.t." in the popup, table and panel, and a page-level note (`dh_future_note`) |
| 5 | T3: "hidden" after 25 hours | **No hidden state (C3):** the at-t functions return a value only inside the series' `staleness_limit`, so the page never sees an older one; `test/staleness-limit.test.ts` fails if a registry limit passes 25 hours. Stale stays the P4b rule (older than twice the step). The age of a series' last value in `latest.json` is KG-233 (**built in #87, PR #107:** `latest.json` gains `lapsed` and `lapsedAge`; a series with no value whose newest value is at least `stalenessLimitSeconds` old is lapsed, and its station (no value at t) is drawn as a small grey dot (`stale` without `has`; `LAPSED_COLOUR`), distinct from the hollow "no value" ring, and the popup, table and panel say "no value within the staleness limit"; a station whose series are all over 25 hours old (`HIDE_AFTER_S`, `lib/stationStates.ts`) is hidden from the map, table and search; a link to it still opens the panel, which says so, with no popup. The legend's stale key shows the dot and names both rules. A series that never had a value, a past `t` and the API fallback have no age, so nothing changes there; "older than two measuring steps" stays the cue for a carried-forward value) |
| 6 | T3: a suspect value has a dashed outline | **A second outer ring**: a MapLibre circle cannot be dashed. The panel and table say it in words (an "!" note) |
| 7 | T3: icons as a sprite; "self-hosted sprite" | **Icons are drawn at run time** (`features/map/icons.ts`: `hatch`, `hatch-area`, `tri-up`, `tri-down` as RGBA, added with `map.addImage`): no sprite file, no request, no `data:` or `blob:` URL, the CSP and the asset pins unchanged (V7) |
| 8 | T5: warnings at any past `t` | **A contract gap, no server change.** The publisher writes a dated file only for ended UTC days and only for the public family, so `t` earlier today (and any past `t` on the owner site) reads `latest.geojson` filtered by validity, which lacks areas that ended earlier today, and the page says "Waarschuwingen eerder vandaag mogelijk onvolledig / Earlier warnings today may be incomplete"; a 404 on a dated file does the same. KG-232 proposes that the publisher write the current day's dated file every cycle |
| 9 | T4, T5: river alerts and rivers | **`warnings-line` draws DE-6 river alerts** (KG-189), **`warnings-hatched` the LHP class "2"** (a pattern cannot use feature-state, V7); `?river=` highlights by the tile property `river_id` and is kept until `reaches-<ver>.json` has answered (C17). There is no tippecanoe fixture: the e2e asserts the layer, its `source-layer` and the filter, and a unit test the filter builder (C7) |
| 10 | T3: a keyboard `<datalist>` search; `scripts/bundle-report.ts` | **Both cut (C15).** The table's buttons give keyboard selection and focus returns to the invoking button (else the station list); `map-build.test.ts` prints the per-chunk gzip sizes. A marker has no focus of its own |
| 11 | T6: "also forecast by" and other runs listed separately | **One run per series (C16).** `recent.json` and `/series/{id}/forecast` hold one run, and only `forecast/latest.json` names other providers; the optional line is not built (KG-236) |
| 12 | T-i18n: `labels-index.gen.ts` maps (source, scale, code) to message keys | **To the message functions imported by name**, so the code never indexes the `m` namespace with data (a computed key makes the bundler keep every message). The map is a null-prototype object read with `Object.hasOwn`; owner labels are in the generated `features/owner/labels.gen.ts` only (the owner chunk) |
| 13 | Plan C1 and C13: widen the dist grep (`api-owner`, `owner_basic_auth`, `/srv/rws/owner`, `:8443`, an `owner.<domain>` pattern, the first 60 characters of every owner `private_basis` clause; `CANARY-` only in the owner chunk; `static-owner` not in the public closure) | **As planned, by the lead after the docs pass.** `build.test.ts` builds with a manifest and fails on every C13 needle in any file of `dist/`, on an owner chunk (`features/owner/{contracts,labels.gen,index}.ts`) or the owner sources schema in a page's initial load, and on the literal `CANARY-` outside the owner chunks. That last check found the owner source-id regex of `OwnerForecastLatest` in the main chunk (`packages/contracts/src/forecast.ts`, shared with the public schema): `OwnerForecastLatest` moved to `static-owner.ts` (server imports follow). `check-boundaries` enforces the import rule: in `apps/web/src`, `@rws/contracts/static-owner` only under `features/owner/`, `/api-owner` and `/status` nowhere, and never the root of `@rws/core` (fixture `scripts/fixtures/boundaries/web-owner`) |
| 14 | T-core: only subpaths | **Also the `StaticSources` move** and a `Contracts` record; `QC`, `SUSPECT_BITS`, `deltaH` and `TREND_BAND` come from `@rws/core/qc` and `@rws/core/trend` (the root pulls XML and CSV code) |
| 15 | T10: attribution | **Already built in P3 (C9):** a unit test asserts `createMap` passes no `customAttribution` and that the new river and warning sources set no `attribution` |
| 16 | T-chart: alert bands between levels | **`markArea` bands between consecutive levels of one source, at 15 % opacity, a heuristic:** every reference with a canonical unit counts as a level, so a low-water reference also starts a band (KG-234). The lines are right |
| 17 | A§10: `reaches` coloured by feature-state | **Not built**: the river line is one colour (the reach colouring, flow and playback are P11, #26) |
| 18 | Owner decision 1: the owner e2e in the CI `e2e` job | **As decided, with C4:** the owner API is a second in-process listener of the e2e API (`createApp({family: 'owner'})`, `rws_owner_api`) on the runner's primary address, which the owner Caddy reaches as `api-owner`; the public API listens on `172.17.0.1`, what `host-gateway` resolves to. The publisher's pool closes before the owner API's opens (the role's limit is 4). The password is made in the job (`openssl rand -hex 16`, hashed in the Caddy image, masked, never written to the repository). One owner smoke runs in the compose `deploy` job on the production build (`E2E_OWNER_SMOKE=1`) |
| 19 | Owner decision 2: owner tiles | **KG-213 closed:** `owner.caddy` has the tiles and river routes of `site.caddy` before `@data`, `compose.owner.yaml` mounts exactly `/srv/rws/tiles` and `/srv/rws/public/data/v1/rivers` read-only, and `isolation.sh` and `test/caddy-owner.test.ts` pin that exact list (C6). Neither is a host file (`host_files()`): no bootstrap re-run. The owner site runs only with P12a |
| 20 | Owner decision 3: Lighthouse | **`lighthouse` 13.5.0, exact pin (published 2026-09-18), a root dev dependency with a BOM row.** The spec is a Playwright project (`lighthouse.spec.ts`, Chromium with `--remote-debugging-port=9222`), not a script (C8); it asserts performance at least 80, accessibility at least 95 and LCP under 2.5 s on the median of 3 runs and writes JSON and HTML to `test-results/lighthouse/`, uploaded with `actions/upload-artifact` (no upload path of its own). It measures `dist-e2e`. The lockfile gains 91 entries (lighthouse and 90 more, a second Zod major, `puppeteer-core` and `@sentry/node` among them, inert unless opted in); no build script, so `allowBuilds` is unchanged |

**Decided during the build (plan §10, binding).** Query keys carry the audience and every query waits for the contracts record (C1); the public e2e seed is raw SQL on base tables, never a view name (C2: `public-seed.ts`), the owner seed likewise (C19: `owner-seed.ts`, called only with `E2E_OWNER_PUBLISH_DIR`); no `site.caddy` change; the banner is a region with the persistent one-line text and the sources list in a `<details>`, never dismissible (C14); a lookup on data uses `Object.hasOwn` over a null-prototype map; an `href` from data only for `https:`; the compose job's owner smoke reaches `caddy-owner` through the host network with `--add-host owner.$DOMAIN:<its rws_edge address>` and does not join the network (C5); `workers: 1`, every project has its own `testMatch` or `testIgnore` (C5).

**Local e2e (WSL, the stand-in `server.ts` for both sites, all projects).** 261 passed, 47 skipped by design (the Chromium-only route and spike checks, the compose-only specs), 0 failed: chromium, firefox and webkit (the public specs), no-webgl2, cvd (9 screenshots), lighthouse, and owner-chromium, owner-firefox and owner-webkit. The specs found two product defects, fixed in the PR: the triangles of a change were lone glyphs that axe could not judge (now SVG), and an owner-source forecast band had no owner badge.

**Lighthouse performance (owner decision 2026-10-06: keep 80, 95 and 2.5 s and optimise).** The first measurement was 42: a layout shift of 0.85 (the loading frame was one line tall, so the arriving content pushed the footer out of view; a child margin collapsed through `<main>`), 2.4 s of total blocking time (MapLibre's set-up, about 1.7 s at 4× CPU) and an LCP of 2.9 s. Three changes: `.main` has `display: flow-root` and a minimum height of one screen (CLS 0); the map starts only when its container comes within 200 px of the viewport (`useMapLibre`, IntersectionObserver; on a phone it sits below the time bar, the controls and the legend, on a 1024 × 768 desktop it starts at once); and the loading frame shows what the static shell says (the intro and the not-official note), so the largest paint does not wait for the data. Result: performance 90, accessibility 100, LCP 2,457 ms (medians of 3). CI on the same build then measured performance 73, 95 and 74 (total blocking time 1.3 s, 0.2 s, 1.3 s on the shared runner), accessibility 100, LCP 1.9 s; the owner chose to report Lighthouse in CI rather than gate on it (`LIGHTHOUSE_GATE=1` gates; KG-237, the P12 performance pass).

### Review round 1 (2026-10-06)

Two read-only reviews with the #25 prompts (code: Sonnet, high, approve with minor changes; security: Sonnet, high, pass with four lows), one PR comment; the lead fixed every finding but two nits:
- **Code, major:** the chart asked `/api/v1/series/{id}/forecast?asof=` at every step of a held key (the panel's `t` is not debounced) and asked the API at the now bucket: the as-of query now waits for the settled `t`, and the now bucket uses `recent.json`'s run (`Chart.tsx`).
- **Code, major:** an equal-level area class won the tie against the gauge's own class: the gauge wins now (`lib/stationStates.ts`, a tie test in either order).
- **Code, minor:** `check-i18n` reads `.ts` too and flags a UI-text property (`name`, `text`, `title`, `subtext`, `label`) set to a literal; the dead `markerStates` and `forecastStates` are gone (their tests run on `stationStates`); a `?t=` that lands on now is live mode; the owner-labels query key carries the audience; the owner site offers no river download (it serves no `/downloads`).
- **Security, low:** `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer` on the owner site; `/runtime-config.json` failures are retried and then an alert, never public (a 404 stays public); a display-only series is not asked for its forecast run; the owner label index moved into the owner chunk, with a `build.test.ts` needle.
- **Not changed (nits):** the fixed "Hub'Eau" wording of an unverified zero (only FR-1 zeros reach it today) and an area issued inside the current bucket showing up to 10 minutes late.

**[U] list.** KG-232 (warnings earlier today and the owner's missing dated files wait for a publisher change), KG-233 (per-series last-value age), KG-234 (the band heuristic), KG-235 (the browser stack, the owner site, the CVD set and Lighthouse are proven in CI only; the CVD screenshots are for the owner's eyes), KG-236 (small edges), KG-237 (Lighthouse reported, not gated, in CI). Nothing needs a bootstrap re-run: `owner.caddy` and `compose.owner.yaml` are not host files (`host_files()` in `deploy/bin/rws-lib.sh`), and the owner site stays off in production until P12a (KG-226). Closed: KG-117, KG-129, KG-189 (as an overlay), KG-194, KG-211, KG-213; KG-120 closed once the Lighthouse run is green; KG-209 partly. KG-119 (the chart's ticks) stays open. No risk changes: `docs/risk-register.md` is unchanged. Threat model 4.39.

## 30. Amendment: P10b build (2026-10-06)

What the P10b build (issue #25, PR "P10b: Pages", `Closes #25`) found or settled against the plan and the issue, and why. P10b is the web's information and legal pages in NL and EN: About, Sources, Method, Disclaimer, Colophon, Privacy, Status and an accessibility statement; the page routes and a real HTTP 404 with a 404 page; the operator, the contact address and the CDN in `/runtime-config.json`; a `verify-prod` check of every page; and the licence of our own code. The PR changes no ingestion, database, migration, API route, registry row, audience or channel flag, capture spec or egress host, and adds no dependency (no ADR-lite line, no BOM row). It changes no host file (`host_files()` in `deploy/bin/rws-lib.sh` lists `deploy/bin`, `deploy/host`, `deploy/systemd` and a few others; `site.caddy`, `owner.caddy`, `compose.yaml` and `compose.owner.yaml` are not among them), so no bootstrap re-run is needed. A§10 and the threat model (4.40, T-WEB-1, T-WEB-2, T-WEB-3, new T-WEB-4) carry the design.

**Where reality differs from the plan** (`~/.claude/plans/snappy-mapping-candle.md`, owner decisions of 2026-10-06 and its §10):
- **The branch is not stacked.** The plan stacked `claude/p10b-pages` on `claude/p10a-ui-core` because #85 was unmerged. P10a (#85) was merged (64b88e2) before P10b started, so the branch came from `main` and the PR's diff is P10b alone: no "also shows P10a" note and no later merge of `main` into the branch.
- **No router and no markdown dependency** (the A§10 owner decision stands): a route table (`lib/routes.ts`) and per-language JSX content files, each its own lazy chunk.
- **One registry, no shell per page.** `features/pages/Page.tsx` holds a static map of 16 `lazy()` imports (8 pages × 2 languages) and renders `content/<locale>/<Page>.tsx` in a `Suspense`; there is no `features/pages/index.ts` and no `<Page>Page.tsx` per page.
- **The route table is `PAGE_ROUTES`**, not `ROUTES`: `scripts/verify-prod.ts` already imports a `ROUTES` (`apps/server/src/api/channels.ts`).
- **The code licence is PolyForm Strict License 1.0.0** (owner, 2026-10-06; ADR-0018, written at the owner's request after review round 1). `LICENSE` is the official text, byte for byte, from the PolyForm Project's repository (no "Required Notice" line and no name added) and the root `package.json` has `"license": "SEE LICENSE IN LICENSE"`. The code is "source available" and the colophon says so; it is never called "open source". The river graph stays under the ODbL (data, a separate licence).
- **The operator and the CDN come from the runtime config**, never from git or the build: `RWS_OPERATOR_NAME` and `RWS_CDN_NAME` sit beside `RWS_CONTACT_EMAIL` in the host's `rws.env` and reach the page through Caddy's `/runtime-config.json`.

**What was built, in short.** `apps/web/src/lib/routes.ts` (`PAGE_ROUTES`, `routeOf`, `pathOf`); `App.tsx` (the map, a page or the 404 page) inside `features/layout/Layout.tsx` (header with the language link to the same page, beta banner with a link to the disclaimer, owner banner, `<main>`, footer with the nine page links, the map credits and the notices link); `features/pages/` (`Page.tsx`, `content/{nl,en}/{About,Sources,Method,Disclaimer,Colophon,Privacy,Status,Accessibility}.tsx`, `parts/`, `official.ts`, `policy.ts`, the generated `method.gen.ts`); `apps/web/404.html` and `en/404.html` as Vite inputs; `lib/config/runtime.ts` and `lib/data/{api,chain,contracts}.ts` (the runtime config's three fields, the loose `StatusPage` and `ReachTravel` readers, `useSiteConfig`, `useStatusPage`, `useReachTravel`); `lib/href.ts` (`httpsHref`, one copy of the only way data becomes an `href`); `lib/attribution.ts` (BAFU's "(Bezugsdatum: <date>)"); `features/owner/OwnerBasis.tsx` in the existing lazy owner chunk; `@rws/core/datums` (a new subpath export of `TO_NAP`); `scripts/gen-web-method.ts` and `scripts/check-i18n.ts` (the content-file rule); `deploy/web/site.caddy` and `owner.caddy` (the page allowlist and the 404 shells), `deploy/compose.yaml` and `compose.owner.yaml` (the three variables), `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (the e2e Caddy containers' environment and the two new required `PASS` lines of the `deploy` job), `deploy/tests/e2e/{run.sh,isolation.sh,owner-check.mjs}`; `scripts/verify-prod.ts` (`pages <path>`, `not found`, `runtime config`); `LICENSE`; and the pages' messages in `messages/{nl,en}.json`.

**Deviations from the plan and the issue.**

| # | Plan or issue | What P10b does, and why |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | T1: the table is `ROUTES` | **`PAGE_ROUTES`** (C1: `verify-prod.ts` imports a `ROUTES`). `lib/routes.ts` has no imports, so Node reads it as it is: `scripts/verify-prod.ts`, `test/page-routes.test.ts` and the e2e stand-in import it, and `tsconfig.tooling.json` and the e2e `tsconfig.json` list it (TS6307) |
| 2 | T3: `features/pages/index.ts` and a shell `<Page>Page.tsx` per page | **One `Page.tsx` with a static map of 16 lazy imports**; a page's text and its language are one chunk, and the map imports none of them |
| 3 | T7 (as C3 and C4 amended it): `@page_nl path …` and `@hidden path /404.html /en/404.html` | **`@page_nl` and `@page_en` are `expression` matchers** `{path} in ['/', '/over', …]` (a `path` matcher folds case and merges slashes: `/Over` and `//over` would be soft 404s), and the shells' hiding is `not path /404.html /en/404.html` inside `@file`, so `/404.html`, `/en/404.html` and their other spellings fall to `@dotted` and are a bare 404. `@dotted` (`path_regexp \.[^/]*$`, `respond 404`) keeps `/favicon.ico` and `/robots.txt` bare 404s; the 404 shell answers only extensionless paths. The same list is in `site.caddy` and `owner.caddy`; `test/page-routes.test.ts` holds both equal to `PAGE_ROUTES` |
| 4 | T6: compose `RWS_OPERATOR_NAME: ${RWS_OPERATOR_NAME:?}` on `web`, and a deploy env check | **`${RWS_OPERATOR_NAME:-}` and `${RWS_CDN_NAME:-}` on service `caddy`** (and on `caddy-owner`, which also gets `RWS_CONTACT_EMAIL:?`), and **no change to `rws-lib.sh`, `bootstrap.sh` or `env_ready`** (C5): a required variable would break the drill, update and basemap tests and flag `host_files_changed`. An unset operator therefore blocks no deploy; it shows "not configured" on the colophon and fails `verify-prod`'s `runtime config` until the owner sets it. The `{ } # " \` rule (Caddy expands `{…}` in a `respond` body, a quote breaks the JSON, `#` starts a comment in an env file) is checked there, and `load_env` already rejects `"`, `'`, a backtick, `$` and `\` |
| 5 | T5: the Method tables come from `scripts/gen-classification.ts` | **A separate `scripts/gen-web-method.ts`** (C7) writes `features/pages/method.gen.ts` from the public, ungated rows of public sources, with `--check` in `pnpm check`; `gen-classification.ts` and `docs/classification.md` are unchanged. `test/web-method.test.ts` fails on any owner or permission source id or agency in the file. The datum table reads `TO_NAP` from `@rws/core/datums` (nothing is generated for datums) |
| 6 | T5: the licence kind through `m.licence_<kind>` | **A static `switch` over the six kinds of the public sources** (`cc0`, `dl-de-zero-2.0`, `etalab-2.0`, `cc-by`, `cc-by-sa-4.0`, `ch-open-use`); any other kind is shown as the registry spells it (`licence.kind` is a free string), so that no owner licence name enters the public bundle (KG-243) |
| 7 | T4: the CDN line says "no CDN" when `cdn` is empty | As planned, and **a missing or malformed `cdn` says that it is not known**, never "no CDN": a privacy page must not claim there is none because a field was dropped |
| 8 | T4: the contact is a `mailto:` built from a `z.email()` value | **Stricter than `z.email()`:** `contactHref` makes a link only for a plain address of letters, digits and `._+-` (no `?`, `&`, `%`, quote or space), else the page shows the text; it is the only `href` of the site with a scheme other than https |
| 9 | T5: Status and Sources show names | **Status shows source ids** (the Sources page has the names); the loose status reader's id pattern is the public one (no canary branch) and a hidden source is dropped (KG-244) |
| 10 | T5: owner crosswalk rows on the Method page | **Not built** (KG-241): the tables hold public rows on both sites |
| 11 | Plan C13: the owner Sources page needs a new owner chunk or none | **`OwnerBasis` joins the existing owner chunk** (`features/owner/index.ts`), so `build.test.ts` keeps pinning three dynamic owner chunks |
| 12 | C2: the runtime-config pins | **Every pin now parses the JSON** and asserts the audience and the four keys: `scripts/verify-prod.ts`, `test/verify-prod.test.ts`, `isolation.sh`, `owner-check.mjs`, `apps/web/test/runtime.test.ts`, the e2e stand-in; no check prints the operator's name (personal data) |
| 13 | Reported by a build package, not in the plan | The entry chunk holds bare ids of sources that are not public: `'BE-3'` (an owner source) in `CLASS_SCALE` and `'DE-10'` (an `off` source) in `AREA_SCALE` of `apps/web/src/lib/labels/labels-index.gen.ts`, the copies that `scripts/gen-web-labels.ts` writes; P10a's build test greps `lbl_be_3_` only. They are ids, no value, and both ids are public in the registry and the catalogue; moving them out of the entry chunk is a follow-up (KG-242) |
| 14 | P10 and T4: the official services are named waterinfo.rws.nl, vigicrues.gouv.fr, naturgefahren.ch, inondations.lu, hochwasserzentralen.de, waterinfo.be and hydrometrie.wallonie.be | **The link text is the host of the link as `features/pages/official.ts` has it** (`new URL(href).host`, so no literal in a part): `waterberichtgeving.rws.nl` and `waterinfo.rws.nl`, `www.hochwasserzentralen.de`, `www.waterinfo.be` and `hydrometrie.wallonie.be`, `www.vigicrues.gouv.fr`, `inondations.public.lu` and `www.naturgefahren.ch`. `inondations.lu` redirects to `inondations.public.lu`, so the page links the target |

**Decided during the build (plan §10, binding).** A path is a page only by exact match (a trailing slash, another case or a doubled slash is a 404, and the PR says so); `routeOf` decodes the percent escapes first, as Caddy matches the path, and refuses a broken one; a link between pages is a plain anchor (a full page load); the language link of a page is the same page's path in the other language and keeps `t`, `s`, `mode` and `river`; the 404 page never shows the path; the footer imports `MapCredits` statically, so the entry chunk holds "ODbL" (`verify-prod`'s `rivers attribution`); an external link in prose is `<a href="https://…" rel="noopener noreferrer">` with no `target`, no image and no icon; every external `href` that comes from data (a credit or licence URL, a travel-time source, an owner basis) goes through `httpsHref`; a content file imports only `react` and `../../parts/<Name>` (`check-i18n`); a part takes every word from the messages and a content file carries only prose; a message key never contains `private_basis`, `owner_sources`, `licence_gate`, `canary`, `__rws` or `nl.e2e.`; a bad optional runtime-config field is dropped on its own and never changes the audience; one query, `['runtime-config']`, serves the audience and the three fields; the owner site's Method page shows the owner family's forecast coverage (the one its map shows) and the public site's the public one; the 404 inherits the site header block and `Cache-Control: no-cache` (public site) or `private, no-store` (owner site, from its deferred header block); `/status/*` stays a 404 on the public site (`/status/capture.json` and `/status/ops.json` stay the status files) and closing KG-118 changed two "other handlers" of `site.caddy` (`redir /over` and `handle /status`); the D21 text of the Method page (the rivers that are not covered) is static prose, so the owner's answer (due 2026-11-10, §6.2 action D8) changes only its two content files.

### Review round 1 (2026-10-06)

Two read-only reviews on Sonnet (high) with #25's prompts: code **approve** (3 minor, 11 nits), security **pass** (4 low, 3 info); no blocker, critical or high, so no second round (owner rule). CI was green on the first push (90b2b01). Fixed by the lead:
- **The owner audience no longer depends on the free text** (security low): `RuntimeConfig` reads `audience` on its own and ignores unknown keys; a bad `contact`, `operator` or `cdn` is dropped on its own. Residual: a body that is no JSON at all (a raw tab or another control character in a value, which `load_env` lets through) is public, so the owner site would lose its banner; the runbook rules out such characters and verify-prod checks the public host (the owner host has no verifier until #27).
- **The access log drops every client-address header but the masked `X-Forwarded-For`** (security low): `Forwarded`, `X-Real-Ip`, `Cf-Connecting-Ip`, `True-Client-Ip`, `X-Client-Ip` and `Fastly-Client-Ip` are deleted in both Caddy log filters (`test/privacy-policy.test.ts`), so the privacy page stays true behind any proxy or a CDN (D20).
- **A doubled slash is never a file** (security low): `@file` adds `not expression {path}.contains('//')`, so `//en//` and `//index.html` are 404s, not a shell with 200 (verified on Caddy 2.11.4; the stand-in mirrors it).
- **`privateBasis` is read only in the owner chunk** (security low): `OwnerBasis` takes the whole source; `build.test.ts` greps the page chunks for the field's name. KG-242 now also names P8's forecast precedence.
- **A page chunk that cannot load** shows an alert and a reload link inside the layout instead of a blank page (code minor: an error boundary in `features/pages/Page.tsx`).
- **The colophon and privacy parts say when the runtime config failed** (code minor: `data_unavailable`, role alert), instead of dropping the operator, contact and CDN lines.
- **The owner Sources spec asserts the owner sources' credit rows** (code minor; `owner-pages.spec.ts`).
- Nits: `routeOf` uses `Object.hasOwn`; the footer nav marks the current page (`aria-current`); the screen-tall `min-height` applies to the map only; a status the page does not know is shown as unknown instead of dropping the row. Not changed (accepted): the information paths get the map's static shell until the app mounts; `MapCredits` on the colophon and Sources pages as well as in the footer (the approved texts); the status and reach readers in the entry chunk (initial JS 156 KiB gzip, budget 250); the CH-1 code `undefined` (the agency's own code); the words "eigenaarsbronnen / owner sources".
- **Owner answers (2026-10-06):** the E5 texts are approved; the access log's stated purpose is right; the sentence on the Autoriteit Persoonsgegevens stays; no sentence about the LAN reverse proxy's log (rk.wijkhuisen.info is an acceptance server); no link to the repository; ADR-0018 records the licence; D21 is accepted as proposed.

## 31. Amendment: P10c build (2026-10-06)

What the P10c build (issue #90, PR "P10c: Rivierkijker brand", `Closes #90`) settled against the issue and its design document. P10c applies the brand (D23): `docs/design/BRAND.md` is the brand pack and says where each part lives.

**Owner decisions (2026-10-06):** the meta description is softened ("met verwachtingen en waarschuwingen waar beschikbaar"), because public forecasts exist for NL and CH (FR only during events) and warning classes for DE, FR and CH, none for BE; the existing map palettes are documented as the signal set, with a test and the beta banner restyled, and the map's colours stay; the fonts are vendored woff2, sha256-pinned, with no npm dependency; the slot is P10c after P10b (#89).

**Where reality differs from the issue:**
- **The fonts are in `apps/web/src/styles/fonts/`, not `public/fonts/`.** Imported from `base.css`, they get hashed names under `/assets/` and Caddy's immutable cache, with no Caddy change; `public/` files keep their names and are revalidated. No CSP change: `font-src 'self'` was already there.
- **No outlined lockup and no DM Sans.** The lockup on the site is the SVG mark plus the name as live text (two message keys, `name_lead` and `name_accent`, so `check-i18n` holds) and the subtitle as text, as the document allows.
- **No `favicon.ico`, no app-icon PNGs, no manifest.** `/favicon.svg` is linked from the four shells; `/favicon.ico` stays the bare 404 that `routes.spec.ts`, verify-prod and the deploy e2e assert. The PNGs wait for home-screen install (KG-247).
- **Tabular numerals on `:root`**, not per table: Source Sans 3 has them by default, and the fallback font gets them too.
- **The `intro` text and the README** say the same softened claim as the meta description.
- **The e2e `mapReady` helper scrolls the map into view.** The map mounts only near the viewport (`useMapLibre`); on the owner site the open owner banner and the taller brand header put it past that margin in the 768 px window, and three owner tests timed out locally.

**Evidence ([CI]):**
- `apps/web/test/brand.test.ts`: the fonts are what `SHA256SUMS` lists, byte for byte, and every woff2 is used by `base.css` with a same-folder `url()`; the brand tokens are the document's; ten contrast pairs meet their minimum (Waterblauw below 4.5:1 by test, so it stays out of small text); no colour of the signal tokens, `palette.ts`, `labels-index.gen.ts` or `stationLayer.ts` is a brand colour.
- `apps/web/test/build.test.ts`: the titles and the h1 of the shells, the meta description, the favicon link and the theme colour in all four shells; `favicon.svg` at the root and no `favicon.ico`; six hashed woff2 under `/assets/`; both OFL texts in `third-party-notices.txt`.
- e2e: the h1 and the subtitle; both fonts loaded (`document.fonts`) while the test's third-party check still passes (invariant 7); `/favicon.svg` is `image/svg+xml`, `no-cache`, with the site headers; the axe colour-contrast runs pass on the new palette.

## 32. Amendment: P10d build (2026-10-07)

What the P10d build (issue #96, PR "P10d: station panel, legend and timebar (waterinfo-like)", `Closes #96`, `Closes #88`) settled against the issue. P10d restyles the station panel, the map legend and the timebar after the layout of waterinfo.rws.nl, in the Rivierkijker brand (`docs/design/BRAND.md` §8). Only layout patterns are taken: no RWS logo, icon, font, CSS or text.

**Owner decisions (2026-10-07):**
1. **Neighbour data:** the web widens its existing read of `reaches-<ver>.json` (one fetch, one query key, each reader parses its own section); no new API field, contract, golden, ETag or `schema_version` change. In the committed build 484 of 1,000 public stations are placed on a river; the others get no neighbour rows.
2. **Cross-river:** the walk follows the reach graph to the first public station. At a confluence or bifurcation it prefers the branch on the same river, else the first branch in file order; the row names the other river.
3. **Zones (#88 folded in, web-side):** a low zone below a `<=` or `<` level; elevated, high and extreme zones from each `>=` level to the next higher level of the same source or the top of the axis; shown-only references (`op: null`: MW, NNW, HHW, NW, HW, Marke I to III, GLW, FR-5 floods) stay lines; NL-4 classes are zones between their From and To bounds. A class with more than one distinct bound at one priority is seasonal, and `recent.json` carries no season, so it stays lines and text (KG-249; #99 since: `recent.json` states each seasonal reference's `season`, and the chart keeps only the rows whose season holds at t, in Europe/Amsterdam). This supersedes #88's "low references stay lines": the owner chose shaded low zones. KG-234 is closed.
4. **Panel "Tabel":** a new per-series table of the chart's points, paged at 100 rows; the page-level `StationTable` stays the no-WebGL2 fallback, unchanged.
5. **Reverse play** and a step-back are in the issue (#96). The P10 scope lists "playback" as P11, but play has existed since P8b; reverse play only adds the other direction (stop at the first day, forward stops at the end of the forecast). No Opslaan, Delen or Export buttons and no placeholders for them.

**Where reality differs from the plan:**
- **The neighbour walk takes the file's own end station, and never a co-located one.** Co-located stations share a reach and a `km_graph`, and the file names one of them per reach end (the alphabetically first). The walk refuses any station with the same reach and `km_graph` as the selected one, and a station is at a sink only when its reach's end station shares its `km_graph` (review round 1: a station upstream on a reach that ends at a sink shares that reach too).
- **A span beyond `recent.json` asks the API only when the series has data from before it.** `dataSince` decides, so a station whose data begins inside the 7 days asks nothing extra; a display-only series (no `api`) says "only the last 7 days are available here" instead.
- **The run's name moved from a paragraph under the chart into the Reeksen legend** (the line, its estimate part and the band), so `p10a.spec.ts` asserts the two list items instead of a paragraph.
- **The threshold model lives in `thresholds.ts`** (re-exported nowhere: `chartModel.ts` keeps points and runs), with tests in `thresholds.test.ts` instead of `station-chart.test.ts`.
- **The timebar** is docked, and sticky only in a window at least 48rem wide and 32rem high (a phone's or a short window's bar would take a quarter of the screen); its heading is visually hidden. The page's `scroll-padding-bottom` follows the bar's measured height (review round 1), so a focused control is never under it, whatever notes the bar shows.

**Evidence ([CI]):**
- Unit: `neighbours.test.ts` (same river up and down; no neighbour at a source, a river end, an unplaced station or one the file lacks; across a confluence and a bifurcation, same river first; a fallback branch; unknown ids walked past; co-located stations; a sink; a cycle and the depth cap; the lenient parse with a bad row, a bad section and a prototype-named id); `thresholds.test.ts` (DE-1, DE-7, CH-2, FR-5, a kind with no role, NL-4 whole-year, seasonal and overlapping classes, the legend text in NL and EN with the unit and its zero, the owner badge, no references); `timebar-play.test.ts` (both bounds, a station without a forecast, reverse play across the DST night in NL and EN); `app-logic.test.ts` (`chartSpan` with 2, 7 and 14 days); `station-chart.test.ts` (`mergeHistory`, `seriesRows`, `recentGap`, `xRange` and `onAxis`).
- e2e (`p10d.spec.ts`, three browsers): the header and last-measurement line; the Grafiek|Tabel radios, the table with its caption, rows and keyboard pager; the period select; the thresholds checkbox against the chart's `markLine` and `markArea`; the Reeksen and Grenswaarden legends with the raw label as text; the neighbour rows across a fork, a click that moves the focus to the new heading, and no block for an unplaced station; the legend in the map's corner, above the attribution button, collapsing with Enter, and in the flow in the table view; the timebar below the map, step-back at the first day, reverse and forward play (one "Pauzeren" at a time, the focus kept), reduced motion, and the bar never hiding a focused control (in its tallest state, with the forecast note and the DST choice, and not sticky in a short window); the legend's open state kept across the map and table views; no now line or key at an earlier t; axe on the panel in both views and on the bar.

## 33. Amendment: P10e build (2026-10-07)

What the P10e build (issue #101) settled against the issue. P10e makes the map the whole page: a sticky top bar, the station panel as a drawer, a collapsed timebar, the credits in a disclosure and a station search. It is web-only: no API, contract, migration, registry or Caddy change and no new dependency (`apps/web/src` and its tests). The look follows `docs/design/BRAND.md` §9; only existing tokens are used.

**Owner decisions (2026-10-07):** decisions D1 to D8 of the issue (#101) were confirmed as written, and four were settled in the planning session:
1. **The bar is sticky** and the map fills the rest of the window. The bar is 3.5rem tall and its measured height is `--chrome-h` on `<html>`; the map stage is `100dvh - --chrome-h`, with no page scroll and no footer on the map. The owner banner is a slim strip directly under the bar (its terms scroll inside 30dvh).
2. **Menu breakpoint 80rem.** The nine page links do not fit the bar at 1024 px, so from 80rem they are a row in the bar and below it a popover under the bar, opened by a "Menu" button.
3. **D6: the station search is an ARIA 1.2 combobox** (no `<datalist>`, so no spike). It replaces the station `<select>` and matches case- and diacritics-insensitively on the name and the water name.
4. **The timebar is collapsed by default** (time, slider, step, play, "Nu", and a "Tijdopties" expander); the legend stays collapsed (KG-251).

**Where reality differs from the plan:**
- **1024 × 768 is below the menu breakpoint**, so the nav is behind "Menu" in the e2e default viewport. BRAND.md said the subtitle hides below about 64rem; the nine links plus the subtitle only fit from 100rem.
- **The name is 1.5rem (24 px) on the bar**, large text, so "kijker" stays Waterblauw (BRAND.md §3); below 40rem the name is 1.1rem and "kijker" takes `--accent`, the colour allowed for small text.
- **The nav is one `<nav aria-label>` with the `popover` attribute**: a row from 80rem (an author `display` beats the closed state), a popover below it. Escape and a click outside close it and the browser returns the focus to the button.
- **Choosing a mode or view by Enter or click closes its disclosure** (the focus goes to the summary); an arrow-key move does not, so a keyboard or screen-reader user can move through the radios. Opening one disclosure closes the other. Escape closes.
- **Below 48rem the station panel is a full-width sheet** that ends above the timebar. With the sheet open the view under it is `visibility: hidden` and the mode and view controls are not shown, so the mode cannot be changed until the panel closes; the status lines are a band above the sheet (KG-254, review round 1).
- **Station panel focus**: choosing the open station again from the search does not re-focus the panel, whose focus effect runs on mount (KG-252). A deep link centres the station in the part the 26rem drawer leaves free (`jumpTo`, then `panBy` half the drawer); a station chosen later does not move the camera (KG-253).
- **MapLibre's compact attribution text and button stay** (OpenStreetMap and Protomaps); the "Bronnen" button and the legend stand above its row. `MapCredits` is still imported statically, so the entry chunk holds "ODbL" (`verify-prod`'s `rivers attribution`).
- **The `.tall` page layout is gone**; `html` gets `scroll-padding-top` of the bar's height plus 0.5rem (WCAG 2.4.11), as the timebar's measured height already feeds `scroll-padding-bottom`.

**What was built, in short.** `features/layout/Layout.tsx` (bar, nav popover, compact "bèta" link whose accessible name is the banner text plus the link text, language link, search slot on the map, owner strip, slim footer); `features/attribution/Attribution.tsx` (the "Bronnen" button with `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls`; the panel is a `<section aria-label>` with an `h2`, the credits of the sources of `t` (`attributionText`, `httpsHref`, the dedup key language, link and text, the Amsterdam date of `t`, `li[lang]`), `MapCredits`, the disclaimer line and the links to the Sources page and the notices; text nodes only, nothing goes to MapLibre's `customAttribution`; Escape closes and returns the focus, and so does the focus leaving; present on the map, the table view and the no-WebGL2 view); `features/search/StationSearch.tsx` and `lib/stationSearch.ts` (a magnifier button, "Zoek een station", then the combobox and listbox with arrows, Enter and Escape; every word of the query must match, a name that starts with the query first, at most 20 results, the list's order breaks ties; options keyed by station id so equal labels stay distinct; the typed text never reaches the URL, a fetch or an HTML sink, only the registry station id leaves, through `?s=`); `features/legend/MapControls.tsx` (the two disclosures, the existing `ModeControl` radios `map-mode` and the Kaart|Tabel buttons inside); the legend, always a floating `<details>` in the bottom-right stack, also in the table view; `features/timebar` (collapsed and expanded states, `--timebar-h` measured in both, the date, time, reverse play, DST choice, missing alert, notes and ticks only when expanded); `App.tsx` and `App.module.css` (the stage under the bar, the status lines stacked under the mode and view row with their roles unchanged, `--drawer-w` of 26rem from 48rem); `station.module.css` and `table.module.css` (the drawer or sheet; the table fills the window and scrolls inside). Closing a panel focuses its opener button, else the magnifier. Messages added in NL and EN: `search_open`, `search_none`, `search_count`, `menu_button`, `beta_short`, `mode_summary`, `view_summary`, `timebar_more`, `attribution_panel_label`.

**Evidence ([CI]):**
- Unit: `apps/web/test/station-search.test.ts` (`fold`; partial, case and diacritics matches; the water name; the rank; all words; a blank query; duplicate labels; the limit of 20).
- e2e (`p10e.spec.ts`, 21 tests after review round 1, three browsers, 63 runs): the bar sticks while a page scrolls, with the slim footer; the nine links in the bar and, at 390 px, in the menu (Escape, focus return, keyboard); the beta link and the language link keep the view; the map fills the window at 1440 × 900, 1024 × 768, 768 × 1024 and 390 × 844 with no page scrollbar and no footer; the mode and view disclosures by keyboard and `?mode=`; the search (`lobit` finds Lobith, Enter opens the panel with the focus in it, the typed text is not in the URL, Escape returns the focus to the magnifier, arrows and `aria-activedescendant`, the no-match text, a click on a result); the table button's focus return; the drawer keeps the map's size and the sheet below 48rem; the timebar collapsed and expanded (controls only when expanded, `aria-expanded`, geometry, never over the legend or the credits; at 390 × 844 not over the legend, the credits or the panel's close button); the credits disclosure lists every credit of the old footer for that `t` (computed from `/data/v1/meta.json` with `attributionText`: the same texts, languages, links and date), the Sources link, the disclaimer and the notices; English and the table view; axe on the map, the open credits, the mode menu, the table view and the open menu.
- Selector changes in existing specs, by a separate package (nothing weakened): `app`, `p10a`, `p10d`, `forecast`, `cvd`, `no-webgl2`, `owner*`, `pages` and `screens` follow the moved controls (the station `<select>` is the search, the footer links are the bar's, the credits are in the disclosure, the mode and view are in disclosures, the timebar's date and time are behind "Tijdopties"); `helpers.ts` gains the helpers for them.
- `screens.spec.ts` (the `cvd` project, Chromium) writes new pictures to `test-results/screens/*.png`; CI uploads them in the `e2e-test-results` artifact.
- Lighthouse stays report-only (KG-237); the numbers after the layout change are KG-255.
- Commands: `pnpm check`, `pnpm -F web build`, `pnpm -F web build:e2e` and `pnpm -F web e2e` (needs `DATABASE_URL`). Final run on the build of this PR, after review round 1: `pnpm check` green (186 unit files, 4790 tests, `check-bom`, `check-boundaries`, `check-i18n` with 492 messages, `gen-openapi --check`; the initial-JS budget of 250 KB gzip per shell, `test/map-build.test.ts`, holds); `pnpm -F web e2e` locally on the three public browsers, `no-webgl2`, `cvd` (with `screens`), the three owner projects and Lighthouse last: 623 passed, 54 skipped (the compose and owner-smoke runs that need their own environment), 0 failed, in 7.7 minutes. Lighthouse (report-only, KG-237), mobile, median of 3 on the owner's WSL box: performance 66, accessibility 100, LCP 2888 ms (the build pass measured 56 and 4954 ms on the same box); CI measured 73 for P10d on another machine, so the comparison to make is the CI run of this PR (KG-255).

**Review round 1 (2026-10-07; Sonnet high code review: 2 medium, 2 medium-low, 1 low-medium, 4 low, nits; Sonnet high security review: pass, 2 low advisories).** All fixed in the fix pass (Opus), each with a test that fails without it (run against the build before the fix):
- **Medium, the credits beside the drawer:** at 768 to about 839 px with a station open the "Bronnen" panel was as wide as the window and its start was cut off; it is now at most `100vw - --drawer-w - 1rem` wide. Test: `p10e.spec.ts` "the Bronnen panel stays inside the window" (768 × 1024, the box inside the window and left of the drawer).
- **Medium, the sheet below 48rem:** the map canvas, MapLibre's attribution button and the table's rows under the sheet were still focusable, and the status lines were under the sheet. Now the view is `visibility: hidden` (MapLibre's open compact attribution by name too, as it sets its own `visibility: visible`), the controls are not shown, the status lines are a band in the flow above the sheet, and `close()` returns the focus in an effect once the panel is gone (a hidden button takes no focus). Test: "below 48rem the sheet hides the view under it" (390 × 844: canvas and attribution button hidden, the Δh status line above the sheet and clear of its close button, Shift+Tab never into the map, the focus back on the magnifier and, in the table view, on the row button). Desktop is unchanged. KG-254 updated.
- **Medium-low, reverse play and the collapse:** collapsing the timebar took away the only pause of reverse play; collapsing now stops it. Test: "collapsing the timebar stops reverse play".
- **Medium-low, the active result out of sight:** the active option scrolls into view (`scrollIntoView({ block: 'nearest' })` through a ref on the active option; no id lookup). Test: the search arrows test walks 17 options down a list of 20 and checks the active one is inside the list's box.
- **Low-medium, the credits in a short window:** the panel's `max-height` is now the room above the button (`100dvh - --chrome-h - --timebar-h - 8rem`, at most 28rem). Test: the same Bronnen test at 720 × 450 (200 % zoom of 1440 × 900) with the timebar expanded: the panel starts under the bar, clear of the timebar, its heading in view.
- **Low, the menu's `aria-expanded`:** the nav's `toggle` event sets React state and the button's `aria-expanded` (Chromium mapped popover invokers implicitly, Firefox and WebKit did not, and the open-state CSS was dead). Test: the menu test asserts `false`, `true` and `false` again; `openMenu` in `helpers.ts` uses the attribute.
- **Low, a press on a toggle where a click does not focus a button (WebKit, Firefox on macOS):** the magnifier and "Bronnen" take the focus on `mousedown` themselves (`preventDefault`, then `focus()`), so the open field or panel no longer closes and reopens. Test: "a press on the magnifier or on Bronnen keeps the focus in the control", which emulates Safari's default action (a press on a button that nobody prevented moves the focus to nothing), since the suite's Linux browsers focus a button on a click.
- **Low, rounded heights:** `--chrome-h` and `--timebar-h` are `Math.ceil` of `getBoundingClientRect().height` (`offsetHeight` rounded a 53.2 px bar down, and the map was a sliver too tall). Test: "a bar of a fractional height never makes the map a sliver too tall" (root font size 15.2 px).

Test: "a deep-linked station is in the part the drawer leaves free" (1024 × 768: the popup's tip in the middle of the free part, its close button clear of the drawer, `getPadding()` all zero); the two `p10a` axe views of deep-linked panels run at the default 1024 px again. KG-253 updated (the deep-link case is closed).
- **Nits:** `station_select_label` and `station_select_none` are gone from both catalogues (no consumer; `gen-web-labels` and `check-i18n` green); the search field has `maxLength` 100 (test: the attribute); "Bronnen" sets `aria-controls` only while the panel exists (test: absent while closed, the panel's id while open); the `Layout.tsx` header comment says the subtitle shows from 100rem. The fold of ß, ø, ł and đ is unchanged (owner). On the map the disclaimer line is inside the "Bronnen" panel and the bèta link's accessible name carries the banner text while it shows "bèta": both as the approved plan placed them (D1 and the bar), so unchanged.
- **The bar measured:** the nine links fit one row between the name and the tools at 1280 × 720 and 1366 × 768 on the map (which also holds the magnifier) in NL and EN, with no horizontal scroll; at 360 × 640 the bar holds the name, the menu button and the tools. Test: "the bar fits". The 80rem breakpoint stays.
