## 34. Amendment: fix #78, CH-4 lake forecasts from `p_forecast` (2026-10-08)

What the fix of issue #78 (follow-up of P8b, KG-207) settled. BAFU publishes the forecasts of the 13 CH-4 lake stations under `plots/p_forecast/{id}_p_forecast_de.json`, not `q_forecast` (owner probe, 2026-10-08, issue comment). They are now captured and loaded; 2646 (Kander – Emdthal) answers 404 on both paths and stays the only station without a forecast.

**Owner decisions (2026-10-08, planning):** real lake fixtures from a live smoke capture of exactly three stations (2209 Zürichsee, 2032 Bodensee-Obersee, 2642 Lac de Neuchâtel; at most one retry); 2646 stays in the seed with its hourly `q_forecast` capture; only the `_de` figure; the three lakes on `off` CH-1 series (2022, 2027, 2101) are captured like the off rivers and store nothing; no contract-check probe for the lake spec.

**What was built:**
- **Seed:** `registry/seed/ch-4.csv` gains a column `plot`: `q` for the 41 river stations (2646 included), `p` for the 13 lakes. The unit test holds `p` to exactly the stations with no CH-1 `/Q`. `ch-1.yaml` and `ch-2.yaml` were regenerated: only the seed's sha256 in their headers changed.
- **Capture:** `ch-4-forecast` takes `where: { plot: q }` (41 variants, URL unchanged); the new `ch-4-forecast-lake` (`cron "37 * * * *"`, `where: { plot: p }`, 13 variants) fetches `p_forecast` with the same conditional, gate, caps, retention and validity. Same host; the hydrodaten budget is unchanged (`budgets()`: peak 65 per hour, 10,759 a week, before and after), as the 13 requests move from `q_` to `p_`.
- **Loader:** `load/wire/ch-4.ts` has a second spec entry with the same caps and `refTarget`. The adapter version stays 1 (it is only recorded in `ingest_batch`), because a `q_forecast` payload normalises exactly as before (the four river goldens are byte-identical).

**Where reality differs from the plan:** the plan expected no adapter change. The recordings showed one: **the lake figure states every trace in `m³/s`** although the values are lake levels in metres (Zürichsee 405.26); only its y-axis label (the one `layout.annotations` entry on the paper in both axes) says `m ü.M.`. Unchanged, the run would have gone to `<id>/Q` in metres. Fix, without loosening the strictness: `parseAxisLabel` (parse.ts, strict and capped: exactly one paper-anchored annotation with a text, else `ch4_axis_label`) and an optional `axisUnit` in normalise's context that only the lake entry passes. For a lake figure the label is the unit: it must be a declared H unit (else `unknown_unit` at `plot.layout`), and the median must state the label or `m³/s` (`LAKE_TRACE_UNITS`, else `unit_mismatch`); the envelope and band rules are unchanged. A river figure never reads the label. The capture test helper also needed an `ALIAS` from the spec to its first recording (`validity.test.ts` wants a fixture per spec).

**Datum check (no extra BAFU request):** the measured trace of each recording against the CH-1 lake level that our public API serves for the same instants (`/api/v1/series/<id>` on rk.wijkhuisen.info, 2026-10-08): Zürichsee 21 instants, −0.4 to +0.5 cm; Bodensee-Obersee 21, −0.4 to +0.5 cm; Lac de Neuchâtel 20, −0.5 to +0.6 cm. Same datum (LN02), the difference is the figure's centimetre rounding.

**Live requests:** 3 GETs to `www.hydrodaten.admin.ch` (`scripts/smoke-capture.ts`, contact the owner's address), all 200 on the first try, no retry; 3 to our own public API for the datum check.

**Evidence ([CI]):**
- `apps/server/test/adapters/ch-4.test.ts`: the three lake recordings are goldens (114 hourly points, `<id>/W` in centimetres, no drop); a lake case (the five traces and their units, the label, the W run, the measured trace not stored, and the same traces read the q way give `2209/Q`: why the label is passed); the label rules (H units only, the trace unit the label or `m³/s`, every other spelling drift); `parseAxisLabel` (none, two, no text, a non-string, too long, too many annotations, a bad layout, not JSON); every real figure has exactly one label (`m³/s` for rivers); `parseAxisLabel` joins the bytes-to-SchemaDrift property; the seed test reads `id,plot`.
- `apps/server/test/capture/budget.test.ts`: 41 + 13 variants, 54 distinct, 2646 on `q`, the lake URL for 2209, both hourly. `catalogue-01a.test.ts` checks both specs (cadence, `first`, gate, conditional, retention).
- `apps/server/test/load/ch-4.int.test.ts`: the real 2209 figure through `ch-4-forecast-lake` stores one run of 114 points on `2209/W` (40526 cm first), none on `2209/Q`; the same figure for 2022 (an off lake) stores nothing.
- `test/verify-prod.test.ts`: `CH4_NO_FORECAST` is `['2646']`, `ch4ExpectedSeries()` is **38** (54 seeded, 15 on off CH-1 series, 2646); `test/contract-check.test.ts`: still eleven specs, the first `ch-4-forecast` row is now 2009, the probe still asks 2091.

**[agent-prod] after the deploy:** `verify-prod.sh rk.wijkhuisen.info` → `PASS forecast CH-4` with at least 38 series once the lakes have had a run (the first `:37` capture after the deploy); `/status/capture.json` lists `ch-4-forecast-lake` with 13 variants and `ch-4-forecast` with 41. No replay: no `p_forecast` line was archived before this release, and the archived 404 lines of the lakes hold no object.

**Review round 1 (2026-10-08; Sonnet high code review: approve with changes, 2 minor, 3 nits; Sonnet high security review: pass, 3 info).** Fixed by the lead: the stale "28" in KG-204 and in the ARCHITECTURE P8b paragraph (minors); `parseAxisLabel` reads the anchors of every annotation strictly but the text of the label only, so a longer note elsewhere never quarantines a lake (code nit 4 and security info 2; test: a 500-character run-start note); the label-derived `unknown_unit` is reported at `plot.layout`, as `ch4_axis_label` (nit 3). Accepted: identical `recorded_at` in the three metas (written by `smoke-capture.ts` per run, not per request), no nightly contract probe of the lake spec (info 1, decided in planning), the seed's ids not schema-checked (info 3, encoded by `render`, pre-existing). No major or high finding, so no round 2.

**[U]:** KG-207, narrowed to 2646 (the owner accepts it or keeps #78 open for it).

## 35. Amendment: P11a reality, flow direction and upstream chain (2026-10-09)

What the P11a build (issue #26, branch `claude/p11a-flow-direction-upstream-chain`) settled against the plan and the issue. P11a draws the flow direction on the river lines and adds the "Stroomopwaarts / Upstream" chain to the station panel. It adds no migration, no new runtime dependency and no URL key (A§10 is unchanged: the flow toggle has none). The public outputs are byte-identical: no public `reaches-<ver>.json`, `rivers.pmtiles`, `geo.yml` or public publisher change.

**Owner decisions (2026-10-09, binding for this PR).**
- **D-A, travel data: "file as-is, flag gaps".** At runtime (superseded by #110, §38) the chain shows only the 7 flood-peak ranges to Lobith that `reaches-<ver>.json` holds (Emmerich, Wesel, Ruhrort, Düsseldorf, Köln, Bonn, Andernach; `registry/rivers.yaml`). Every other row reads "geen bronwaarde / no sourced value"; no arithmetic derives a number. The one formatter (`apps/web/src/lib/travel.ts`) accepts a range, a labelled single value or a derived one, and its goldens (`travel-priors.ts`, 59 priors with catalogue references) cover every §3.7 anchor; the figures §3.7 does not source well enough are `unverified` and give no text. No P6 contract, registry or geo change. Flagged in KG-262, KG-263 and the follow-up issue.
- **D-B, fps: stop and ask.** `apps/web/e2e/fps.spec.ts` (project `fps`, Chromium, after `lighthouse`) measures presented frames while the timebar is scrubbed with the flow on: desktop at least 30 fps, mobile viewport at 4× CPU throttle at least 20 fps. The thresholds are never lowered; a shortfall goes to the owner before the PR is ready. **Result (2026-10-09):** with software WebGL (local Chromium on the WSL box) the desktop run measured 26.4 fps as first written, a count bounded by the key presses (Chromium presents a frame only when something changed, about 26 presses a second), and 23.3–25.6 fps over two runs once the map repaints continuously while measured (the method kept: frames the page can render); the mobile run (Pixel 5 viewport, 4× CPU throttle) measured 30.2 fps, above its 20. The same continuous-repaint measurement gave 22.7 fps with the flow off and no scrubbing, 19.1 with the flow on and no scrubbing, 27.7 scrubbing with the flow off: the map alone is below 30 before the flow is added, and the flow costs about 3–4 fps. **Owner decision (2026-10-09): report-only plus a GPU check** — the thresholds stay; `fps.spec.ts` fails on them only with `FPS_GATE=1`, CI reports the numbers and uploads the traces, and the owner runs the spec once with `FPS_GATE=1` on a machine with a real GPU before the launch (KG-269, [owner]).
- **D-C, owner split: read-only mount and km split.** `publish-owner` mounts `/srv/rws/public/data/v1/rivers` read-only at `/srv/rivers`, splits the installed release at the owner stations, placed by river and calibrated `km_graph` from `registry/rivernet.yaml`, and writes `v1/rivers/reaches-<ver>.json` into the owner tree; `owner.caddy` serves that file in preference to the public one.
- **Reviewers:** Sonnet (high) code and Sonnet (high) security, read-only, returning findings (the issue's table is overridden).

**Data facts (decided, not fixed; tests follow the data; `registry/` is not edited).**
- **F1:** Lixhe (`nl.rws.lixhebiefaval`, km_graph 554.91) is downstream of `nl.rws.eijsden.grens` (554.74) in the P6 graph (KG-264). The public Eijsden chain has no Lixhe row (gap, Chooz, … Saint-Mihiel); the owner chain is Eijsden, `be.spw.5447`, `5451` … `8702` (Chooz, co-located with `fr.sandre.B720000002` at 0.03 km).
- **F2:** the Vesdre and Amblève are not in the graph (KG-163, open): the owner chain has no group for either.
- **F3:** the Ourthe does not touch the Meuse (KG-161), so `ourthe.1` has no upstream or downstream reach: the 15 Ourthe SPW gauges are placed in the owner variant but no chain reaches them. The owner Eijsden chain has the Sambre group only, beside the public Houille, Viroin, Semois and Chiers groups (KG-265).
- Release reach ids are renumbered per build (KG-162, KG-164): the owner split joins registry and release by station id, river and km, never by reach id.

**What was built.**
- **Fixture river release (L0).** `test/fixtures/reaches-fixture.json` (the `reachesFile()` of the committed `tools/geo/fixtures` graph, version `20261003`: 709 reaches, 484 stations, 65 rivers, 5 NL entries, 7 travel pairs; since #100: 907 reaches, 586 stations, 98 rivers; since #126: 1,080 reaches, 660 stations, 134 rivers; since #125: 1,092 reaches, 667 stations, 137 rivers; since #139: 1,185 reaches, 692 stations, 162 rivers; since #140: 1,427 reaches, 723 stations, 195 rivers; since #141: 1,583 reaches, 766 stations, 240 rivers) and `tools/geo/fixtures/rivers-fixture.pmtiles` (the CI tiles of the same fixture, provenance in `tools/geo/fixtures/README.md`). `test/reaches-fixture.test.ts` regenerates and diffs the reaches. The e2e `prepare-tiles.ts` serves both instead of an empty file and a basemap.
- **Flow direction** (`apps/web/src/features/flow/`, a lazy chunk). `flowLayer.ts` adds the dash layer `rivers-flow` over the non-tidal reaches of the `rivers` source (filter: `reach_id` present and `tidal` not true; the tile `tidal` equals the file's `flags.tidal`) and the symbol layer `rivers-flow-arrows`, visible only while the clock is stopped. The arrow icon is drawn on a canvas and added with `map.addImage`: no request. `animation.ts` is pure with an injected host: one loop, at most 25 ticks a second with at least 40 ms between them (20 a second on a 60 Hz screen), none under reduced motion, cancelled in a hidden tab and resumed when visible. `FlowToggle.tsx` ("Stroming animeren / Animate flow", `aria-pressed`, WCAG 2.2.2) sits beside the map controls, defaults to on (**amended, owner 2026-10-22, #205, §58:** off by default; the visitor turns it on), is inert under reduced motion and has no URL key. In the e2e build only, `window.__rwsFlowFrames` counts the ticks; `build.test.ts` fails if a production file contains it.
- **Upstream chain** (`chain.ts`, `rows.ts`, `UpstreamChain.tsx`, lazy, in `StationPanel` after Nearby). `chain(graph, rivers, targetId, known)` walks the graph with the walk of `neighbours.ts` (exports shared): main-stem rows with co-located stations in one row, tributaries collapsed to native `<details>` groups, a gap row when two main-stem rows are more than `GAP_KM = 120` km apart (KG-268). Stations not in `known` (the site's audience-filtered `stations.json`) are skipped. Rows show the name, river, state, basis, the travel text and its source as a plain `https` link through `httpsHref`; the section and "owner only" badges follow P10. A note says travel times vary 1.5–2× with discharge.
- **One travel formatter and the ETA scan.** `lib/travel.ts` (`travelText`) replaces the Method page's own text; `apps/web/e2e/eta-scan.ts` (`scanEta`) forbids ETA, arrival and clock wording everywhere, and a clock, date, weekday or countdown in a travel row; a travel row with a number must say "indicatief" or "indicative".
- **The owner variant of the reaches file.** `splitReaches` (`apps/server/src/publish/render/reaches-owner.ts`, pure) cuts a release reach into parts `<river>.<seq>-<k>` with `part_of` at each owner station; the contract is `@rws/contracts/reaches-owner` (a subpath, not in `index.ts`, so never in the web bundle). `publish/rivers.ts` (`OwnerRivers`) reads the manifest and the two releases from `RWS_RIVERS_DIR` (default `/srv/rivers`), verifies bytes and sha256, parses strictly and writes the variant for `current` and `previous` only when the version or the owner set changed. On the fixture release: 72 BE-3 primaries placed of 316, 1 skipped (`be.spw.3884`, `owner_reach_ambiguous`, KG-267), 0 unplaced; 709 → 778 reaches, 20 of them split. The variant is served without `immutable` (its content follows the owner station set; `private, no-store` applies).

## 36. Amendment: P11b reality, reach colouring and playback (2026-10-09)

What the P11b build (issue #26, branch `claude/p11b-reach-colouring-playback`, draft PR #111) settled against the plan and the issue. P11b colours the river reaches between stations and plays back the hourly frames of the last 14 days. It adds one API route (`/api/v1/frames`, in `api` and `api-owner`), no migration, no new runtime dependency and no Caddy or host file (so no bootstrap re-run). The public static outputs are unchanged. The PR says "Part of #26": P11c is not cut.

**Owner decisions (2026-10-09, binding for this PR).**
- **D-1, State mode during playback: "play in Δh/Q only".** Frames carry hourly values and no per-hour state, so there is no browser classification and no P9 change. In State mode Play and reverse Play are `disabled` with the visible hint `play_state_hint` ("Playback works in Δh and Q mode"), linked by `aria-describedby`; switching to State mode while playing pauses. Stepping while paused works in every mode (a paused `t` is ordinary page state and reads its snapshot, which has states). KG-270; follow-up issue lane P9.
- **D-2, owner sub-reaches: "midpoint per public reach".** No tile change. Each tile feature (one public reach) takes the colour at its own chainage midpoint; on the owner variant that midpoint is evaluated in the owner sub-reach that contains it, between that sub-span's two SPW ends. KG-271; follow-up issue lane P6 (position bins in the tiles).
- **D-3, low-water scene: "the lead records at most 20 files".** `scripts/record-frames.ts`: opt-in, exit 2 under `CI`, one fixed host (`rk.wijkhuisen.info`, a constant, not configurable), User-Agent with the repository URL and no e-mail, at most 20 requests in all (preflight and redirects included), public `meta.json`, `stations.json` and `frames/<day>/v<n>.json` only. 16 live requests were made in all. If production had held no Aug–Sep frames the build would have stopped and asked; the scene is never made by hand. See R-D3 below for the substitution.
- **D-4, reviewers:** Sonnet (high) code and Sonnet (high) security, read-only, returning findings (the issue's table is overridden).
- **D-5, base:** #108 (P11a) merged before the build started.
- **D-6, nothing cut:** both halves are built.

**Reality against the brief (R1–R12, decided facts).**

| # | The brief or plan said | What P11b does, and why |
|---|---|---|
| R1 | `/api/v1/frames` exists (A§9.2) | It was `planned` in `ROUTES` (KG-224). Built: `framesParams(url, now, displayStartMs)` in `apps/server/src/api/params.ts` adds no error code. Unknown, repeated, over-long or missing `step` hit the pipeline's codes; `from`/`to` not whole UTC hours or `from >= to` is `bad_parameter`; over 336 h (`FRAMES_MAX_HOURS`) is `span_too_long`; `from` before `ceilHour(displayStart)` or `to` after now is `out_of_range`; all before any query. `readFrames(db, family, {from, to})` (`data.ts`) reads the **api** views (`lic_api`, the history window inside the view; A§8 Q5) and shares the pure `assembleFrames` with `publish/render/frames.ts`. `qc_or` rides as a non-enumerable property for `bodySources` (so FR-3 and CH-3 fill sources are credited) and never reaches the body; the attribution is dated by `to`. Rate class `heavy` (5 a second, burst 20). Immutable only when `v` equals the version of every spanned day, every day is settled and no series lacks `history_export`; the owner answers `audience: "owner"` and `private, no-store`. The owner host depends on it: `publish-owner` writes no frames |
| R2 | A series-order hash guards a frames file | Frames name their series explicitly (ascending id, one `vlast` row each), there is no hash. The check is: the strict Zod parse plus `checkFrames` (whole hours, series unique, one row per series, one entry per hour); every series id must be a series of **this audience's** `stations.json` (a `Map` lookup); an unknown id is dropped and counted, never mapped; a file that fails schema or bounds is not used (the API covers the range, else no data). KG-273 |
| R3 | `FramesFile` rows are capped at 120 h | `FramesFile` keeps 120; the API needs 336. One shared `framesObject(source, maxHours)` lives in `api.ts` (`static.ts` imports `api.ts`, so the reverse is impossible); `FramesAnswer` = rows ≤ 336, `OwnerFramesAnswer` in `api-owner.ts`; the web `Contracts` has both, the owner record `FramesFile: z.never()` |
| R4 | Reaches run from station to station | A reach starts at a confluence, a bifurcation, a river change or a station, so the colouring unit is the **span**: the run from a station to the next station downstream on the same river (`spansOf` in `features/flow/reaches/spans.ts`, a depth-first walk over same-river downstream reaches, first closed path wins; tributaries never colour the main stem). Each tile feature gets the span value at its own chainage midpoint (D-2) |
| R5 | A gap in the Meuse (Chooz → Lixhe) | A span longer than `GAP_KM` (120, `features/flow/chain.ts`) is grey and never interpolated. On the fixture public graph `meuse.24+25+26` = 139.2 km (Chooz `fr.sandre.B720000002` → Eijsden) is a gap; `meuse.23` (2.3 km) and Eijsden → Lixhe are coloured. The only other span over 120 km is `scheldt.8→12` (Maulde → Antwerpen, 165.6 km). The canal points `nl.rws.smeermaas.zuidwillemsvaart` and `nl.rws.kanne` are not in the graph. KG-272 |
| R6 | "Stale" | Two rules, both documented: a **reach end** is stale when its age exceeds the series' `stalenessLimitSeconds` (then the reach is "no data"; no one-ended extrapolation); a **station dot** keeps P10's rule (dimmed past 2 × the expected step, lapsed past the limit; `lib/stationStates.ts`) |
| R7 | Optional travel-time shift | Skipped. D-A (§35) leaves 7 pairs to Lobith and no span-level travel times; add it when the §3.7 travel-time v2 lands (#110; the v2 data landed in §38, the shift itself is still open). KG-274 |
| R8 | (no visual infrastructure) | A Playwright project `visual` (Chromium; ignored by the public projects, run in the CI `e2e` job, locally only with `VISUAL=1`; part of `LIGHTHOUSE_AFTER`) with baselines made in CI's pinned Playwright image. The first CI run is red by design (a missing baseline is written and fails); the lead views every PNG before it is committed. KG-278 |
| R9 | P10d's timebar plays 10-minute snapshots | Replaced for `t ≤ now` by hourly frames playback (below). There is no play after now (the future stays on the P8 slider) |
| R10 | The e2e stand-in renders frames for its newest settled day only (KG-221) | `publishOnce(…, settledDays: 9)` in `apps/server/test/e2e/api.ts`: a 7-day playback reads one file per day; KG-221 closed |
| R11 | One frames path | Two paths hold different series: the static files come from the display views (plus `historyExcluded(f,'other')`), the API from the api family (`lic_api`, history window in the view). **An API-fallback range lacks display-only series**: such a series shows "no data" for those hours, never zero, never carried forward. KG-275 |
| R12 | What a frame shows at t | Bucket `h` holds the last value in `[h, h+1h)`. Playback at hour `t` shows bucket `t − 1 h` (or the last non-null bucket before it), so every value is ≤ t and its age is measured from `t`; a value at or past its staleness limit is omitted. The playback range ends at `floorHour(now)`, so the partial bucket of now is never used |

**What was built (as built, with the facts the plan did not have).**
- **Reach colouring** (`apps/web/src/features/flow/reaches/{spans,colour,reachLayer}.ts`, lazy, with the flow chunk). Paint kinds: `v` (colour and width), `nodata`, `tidal`, `impounded`. Rule order: a tidal reach is `tidal` (hatch, never interpolated), and a span that contains a tidal reach is `nodata` for its other reaches; a gap, an open span or an unknown length is `nodata`; an impounded reach in **Δh** mode is `impounded`; a missing or stale end is `nodata`; otherwise the mode rule (Δh: linear in cm with core's dead band then `dhBin`; State: the rounded ladder index between the ends, `no_ref` at either end is `nodata`; Q: both ends needed, `Q_COLOUR` with `Q_WIDTH {0: 0.6, 1: 0.8, 2: 1, 3: 1.4, 4: 1.9}`). The base `rivers` line has opacity 0.7 only where a reach has no paint. Layer order under `rivers-highlight`: `rivers-reach`, `rivers-reach-nodata` (#8c8c8c, dashed), `rivers-reach-impounded` (#9aa5ad), `rivers-reach-tidal` (the hatch image `reach-hatch`, width at least 3 px). `paintReaches` writes feature state (`k`, `c`, `w`) only for reaches whose paint changed; no HTML. The legend gains the reach entries (`reach_*` messages). No toggle and no URL key: the colours follow the mode.
- **D12 recorded.** Impounded reaches "never stage Δh; neutral in the Δh mode, labelled" ("gestuwd / impounded"); in State and Q mode they use the span's values like any other reach.
- **On the fixture** (709 public reaches, 484 stations; since #100: 907 and 586; since #126: 1,080 and 660; since #125: 1,092 and 667; since #139: 1,185 and 692; since #140: 1,427 and 723; since #141: 1,583 and 766; since #142: 1,656 and 785; since #143: 1,767 and 815) 172 reaches are open and grey. Impounded is not only `meuse.23–27` (`meuse.26–30` since #126, `meuse.30–34` since #142): `nederrijn.3–5` and `moselle.15/17/18` are impounded too. `scheldt.8` (`scheldt.11` since #142) is not tidal itself, but its span (Maulde → Antwerpen) holds tidal reaches, so it is "no data" in every mode (KG-272). On the owner variant only `meuse.25` is split by SPW stations; `meuse.24` and `meuse.26` end at them (since #126: `meuse.28` split, `meuse.27` and `meuse.29` end at them; since #142: `meuse.32` split, `meuse.31` and `meuse.33` end at them).
- **Frames loader** (`lib/data/frames.ts`: `framesPlan`, `framesUrl`, `buildFrameStore`, `MAX_FRAMES_BYTES` = 16 MiB, `readFramesBody`; `useFrames` in `lib/data/api.ts`). Stage 1 reads the static files (a settled day from `frames/<day>/v<n>.json`, an absent day is v1; the unsettled days as one `frames/recent.json`); stage 2 asks the API for the days with version 0 or a failed fetch, and for the whole range on the owner host (one call per range of at most 14 days). A failed `recent.json` sends its unsettled days to the API. A failed API range is answered with no data and never retried in a loop. Credits are text only; the sources panel lists the played frames' credits first (`played_sources`).
- **Playback** (`features/flow/playback/{engine,usePlayback}.ts`, `features/timebar/steps.ts`; `features/timebar/play.ts` is removed). Speeds 9, 12 and 16 hours a second (slow, normal, fast; 7 days in about 18.7, 14 and 10.5 s); the engine holds, never skips, while an hour is missing and a `role="status"` says `play_waiting` after 1.5 s; it stops at the ends of the range `[ceilHour(max(displayStart, now − 14 d)), floorHour(now)]`; the play window loads 25 hours before the first hour (bucket `t − 1 h` and the Δh hour). The speed is a native `<select>` in the collapsed bar. Any manual change pauses; a hidden tab pauses; reduced motion disables Play (stepping stays); the step buttons step ±1 hour. URL: `play=slow|normal|fast`, an enum, an invalid value dropped; a deep link `?t=…&play=…` floors `t` to its hour inside the range and starts paused; live or a `t` after now drops it.
- **While playing**: no snapshot, changes or warnings requests (warnings stay as they were when play started); no lapses, so a station hidden for more than 25 hours without a value comes back as an empty marker during playback (KG-277); a `played` flag hides state, basis and class in the panel, the table, the chain, and gives the popup the badge "afgespeeld / played back". The e2e build has `window.__rwsPlayHold` (set before load) to hold on the first hour.
- **Recording and synthetic scenes.** `scripts/record-frames.ts --out <dir> --days <YYYY-MM-DD,…> [--report <seriesId>]` and `scripts/synthesize-frames.ts --out <dir> [--seed <n>]` (default seed 11; scenes `flood` 2026-10-10…12 and `dst` 2026-10-24…26, both marked `synthetic: true`). Files under `apps/web/e2e/fixtures/visual/`; Biome ignores that directory. A paraglide pitfall hit again: `m[\`play_speed_${s}\`]` bundled every message into the main chunk (the spike page's text tripped `build.test.ts`); the three functions are named instead.

**Deviations from the plan.**

| # | Plan | What P11b does, and why |
|---|---|---|
| R-D3 | The low-water day is the lowest daily-mean Lobith H of Aug–Sep | **NL-1 has no frames before 2026-10-02** on production, so Lobith H could not rank those days. The day was chosen by the Rhine gauges that do have Aug–Sep data (Basel CH-1, Lauterbourg FR-1): the lowest of the 10 sampled days (every 4th day, 2026-08-24 … 2026-09-29) is **2026-09-29**, kept with 2026-09-28 for its Δh. `apps/web/e2e/fixtures/visual/lowwater/` holds the two day files, `meta.json` and `stations.json`, each with a provenance `.meta.json` (`from: recording`, url, sha256, `fetched_at`). KG-276 |
| 2 | `reachColour(span, ends, mode, pos)` | `reachColour(fs, ends, mode)` (the position is inside the feature span); `framesPlan(from, to, meta, audience, failed?)` |
| 3 | Only `meuse.23–27` are impounded | `nederrijn.3–5` and `moselle.15/17/18` are impounded in the data as well; they are shown neutral in the Δh mode (KG-279) |
| 4 | Owner `meuse.24–26` all impounded in Δh | Only `meuse.25` is split by SPW stations on the owner variant; `meuse.24` and `meuse.26` end at them |
| 5 | The API fallback is equivalent | It lacks display-only series (R11, KG-275) |
| 6 | `readFrames` joins the api hourly view to the api series view `WHERE active` (as `readSeries` does) | Two reads in one snapshot instead (the active ids, then the hourly view), filtered in code: the join of two security-barrier views that both repeat the series and source join made the planner estimate one row and re-run the hourly view per series. On the e2e stand-in (1,418 public api series) a 4-hour range took 5.4 s, past `rws_api`'s 2 s `statement_timeout` (a 503); quadratic in the series count, so production would have hit it too. `/series` was never affected (one series id) |
| 7 | The speed `<select>` beside Play | In the expanded part, beside the reverse play: in the collapsed bar it wrapped to a row of its own. ## 37. Amendment: P11c reality, the Hovmöller panel (2026-10-09)

What the P11c build (issue #26, branch `claude/p11c-hovmoller`, stacked on PR #111) settled against the plan and the issue. P11c adds the lazy "Langs de rivier / Along the river" panel: x = river kilometre to the NL entry (upstream left), y = hourly time, colour = the map's 24-hour change, so a flood wave shows as a diagonal band. It is the last PR of Phase 11 ("Closes #26"). It adds one URL key (`hov`, A§10), no migration, no API route, no new runtime dependency and no host or Caddy file. The public static outputs are unchanged.

**Owner decisions (2026-10-09, binding for this PR).**
- **D-1, base: stack on P11b.** The branch starts at the head of #111 (`a78402f`); the PR targets `main` and says "Stacked on #111, review the commits after `a78402f`". When #111 merges, `main` is merged into the branch (never a rebase).
- **D-2, colour = the map's Δ (24 h), no state.** Frames have no per-hour state (§36 D-1, KG-270), so the State choice is shown disabled with the hint `hov_state_hint`. Per column the series follows the map's own Δh-mode rule (`lib/stationStates.ts`, `trendSeries`): the first H series with a change, else the Q series, binned with `dhBin(change, quantity)`. H stations show Δh in cm; Q-only stations (the SPW gauges 8078, 8016, 7132, 5451 are Q-primary) the same ±1 trend bin the map shows, with the Δ in m³/s in the tooltip and the table. No Q level colour. An H-only panel would have left every SPW column grey and the owner criterion could not pass. KG-282.
- **D-3, weir pairs: key gauge, a tie goes to `.boven`.** A `<base>.boven` / `<base>.beneden` pair on the path is one column, the lower `tier` wins; exact same-km duplicates merge public before owner (C5: an owner station copies the public km), then tier, then the smaller id. No proximity merge: Maaseik and Herenlaak stay two columns. KG-286.
- **Models and reviews:** build packages on cheaper models; code and security reviews Sonnet (high), read-only, returning findings; all GitHub work by haiku.

**Reality against the brief (R1–R9).**

| # | The brief or plan said | What P11c does, and why |
|---|---|---|
| R1 | The km axis "as in the registry" | The sign convention is A§6 (`tools/geo/rivernet/place.ts`, `test/rivernet-place.test.ts`): `km_to_nl_entry` is positive upstream of the entry node, 0 at it, negative below, and falls downstream. So **x = −km_to_nl_entry** and the axis grows downstream. `packages/contracts/src/reaches.ts` gets a doc comment saying so |
| R2 | Lixhe is above Eijsden (the issue's listing) | The registry puts the Lixhe weir after Eijsden (+0.34 against +0.51, F1 of §35, KG-264). The order is the data's: `path.ts` sorts by km and hard-codes no station order, and the test asserts Lixhe after Eijsden. KG-287 |
| R3 | `stations.json` gives km, river and role | It gives none (`ApiStation`). Kilometres and reaches come only from `reaches-<ver>.json`, which holds the audience's primary stations (twins, mirrors, canal points and unsnapped stations are absent); the owner host serves its variant at the same path, read by the same `useReachGraph`. `GraphStation` of the web contract gains `km_to_nl_entry` (nullable, optional, `.catch(undefined)`, so older typed literals still compile); name, tier, flags and series come from `ApiStation` |
| R4 | A station's `river_id` says which branch it is on | It does not: the Millingen gauges carry `rhine` on `waal.2/.3`. Membership is therefore taken from the **reach graph**: `buildPath` walks `downstream` from the start station's reach and, at each split, enters only the downstream reaches whose river ranks highest in the path's list (`rhine.57` to `waal.1` or `pannerdensch-kanaal.1`; `nederrijn.1` to `ijssel.1` or `nederrijn.2`; weir side channels of equal rank both kept). A station is a member when its reach was visited, its km is a number, it is in `stations.json` and, on the Meuse, it lies between Chooz and Lith beneden |
| R5 | Kilometres of BE and FR rivers are river km | They are the graph's chainage (KG-157); the browser never recomputes them. Owner and public km come from different builds (KG-164). KG-285 |
| R6 | State or Δ colour | Δ only (D-2). The State choice is disabled with the KG-270 hint |
| R7 | The Meuse path is continuous | On the public graph there is one gap of 139 km, `fr.sandre.B720000002` (+139.74) to Eijsden (+0.51), longer than `GAP_KM` (120, `features/flow/chain.ts`): a hatched band with the text `hov_gap_wallonia`, in the chart and as a column of the table. On the owner variant the SPW gauges fill it and no gap shows. KG-287 |
| R8 | The fps criteria are re-verified | `fps.spec.ts` gets two scenarios with the panel open and playing (desktop, 4× CPU mobile), report-only in CI like KG-269 (`FPS_GATE=1` fails on them); the owner's GPU run stays [U]. KG-281 |
| R9 | Visual baselines come with the PR | They were not needed: CI's pinned image passed the three scenes of `visual.spec.ts` against the P11b baselines on the P11c head (the toggle is within `maxDiffPixelRatio` 0.002; the panel is in no scene). KG-284 |

**What was built (as built, with the facts the plan did not have).**
- **Paths and columns** (`features/flow/hovmoller/path.ts`, pure). `rhine-waal`, `rhine-lek`, `rhine-ijssel` from Basel (`ch.bafu.2289`) and `meuse` from Chooz (`fr.sandre.B720000001`) to `nl.rws.lith.beneden`; a missing start station gives an empty path. A column is `{ id, name, riverId, x, tier, tidal, owner }` (`owner` = the station has a series of an owner source, `tidal` from the reach or the station flag); gaps are consecutive columns more than `GAP_KM` apart, `wallonia` on the Meuse when the gap ends at or above the NL entry, else `plain`.
- **Rows and cells** (`grid.ts`, pure). Rows are whole UTC hours in pages of 168 aligned to the end of `playRange`; there are at most two pages, and a range that starts exactly 14 days back on a whole hour leaves its first hour off both (KG-290). A full page asks **192 h** of frames: 168 rows plus the 24-hour lead, `[from, to)` through `hovFetch`. `buildGrid` reads each hour once (memoised, one row's h − 24 h is another's h), restricted to the path's series, and returns a grey cell for no value, a value past its staleness limit or no value 24 h before.
- **The panel** (`HovmollerPanel.tsx`, `HovTable.tsx`, `chart.ts`, a dynamic entry; ECharts only through `import('./chart.ts')`). It calls `useFrames` itself (the page's frames exist only while playing) with the full station list, so a lapsed station is a column with grey cells; the public query keys are shared with the page's own frames, and on the owner host the page is one bounded `/api/v1/frames` call (again on the next whole hour, and one beside the playback's own while both run). The chart is created only in the chart view; the t line and the selected column are a small separate series. The table renders the newest 48 rows first (`NEWEST_ROWS`, "Toon alle uren" for the rest, KG-289); every cell says its change in words ("+12 cm", "−40 m³/s", "geen gegevens"). A click on a cell or a row or column header pauses playback, moves `t` and opens the station. The frames credits are listed under the panel.
- **App and layout.** A toggle in `.controls` (`aria-pressed`) opens the panel with `meuse` when the river chip says so, else `rhine-waal`. Closed, the DOM and CSS are as before; open, the panel is an in-flow child of the stage between the view and the timebar, `min(40dvh, 20rem)` high (`--hov-h`), and the two `.corner` rules add `--hov-h`; `--timebar-h` is reset in `.hovOpen .body`. **Known limit:** on a 768 px screen the plot gets under 1 px per hour row for 168 rows, so the chart is for the pattern and the table is the precise view (KG-288).
- **URL.** `hov` is the enum `rhine-waal|rhine-lek|rhine-ijssel|meuse` (`HOV_PATHS` in `lib/url/url.ts`, so the entry chunk never loads the panel); an invalid value is dropped; opening the panel never autoplays.
- **Hook.** `window.__rwsHov` (e2e build only, `import.meta.env.MODE === 'e2e'`): the chart, columns, rows, `cellAt` and `pixelOf`. It is not in `__rws.charts` (the station panels' idle check counts those); `build.test.ts` greps every built file for `__rws`.

**Evidence ([CI]) of #26's criteria.** Results of the CI-only runs are in the PR; no number here is invented.

| Criterion | Test |
|---|---|
| **P11c:** the km axis runs upstream to downstream as in the registry | `apps/web/test/hov-path.test.ts` on the fixture graph and synthetic `ApiStation[]` ("x strictly increasing, and the order is the registry's km, upstream first" for the four paths; one branch per path; Millingen on the Waal only; "puts Lixhe after Eijsden, the Grensmaas points in, and Maaseik and Herenlaak in two columns"; the D-3 merges; the canal point, the unsnapped gauge, the canary and the SPW gauges never a column; "finds exactly one on the public Meuse: Wallonia"), and `apps/web/e2e/p11c.spec.ts` (tick order and table headers equal the registry order) |

## 38. Amendment: fix #110, travel-time v2 and the Ourthe join (2026-10-10)

What PR 1 of issue #110 (the follow-ups of P11a, KG-262 to KG-265) settled. PR 2 (#115, below) holds the Vesdre and Amblève.

**Owner decisions (2026-10-10, binding for this PR).**
- **Published anchors only.** The v2 data are the sourced catalogue §3.7 anchors: no low-water legs (map-rivers' own cross-correlation), no map-rivers medians, no UNVERIFIED figure. Chalaines to Chiers is left out (no gauge at the confluence); Namur or Ourthe to Borgharen is left out (owner-only SPW gauges can never be in the public reaches file).
- **Whole hours, rounded outward, for the seven Rhine ranges, Emmerich with a floor of 1 h** (KG-263): Andernach 28–49, Köln 22–41, Wesel 6–20, Emmerich 1–9; Bonn 24–49, Düsseldorf 11–34, Ruhrort 13–27 unchanged. The scan of GWIO 85.006 appendix 1 is the evidence (unstruck rows; catalogue §3.7, §8 C1).
- **Lixhe stays after Eijsden** (KG-264): both providers' coordinates put the gauge in the downstream pool of the weir, about 190 m north of `eijsden.grens`. Documented in the `registry/snap-overrides.yaml` reason; no graph change.
- **Two PRs.** The Ourthe join is in this one; the Vesdre and Amblève are PR 2.

**What changed.**
- **Contract** (`packages/contracts/src/reaches.ts`, `rivers.ts`): a travel time holds exactly one of `h` or `d`, each a range or a single positive number; a single number needs a reviewed `label` {nl, en} (1 to 80 characters each); `derived: true` marks a derived figure. `schema_version` stays 1 (`deploy/bin/rws-rivers-refresh` pins it) and a pre-#110 row is still valid. `validateRivers` reports `exactly one of h and d`, `a single value needs its label` and `a range must be lo < hi`.
- **Registry** (`registry/rivers.yaml`): 22 `travel_times`: the seven Rhine ranges; Basel to Maxau 23 h; Maxau to Lobith 4 to 5 d, Kaub 2 d and Koblenz 40 to 45 h (derived); seven Lobith onward values (GWIO 85.006 appendix 2); Eijsden to St. Pieter 1 h, Borgharen 3.5 h, Venlo 38 h and Megen 82 h (§3.7). The label text is reviewed registry text, rendered as text only (T-WEB-6).
- **Outputs** (`tools/geo/rivernet/outputs.ts`, `place.ts`): every travel field is copied to `reaches-<ver>.json`; a reach's own `travel_time_h` is set only for an `h` range.
- **Join rule** (`tools/geo/rivernet/build.ts`): for a join onto another river, the vertex of a kept way that carries `to_river` but not `river`, nearest `at` and within `max_m`, becomes a graph node. New join `ourthe → meuse` at [5.5796611, 50.6230914], `max_m` 150, landing 97 m away. `ourthe.1` now runs into `meuse.27`; the 15 Ourthe SPW gauges get `km_to_nl_entry` 22.78 to 149.72 and entry node `eijsden`. The old `meuse.26` is now `meuse.26` and `meuse.27`; every old Meuse N of 27 or more is now N+1 (Meuse km_graph values are unchanged). KG-161 still lists the Ill, Lys, Schwalm, Dieze and Aa of Weerijs as detached.

**Where reality differs from the plan:** the issue named the PEGELONLINE gauge for Basel; `de.wsv.2310010` is a tier-2 mirror that never reaches the public file, so the pair starts at the BAFU primary `ch.bafu.2289` (a placement test now fails when any registry pair is dropped).

**Evidence ([CI]):** the v2 shapes: `packages/contracts/test/rivers.test.ts` (travel_times describe) and `packages/contracts/test/reaches.test.ts` (a pre-#110 row stays valid); every registry pair reaches the file: `test/rivernet-placement.test.ts`; the landing vertex: `test/rivernet-build.test.ts` (the join splits the target way, a same-river join splits nothing, beyond `max_m` nothing splits and `join_too_far` throws, a shared way never counts); the Ourthe group: `test/owner-reaches.test.ts`; the 22 texts in NL and EN: `apps/web/test/travel-file.test.ts`, with `eta-scan.test.ts`, `flow-rows.test.ts` and `pages-data.test.ts`; the renumbered Meuse reaches: `reach-colour.test.ts`, `reach-spans.test.ts`, `test/reach-spans-owner.test.ts` and the e2e `p11b`/`owner-p11b` specs; the fixture tiles: `tools/geo/fixtures/README.md` (run 38005400582, whose reaches file equals the fixture but for `version` and `travel_times`).

**Production needs** a geo release published from main (`geo.yml` `rivernet-publish`: a `workflow_dispatch` on main, or the monthly cron) and `rws-rivers-refresh` on the VPS. Until then production serves the old file (7 ranges, no Ourthe join). The e2e river tiles `tools/geo/fixtures/rivers-fixture.pmtiles` carry the old reach ids until the lead replaces them from CI.

**Gaps:** KG-262, KG-263, KG-264 and KG-265 close in #110 (KG-262 and KG-265 show in production after the geo release); KG-161 narrows (the Ourthe is joined); KG-274 (the time shift of the reach colours) stays open.

**PR 2 (#115): the Vesdre and the Amblève, with a fixture refresh.**
- **Registry.** `registry/rivers.yaml` gains `vesdre` (Q707598, OSM relation 12117339, "Vesder" / "Vesdre") and `ambleve` (Q461361, relation 12641506, "Amblève"), both `parent_river_id: ourthe`. `registry/snap-overrides.yaml` `waters` maps the BE-3 label "Vesdre" to `vesdre` (7 gauges, all within 154 m of the river) and "Amblève" to `ambleve` (8 gauges, all within 25 m). The distances in the older `reason`s were measured on the earlier fixture (OSM 2026-10-01); the two new `waters` rows were measured on this one (OSM 2026-10-09).
- **Fixture refresh.** The four `tools/geo/fixtures/rivernet.*` files are the artifact of `geo.yml` run 38006225186 (`workflow_dispatch` on `claude/fix-110-vesdre-ambleve`, OSM 2026-10-09T20:21:04Z; PBF 2,073,740 bytes). The refresh changed almost nothing else: only the lengths of `ahr.1` and `mark.1` by metres; the Meuse and every other reach id are unchanged. The readers' golden moved from 6,672 ways and 223 relations to 6,724 and 225; the bifurcation golden is unchanged.
- **Reach split of the Ourthe.** The Ourthe (130.98 km) is now cut at its two confluences, which are shared OSM nodes (no join needed): `ourthe.1` (101.147 km, to the Amblève at Comblain), `ourthe.2` (27.108 km, to the Vesdre at Chênée) and `ourthe.3` (2.726 km, to the Ourthe join onto `meuse.27`). New reaches `ambleve.1` (85.3 km) and `vesdre.1` (72.3 km) carry no public station. The 15 Ourthe SPW gauges sit on parts of `ourthe.1` to `ourthe.3`; the BE-3 placement rises by the 15 new gauges (87 added points); the owner Eijsden chain has a Vesdre and an Amblève group, nested in the Ourthe's, in graph order.
- **Production needs** a geo release published from main and `rws-rivers-refresh`, as for the Ourthe join; until then it serves the old file.
- **Gaps:** KG-163 narrows to the unmapped Ourthe and Dendre headwater labels; KG-164 now names OSM 2026-10-09.

## 39. Amendment: fix #112 PR A, per-hour state in frames (2026-10-10)

What PR A of issue #112 built: item 1 (a state code per series and hour in the frames, so playback runs in the State mode) and the Hovmöller State choice. PR B (the tile position bins and the travel-time shift) is separate and not described here.

**Owner decisions (2026-10-10, binding).**
- **D-1 Two PRs.** PR A is item 1 plus D-3 (server, contracts, web; no geo release; "Part of #112"). PR B is items 2 and 3 ("Closes #112").
- **D-2 The played hour shows the state and the section badge.** Frames gain a state code per series and hour (`no_ref` to `extreme`, plus a bit when the state comes from an area class). Table, chain, popup, panel, markers and reaches show the played state; the basis text, the class label and the `area` beside a gauge state stay hidden behind the existing "played back" badge. No provider text enters frames.
- **D-3 The Hovmöller State choice is enabled** and the cells are coloured by the played state ladder (KG-282 closes).
- **Reviewers** (workflow default): Sonnet (high) for the code review and Sonnet (high) for the security review, read-only; the lead fixes small findings.

**What changed.**
- **Contract** (`packages/contracts/src/api.ts`, `static.ts`): `framesObject` is `schemaVersion: 2` with a `state` matrix parallel to `vlast`. Code = `STATES.indexOf(state)` (0 `no_ref`, 1 `low`, 2 `normal`, 3 `elevated`, 4 `high`, 5 `extreme`) plus `SECTION_BIT` (8) when the state comes from an area class; the valid codes are exactly 0 to 5 and 8 to 13 (`stateCode`, `isStateCode`, `stateOf`). `checkFrames` also demands one `state` row per series and a valid code exactly where `vlast` holds a value and `null` exactly where it is null. `FramesFile`, `FramesAnswer` and `OwnerFramesAnswer` are v2 only; `framesObjectV1` and `FramesFileAny` (a discriminated union of the refined v1 and v2 shapes) exist for the static readers only: the web's static parser, verify-prod's settled-day reads and the frames recorder.
- **Classifier** (`apps/server/src/api/states.ts`): the shared builders of `readStates` were extracted without changing its answers, and `readHourStates(db, family, {ids, vlast}, from, to, opts)` classifies a whole range in one read snapshot (warnings overlapping the range, the latest class row before `from` and every one inside it, refs and series from the `StaticCache`), in process, per hour. A series with no ref, class or area in the range is code 0 without `classify`.
- **Producers:** `renderFrames` (`publish/render/frames.ts`, display views for the values) and `readFrames` (`api/data.ts`, api views) both write v2 with `state`. The refs, classes and warnings always come from `VIEWS[family]`; the values come from the caller's views.
- **Re-render:** `#framesDirty` is also set by dirty `reference`, `class` and `warning` rows that reach the unsettled span. `BumpReason` gains `'schema'` (like `'registry'`: the old complete version stays named until the new one completes). `framesSchemaBump` (P18a: replaced by `schemaBump(tx, now)` in `load/dirty.ts`, which also stores `snapshot_schema:tide`, §54 "P18a as built") runs in `migrate`'s `publishTail`, before `registryBump`.
- **Web:** the frame store decodes the code of the bucket a value came from; a v1 chunk gives values with the state unknown (shown as no data in the State mode, never as `no_ref`); `playDisabled(reduced)` no longer looks at the mode, the State-mode hints (`play_state_hint`, `hov_state_hint`) are gone; the Hovmöller State choice is on, with a state reader beside the Δ one in `grid.ts`.

**Where the build differs from the issue's proposal, and why.**

| # | Issue or plan said | Built | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| C1 | The state "of the hour" | The cell of hour h is classified at the instant h + 1 h - 1 ms (the partial current hour at `min(that, now)`) | `pub_obs_at` takes `ts <= t` and a stamp exactly on :00 is common (10-minute and hourly sources); at t = h + 1 h the snapshot would take the next hour's :00 value, while bucket h holds the last value before it (§36 R12). The cell therefore equals the snapshot at the last instant the value belongs to |
| C3 | Re-render on `obs` dirty rows | `recent.json` also re-renders on `reference`, `class` and `warning` rows reaching the unsettled span | The state is derived from them; a new class or warning changes a cell without any new value |
| C4 | "Bump the day versions of rendered days" | A one-time bump of the last 16 public days (reason `schema`), stored under the meta key `frames_schema:public`; a database never migrated before bumps nothing and only stores the schema | 16 days cover the 14-day playback start and its 25 h Δh lead; a fresh database has rendered nothing, so a bump would only waste cycles |
| C5 | State of a v1 file unspecified | A v1 file is "state unknown" and shows as no data in the State mode, never as `no_ref` | `no_ref` means "this series has no reference", a statement about the data; a day rendered before the schema says nothing about it |
| C6 | One shape | Strict v2 in the publisher and the API; `FramesFileAny` (v1 or v2) only in the static readers | A publisher that could write v1 would hide a regression; the readers must still parse the days not yet re-rendered and the recorded low-water scene |
| C13 | Each non-null cell has a state | The partial current hour (never played) is classified at `now` | Its last instant is still in the future; classifying at now keeps `state` non-null exactly where `vlast` is |
| C14 | Views unspecified | Rows (refs, classes, warnings) from `VIEWS[family]`, values from the caller's views | The same split as `readStates`; the publisher's values come from the display views and the API's from the api views (§36 R11) |
| D-2 | "`state` and `basis` for the played hour" | No basis in frames | Basis text is provider-derived; the issue mentions it, the owner decision keeps it out. The played hour shows the state word and the section badge only |
| Memo | A bounded LRU per (family, day, version) in both processes | An exact per-series memo inside `readHourStates` (key: the valid rows, the NL-4 season day and the value's place among the series' reference values; classify compares a value only with reference values, so this is exact); a settled-day memo (`HourMemo`, key `family|day|version`) in the API route only, used when the day versions are known; none in the publisher | A settled day renders once per version in the publisher, so a memo there would never hit; in the API, repeated 14-day requests reuse the settled days |
| Owner | Public frames never hold an owner-shaped state | In the public family a code whose state an owner-only source shaped throws `owner_basis` (fail closed, as `publicSnapshot`) | Belt and braces beside the public views and the `family: 'public'` classify rule (invariants 8 and 11) |

**Measured (L0, the `bench-q1` style seed: 1,500 series, half with 4 DE-1 references, a third with DE-6 classes, 200 warnings; random values).** Real data compresses better and repeats values, so these are upper bounds.
- A `recent.json` render (82.5k cells): the state codes take 127 to 208 ms wall. A settled day: 89 to 155 ms.
- A 14-day `/api/v1/frames`: cold 1.7 to 1.9 s CPU in total, warm (settled days from the memo) 1.3 to 1.4 s. The 2 s `statement_timeout` does not bound Node CPU; the heavy rate class, the semaphore and the single flight still apply.
- Sizes: a settled day 418 KiB plain (169 KiB gzip) against 344 KiB (161 KiB gzip) in v1; 7 days 2.85 MB (1.14 MB gzip); 14 days 5.7 MB, under `MAX_FRAMES_BYTES` (16 MiB). The A§8 Q5 estimate (370 KB gzip for 3,000 × 72) predates the state rows and is for the values alone.

**Criteria (#112 "Verify", item 1).**

| # | Criterion | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| 1a | State mode: Play enabled; reaches, markers, table and chain show the played state | evidence: see PR |
| 1b | A frames file without the new row fails the strict parse | evidence: see PR |
| 1c | The 7-day size within `MAX_FRAMES_BYTES` and the Q5 order of magnitude | evidence: see PR (measured above) |
| 1d | The played state equals the snapshot state of the same hour | evidence: see PR |
| 1e | The canary sweeps stay green; no owner state in a public file | evidence: see PR |

**Upgrade.** No host file and no migration file: the bump runs in `migrate` (`publishTail`, under the loader lock) and logs `frames schema bump N day(s)` (P18a: `schema bump N day(s)`). It marks the public days of the last 16 (the unsettled ones included, which only get an early version) with reason `schema`; the publisher then re-renders about 14 settled days at one per cycle, and each day also re-renders its 144 snapshot files (the `registryBump` load pattern), while the old complete versions stay named and served. Meanwhile the web plays those days from the v1 frames with the state unknown: Δh and Q work, the State mode shows no data for those hours. Days older than the bump window keep v1 for good. A second `migrate` bumps nothing.

**Gaps:** KG-270, KG-280 and KG-282 close; KG-292 to KG-296 open (see `docs/known-gaps.md`).

## 40. Amendment: fix #112 PR B, reach position bins and the travel-time shift (2026-10-10)

What PR B of issue #112 built: item 2 (position bins in the river tiles, so a long reach shows its change along it) and item 3 (an indicative travel-time shift of the reach colours). It is stacked on PR A (§39) and closes #112.

**Owner decisions (2026-10-10, binding).**
- **D-1 Two PRs.** PR A is §39. PR B is items 2 and 3 ("Closes #112").
- **D-4 The shift is exact pairs only.** A span is shifted only where a sourced (never `derived`) travel time names exactly its two ends (`from` in the span's up group, `to` in its down group). Everywhere else the colours are unshifted. The legend says "tijdverschoven, indicatief / time-shifted, indicative". No apportioning by chainage, and no numeric ETA anywhere.

**What changed.**
- **Tile layer `reach_bins`.** `tools/geo/rivernet/bins.ts`: `BIN_M` 500, `BIN_MAX` 8, `BIN_MINZOOM` 8; `binCount(km)` is the rounded metres divided by 500, floored, clamped to 1..8 (null: 1); `binLines` cuts the drawn line into n equal parts. `outputs.ts` writes `reach-bins.geojsonseq` (per bin `reach_id`, `bin` 0-based, `seg` = `<reach_id>/<bin>`, `tidal`, feature-level `tippecanoe.minzoom` 8). `tiles.sh build <rivers> <out> [<bins>]` names the two layers (`-L rivers:`, `-L reach_bins:`), the bins file beside the input, no network; `geo.yml` passes it.
- **Two tile generations in the web.** `hasReachBins` (`features/map/rivers.ts`) reads the archive's metadata once (same origin, lazy `import('pmtiles')`) and takes only the ids of `vector_layers`; any failure means false. The rivers source has `promoteId: {rivers: 'reach_id', reach_bins: 'seg'}`. Without the layer the reach colouring paints per reach at every zoom, as before.
- **Per-bin paints.** Each bin is painted from the span value at its own centre `(i+0.5)·L/n` (`FeatureSpan.bins`); on the owner variant the centre is evaluated in the owner part that holds it. `addReaches` adds the five bin layers (`<id>-bin`, source-layer `reach_bins`, minzoom 8, butt caps) when the bins promise resolves true, limits the per-reach layers to zooms [0, 8) and writes per-bin feature states (changed keys only).
- **The shift.** `reaches/shift.ts`: `shiftHours` (the range's midpoint, or the single value, whole hours, days × 24; derived: null), `spanShift`, `shiftAt(T, pos)` (T · position, rounded to the hour) and `maxShift`. A shifted span reads its down end at t and its up end `shiftAt` hours earlier. A missing past value makes that end missing, so the reach is "no data".
- **Frames window.** While playing, the lead is 25 h + the largest T (`usePlayback` `extraLeadHours`). Paused, a second frames read covers the whole UTC days around [t − T − 25 h, t) (from the day of t − T − 25 h to the end of t's day, never past now nor before the display start), only while the map shows the reach colours and for a t up to now, reading only the shifted ends' series; it is one file per UTC day, cached 300 s and shares query keys with playback and the Hovmöller panel, and a scrubbed t rebuilds nothing until its day changes. Nothing is read when no span is shifted. T is capped at 96 h (`MAX_SHIFT_H`, review round 1): a longer figure leaves its span unshifted. The lead is fixed when Play starts (KG-302).

**Where the build differs from the issue's proposal, and why.**

| # | Issue or plan said | Built | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| C8 | Bins in the `rivers` tiles | A second layer `reach_bins` | The flow dashes and the existing per-reach features stay untouched; a bin feature carries only `reach_id`, `bin`, `seg`, `tidal` |
| C9 | Bins at every zoom | Feature-level minzoom 8, per-reach layers drawn below it | Tippecanoe's per-tile limits would drop features unpredictably in the dense low-zoom tiles; z5 and z7 tiles hold `rivers` alone |
| C10 | The web assumes the new tiles | A metadata read picks the generation | Between the web deploy and the tile refresh the installed archive has no bins; a rollback of the tiles must also work |
| C12 | Shift every travel time to Lobith or a span | Exact pairs only (D-4) | Most sourced travel times span an intermediate station; apportioning them by chainage would invent a figure. One span matches on the national release |

**Measured.** Fixture run and full-data run 38038752392 are both green, and the national release equals the fixture graph.
- `rivers-20261010.pmtiles`: 2,471,390 bytes (1,653,660 without bins; the gate is 30 MB). Layers `rivers` 714 features and `reach_bins` 4,332 (1 to 8 per reach: 153 reaches of 1 bin, 473 of 8). Bins sit only in tiles of zoom 8 and above.
- Item 3: exactly one shifted span: Emmerich `de.wsv.2790020` to Lobith, [1, 9] h, T = 5 h, reach `rhine.56` (10.328 km, 8 bins). Every other travel time spans an intermediate station or is derived.
- Cost: production's `frames/recent.json` (v1) is 430 KB raw and 123 KB gzip (2026-10-10). The paused shift read adds about that per paused page view (cached 300 s, shared with playback and the Hovmöller panel). On the owner site it is one bounded `/api/v1/frames` call (two to three days, ending at now) per paused day.

**Criteria (#112 "Verify", items 2 and 3).**

| # | Criterion | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| 2a | Tiles carry `reach_bins` with 1 to 8 bins per reach, only from zoom 8; the 30 MB gate holds | evidence: see PR |
| 2b | At zoom 8 and above a long reach shows more than one colour; below it one per reach | evidence: see PR |
| 2c | Old tiles (no `reach_bins`): per-reach colours at every zoom, no error | evidence: see PR |
| 2d | Owner variant: a bin takes the colour of the part that holds its centre | evidence: see PR |
| 3a | Only exact sourced pairs are shifted; derived and intermediate-station figures are not | evidence: see PR |
| 3b | The legend labels the shift; no numeric ETA appears; the frames window grows by T and stays within `MAX_FRAMES_BYTES` | evidence: see PR |

**Deploy order.** (1) The owner merges; the web deploys. The installed tiles are the old archive, so the map keeps per-reach colours as today. (2) The owner dispatches `geo.yml` on `main`; first check for a same-day `geo-*` release (a geo release is never rewritten). (3) `sudo rws-rivers-refresh` installs the new archive; the bins are live. (4) `scripts/verify-prod.sh <domain>` rivers checks. A rollback of the tiles (`--rollback`) falls back to per-reach colours.

**Gaps:** KG-271 and KG-274 close; KG-298 to KG-303 open (see `docs/known-gaps.md`; KG-303 is the bins' frame-rate cost measured in the build).

## 42. Amendment: P12a reality, flood hardening, WireGuard and the owner site (2026-10-10)

What P12a (#27, PR #130, "Part of #27") built, and where the build differs from the P12 brief. The plan was approved by the owner on 2026-10-10 (one PR; the connection limit stays in `roles.sql` with a guard migration).

**Owner decisions (2026-10-10, binding).**
- **One PR** for the whole of P12a (WireGuard was not pulled forward).
- **The `rws_api` connection limit stays in `deploy/postgres/roles.sql`** (applied as superuser by `db_prepare` on every deploy). A migration cannot set it because `rws_migrator` cannot `ALTER ROLE`. A read-only guard migration (`20261109000001_connection_budget_guard.sql`) fails a migrate when the budget is broken.

**Where the build differs from the brief, and why.**

| # | Brief said | Built | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| D-1 | "a migration sets `rws_api` CONNECTION LIMIT" | `roles.sql` sets it; a read-only guard migration checks `rws_api ≤ max_connections − (load + publish + owner_api) − 5` | `rws_migrator` has no `ALTER ROLE`; `roles.sql` already runs as superuser on every deploy (owner decision) |
| D-2 | Brownout auto-arms "when 503 responses exceed 2 % for 5 min" | Every 5xx on `/api/v1/*` over all `/api/v1/*` requests, ≥ 200 requests, 15 s buckets; the brownout's own 503s (`X-Brownout`) excluded; disarm after 10 min under 0.5 % | A dead upstream answers 502 from Caddy and a saturated api 503 `busy`: both mean the API cannot keep up. Excluding its own refusals keeps the brownout from holding itself on (KG-307) |
| D-3 | "file-watched" flag | A host-side evaluator (`rws-brownout evaluate`, systemd timer every 15 s, root) reads Caddy's access log; the containers only read `/run/rws-brownout/active` (2 s cache) | The access log is on the `caddy_data` volume, which no container but Caddy may read; the flag directory is mounted read-only |
| D-4 | "one offset" for the flood drill | One offset per payload; an alert and its Cancel share one | The recordings come from different days (2023 to 2026), so a single offset would put some in the future. The LHP test-server stations carry two clocks (`updated` vs. the readings), so their events land 35 min before the drill clock. LU-Alert identifiers are shifted too, since the base archive already holds the real Cancel of the drilled alert |
| D-5 | Wayback Vigicrues levels 2–3 replayed | A synthetic level-4 map (`fr-5-vigilance-level4.synthetic`) with the Wayback's structure on the 56 real sections (levels 2, 3 and 4) | The real Wayback payload names none of our 56 sections; the loader refuses it as `too_few_areas` |
| D-6 | Provider blackholed by the fake upstream | The fake upstream blackholes per host (a control file), and the chaos check proves the cause through `capture.json` and `status.json` | Pausing the whole fake would also silence the fake healthchecks; every capture group holds unfaked specs, so a `/fail` alone is not causal (KG-305) |
| D-7 | "others' p95 moves ≤ 10 %" | ≤ max(10 %, 5 ms) | CI p95 values are a few milliseconds; 10 % of that is below the run-to-run noise (KG-304) |
| D-8 | History view clamps to 30 days | The API refuses spans over 30 days while the brownout is on, and the chart asks `res=1h` | The panel's periods are 2, 7 and 14 days, so no web clamp is needed (KG-312) |
| D-9 | "loader lag holds while api is saturated", from the six k6 clients | The saturation phase sends from a crowd of 126 addresses (203.0.114.128–253 in the outside namespace, 21 per k6 process, about 6 r/s each, inside the limiter), at most 2 × the rate in flight | Six addresses at the edge of their limiter got 429s and 2 ms answers and never saturated the API. The first crowd run without the in-flight cap filled Caddy's 256 MiB with about 7,600 TLS connections and measured Caddy, not the API (KG-313, ADR-0019 §5) |

**What changed.** The PR body of #130 lists every piece. The new commands are in CLAUDE.md § Commands, and the gaps are KG-304 to KG-316, R-094 (R-029 closed), R-095 (the expiring Grype rules) and, from review round 1, R-096 and R-097. ADR-0019 records the tuning values with the k6 evidence; ADR-0020 records the HSTS preload decision (D17: not at launch).
