## 49. Amendment: P14a backfill runner, row rules and NL-1 (2026-10-12)

What P14a (issue #29, group P14a) built: the resumable backfill runner (`backfill` server role, `registry/backfill.yaml`, `backfill_job` and its ledger `backfill_chunk`), the row rules in the loader's upsert, yearly partitions below 2026-01-01, and the NL-1 history on top of them. The runbook is `docs/runbooks/backfill.md`; the rules are A§6 and A§8 Q6; the threat is T-BF-1 (trust boundary 7). The owner decisions of 2026-10-12: bit 512 plus `ingest_batch.origin` (no new qc bit); P40D chunks; validated is Gecontroleerd and Definitief; at most 5 live NL-1 requests (made by `scripts/smoke-capture.ts`, no X-API-KEY).

- **Evidence ([CI]).**
  - Backfill never changes a live row unless the provider-validated flag is set, and every such change is in `obs_revision`: `apps/server/test/load/backfill-precedence.int.test.ts` (the Q6 matrix, plus a fast-check property over random live, fill and backfill sequences in random orders: the same final `obs`, a revision for every live-row change, no live row changed by an unvalidated backfill row).
  - Kill and restart resume with no duplicates and no gaps: `apps/server/test/backfill/resume.int.test.ts` with `backfill/crash-child.ts` (a real SIGKILL since review round 1, after the put, after the append and after the cursor; 9 of 9 tests green on 3 runs (about 15 s each), kills after the put, after the append, after the cursor and in the middle of a request; the row set equals the fixtures exactly once, the ledger is reconciled, a re-run gives 0 new and 0 revised).
  - The per-provider rate budget holds, on top of the live 400 requests an hour: `apps/server/test/capture/budget.test.ts` (live stays above 300 and at most 400; backfill `min_interval_ms` at least 1000, `max_per_hour` at most 3600, the off-peak window) and `apps/server/test/backfill/pacer.test.ts` (fake clock: spacing, refused outside the window, stops at the budget).
  - Partitions: `apps/server/test/db/partitions.int.test.ts`; rollups, `dayVersions` and D9: `apps/server/test/load/backfill-rollups.int.test.ts`; reconciliation and truncation: `apps/server/test/backfill/truncation.test.ts` and the ledger asserts of `resume.int.test.ts`; the dry-run: `apps/server/test/backfill/dry-run.test.ts`.
- **[U] items** (also in `docs/known-gaps.md`): KG-339 (RWS at 160,000 values), KG-340 (where the 10-minute data starts per station), KG-341 (the `recover()` race on the shared day manifest), KG-342 (history under other methods is dropped), KG-343 (the [agent-prod] freshness check waits for the production run), KG-344 (the DB projection is computed, not measured), KG-345 (the order-independence assumption), KG-346 (a throttled run forgets its backoff on restart; review round 1). KG-122 is updated.
- **Reality differs from the plan and the issue.**
  - **Chunks are P40D, not about 2.5 years.** Our parser caps are 10,000 values per list and 150,000 nodes (about 11 nodes per value), so a 2.5-year chunk of 10-minute values would be cut. P40D holds 5,760 values per list, under 90 % of the cap. The caps stay (`JSON_CAPS`, 25 MiB wire and 100 MiB decoded). 13,776 chunks and 15,293 requests for NL-1 up to the data epoch, about 4.2 hours at 1 request/s. A truncated answer halves the chunk at its cursor down to one day (review round 1).
  - **Validated means Gecontroleerd and Definitief** (qc bit 2, the mapping live and in the backfill since P2b). The issue's default was Definitief only; one bit and a single mapping won, because every qc bit is taken and live rows are Ongecontroleerd in practice.
  - **Hoedanigheid NVT is sent for Q in the backfill only.** The smoke showed RWS answers 200 for Q with `Hoedanigheid NVT`; the live bodies are byte-identical to before (a test).
  - **Fill detection moved to the batch's origin.** Bit 512 now means "not captured live from the series' own source"; `ingest_batch.origin` (`live` or `backfill`) tells a fill from a backfill row. The set of fill rows is found by bit 512 and `origin = 'live'` (replay.md §7, R-068).
  - **Rollups stay inline per chunk.** A deferred drain would make the nightly `reconcileRollups` raise false `rollup_mismatch` alerts; each chunk is a bounded batch (one series, 40 days, about 960 hourly buckets), and `backfill_guard` throttles the runner while the loader lags.
  - **Yearly partitions below a constant boundary 2026-01-01**, not one read from the catalog (that depended on call order and broke the existing tests), with a `pg_partition_tree` guard that raises if a monthly `obs` partition lies below it. `forecast_value` keeps none below 2026-01-01.
  - **`dataSince` is clamped to `DATA_FLOOR`** (and `computeChecksums` reads from it): otherwise the public stations list would show 1990.
  - **204 chunks write no manifest line**, so a `key: null` line never reaches fetch health; the cursor moves only.
  - **History under other methods is dropped** (`unregistered_method`: F216, F009, F001, F029 are not registered series), counted and retained, never merged into the instantaneous series; registering them is the follow-up P14b (KG-342).
  - **The role budget** goes from 38 to 40 of `max_connections` 40 (33 + 2 + 5, no headroom; pinned by `roles.int.test.ts`): `rws_backfill` has CONNECTION LIMIT 2, the running job plus a status, pause or abort call beside it. Host files change, so the owner re-runs `bootstrap.sh` after the deploy (it creates `db_rws_backfill`); nothing starts the service. A rollback to an older release counts the new manifest lines (`retention: backfill`, `backfill`) as bad lines.
- **Left for later P14 PRs:** the other providers (DE-8, BE-3, BE-1/2, FR-2, CH-8, CH-9, LU-7 and so on), the climatology, and the storage ADR at about 50 GB.

### Review round 1 (2026-10-12)

Code review C1–C10 (Sonnet, high) and security review S1–S9 (Sonnet, high) on head 86f9cd2. No blocker or high finding. What was done:

| Finding | Done |
|---|---|
| C1 = S1 (two runners) | A lease table `backfill_lease(host, holder, until)` in migration 000001 (`rws_backfill`: SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE; advisory locks stay revoked). `runBackfill` takes the lease of every host its runnable jobs use with an atomic `INSERT … ON CONFLICT … WHERE until < now() OR holder = me`, renews it to now + 2 min before every request and gives it back at exit; a run that cannot take it exits 1 with `stopped: busy`. A killed runner's lease lapses within 2 minutes (runbook; its false "a second run only waits on the pacer" is gone). Tests: `backfill/run.test.ts` (memory store), `backfill/resume.int.test.ts` (two runners, the second `busy`, after the lapse it proceeds) |
| C2 + S2 (the job row, `--to`) | `DATA_EPOCH` (2026-10-02, `load/dirty.ts`, pinned to the `data_epoch` seed of `20261014000001_display_window.sql` by `backfill/spec.test.ts`); `plan` defaults `--to` to it and refuses a later one; `runJob` fails a job as `invalid_job` before any request unless its chunk is the spec's, its range lies in [spec floor, `DATA_EPOCH`] and its budget is at most the plan's. The fixed code is `invalid_job`, not `invalid`, which already names an invalid response body. T-BF-1's "never from the database" is corrected |
| S3 (loader window) | `LoadContext.backfill` (the line's chunk cut at `DATA_EPOCH`, set by the pipeline for a backfill spec); the NL-1 backfill loader also cuts at the spec floor `NL1_BACKFILL_FLOOR` (pinned to `registry/backfill.yaml`) and drops the rest as `outside_backfill`, counted in `dropped`, so both identities hold. Tests: `adapters/nl-1-backfill-golden.test.ts`, `load/backfill-precedence.int.test.ts` |
| C7 (partition floor) | `ensure_partitions` keeps the 2000-01-01 floor for every live caller and calls the body, now `ensure_history_partitions` (floor 1900, SECURITY DEFINER, fixed `search_path`, EXECUTE to `rws_load` only), which `upsertObs` calls in backfill mode only. Yearlies below 2026 come from either within its floor; the `pg_partition_tree` guard stays. `partitions.int.test.ts` and the privileges golden updated |
| C3 (truncation) | A truncated answer, a parser cap error or the client's size cap halves the chunk at that cursor (40, 20, 10, 5, 2.5, 1.25, 1 day) and asks again; below a day the job fails `truncated`. Nothing is committed for a truncated answer; every request counts. `backfill/truncation.test.ts` |
| C6 + S4 (backoff) | `stopped: throttled` (exit 1) when the client backs off past the window after a 403, 429, 451, 5xx or network failure; a request is counted only once it went out (not for a backoff, an open breaker or a refused URL; a request a kill interrupts is not counted). The runbook says a restart forgets the backoff |
| C5 + S6 (unloaded chunks) | `backfill_job.chunks_with_data` (the runner's, in the cursor's update); `backfill_guard` says `backlog` when a job of the source has more than 2 chunks with data the ledger does not hold (round 2, N1: now its own verdict `unloaded` above 30, active jobs only). Health `detail.backfill` gains `chunks_with_data` and `quarantined` (backfill batches of the source set aside), optional in the contracts; OpenAPI regenerated |
| S5 | `backfill_guard` fails closed when `computed_at` is missing (`COALESCE(…, '-infinity')`) |
| S7 | `roles.sql`: `rws_backfill` gets `statement_timeout` 5 s and `idle_in_transaction_session_timeout` 30 s; the roles.int defaults list follows |
| S8 | `loadBackfill` refuses a spec whose source is not `public` or has `history_export` off, or that selects a series narrowed to another audience (`backfill/spec.test.ts`) |
| S9 | The compose and nftables comments name the backfill job; the threat model writes down any-address egress on 443, the `db` network and the read-write archive |
| C8 | A comment at the `upsertObs` `ON CONFLICT`: race-free only because every obs writer holds the loader lock |
| C9 | `crash-child.ts` dies by `process.kill(process.pid, 'SIGKILL')`; `resume.int.test.ts` asserts `signal === 'SIGKILL'` |
| C4 | No code: with `--to` at most `DATA_EPOCH` a backfill never reaches the newest live point, so `obs_latest` never needs it (KG-345) |
| C10 | Accepted as is: `budget.test.ts` asserts the backfill limit and the live at most 400 an hour separately; their sum is the policy, and `max_per_hour` 3600 equals the 1 request/s cap |

The threat-model delta of the security review (items 1–8) is in v4.55. A budget-paused job is re-planned (abort, `plan --from` the cursor's day) instead of raised in SQL, since the runner refuses a budget above the plan's.

### Review round 2 (2026-10-12)

Combined code and security re-review of the round-1 fix diff (Sonnet, high), findings N1 to N6:

| Finding | Done |
|---|---|
| N1 (the guard throttled the run to weeks) | `backfill_guard` has a verdict of its own for unloaded chunks, `unloaded`, above **30** chunks with data that the ledger does not hold; `loader_lag` and `backlog` (age, files) come first, `stale` last. 30 is the arithmetic of a healthy night: the runner writes at most 1 chunk/s, the loader ticks every 10 s (`TICK_MS`) and reads up to 20 s a tick (`TICK_BUDGET_MS`), so 10 to 30 chunks wait normally. The runner sleeps `UNLOADED_SLEEP_MS` (15 s) on `unloaded` and `GUARD_SLEEP_MS` (5 min) on the others, so the 4.2 h pace of §7 holds. Tests: `pacer.test.ts` (a loader ticking every 10 s on a fake clock: 154 requests in under 3 minutes, no sleep over 1 s; the short sleep), `resume.int.test.ts` (31 and 30) |
| N2 (halved length for one cursor only) | `runJob` keeps the last working (halved) chunk length for the rest of the job; the halves cost requests, which the plan's 20 % can run out of (the job then pauses `budget` and is re-planned). `truncation.test.ts` |
| N3 (cursor not validated) | `runJob` also needs `cursor_ts` in [max(`range_from`, floor), `range_to`], else `invalid_job`. `run.test.ts` |
| N4 (aborted and failed jobs block the source) | Fixed with N1: the guard counts `planned`, `running` and `paused` jobs only. `resume.int.test.ts` |
| N5 (SIGTERM, throwing release) | The `run` CLI sets a stop flag on SIGTERM and SIGINT (`RunOptions.stop`, `stopped: interrupted`, exit 0; the sleep wakes at once), polled at the top of each pass, never between put, append and cursor; the `finally` releases the lease and a throwing `release` no longer masks the original error. Runbook §3. `run.test.ts` |
| N6 (a crash inside the fetch consumes no budget) | Accepted: the runbook already says `requests` may be one short after a crash |

Migration 000001 was edited in place (none of this PR's migrations is merged); its sha256 in `test/migrations.test.ts`, `db/schema.sql` and `generated.ts` follow.

### Incident 2026-10-12/13 and the health-scan fix (issue #29)

P14a was deployed on 2026-10-12 at 16:01Z. The first NL-1 backfill night ran from 22:01 to 05:00 UTC and inserted 7.29M history rows in 2,072 chunks (`revised` 0, `unreconciled` 0). Live freshness failed the [agent-prod] criterion (KG-343):

| Live lag (`loaded_at - fetched_at`, `origin = 'live'`) | p50 | p95 |
|---|---|---|
| Night 10-11 to 10-12, and 10-12 16:00 to 21:59 UTC after the deploy | 5 s | 10 s |
| 10-12 22:00 to 10-13 05:00 UTC (backfill) | 157 to 2,660 s | 743 to 3,598 s |
| 10-13 07:00 UTC | 31 s | 53 s |
| 10-14 11:41Z, no backfill for 30 h | - | 74 s (`/api/v1/health`) |

NL-1 and up to nine other sources were `down` from 01:00 to 04:00 UTC. The loader logged no errors and PostgreSQL no lock waits.

- **Root cause.** `computeHealth` runs every 60 s inside the single load loop. Its Q7 gap scan (and the outage variant) had `NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM obs ... o.ts >= g.b AND o.ts < g.b + step)` with `g.b` from a lateral `generate_series`: no constant `ts` bound, so the planner read every `obs` partition, history included. The cost grows with rows per tier-1 series times buckets times series, and the backfill put all 7.3M rows on 41 tier-1 NL-1 series. Reproduced on PostgreSQL 18: `computeHealth` 2.2 s without history, 43 to 45 s at 6.5M rows, 137 s at 21M. While the pass ran the loop loaded nothing, so the live lag was the tick budget (about 20 s) plus the pass: the 74 s that remained after the backfill. The live upsert (5 to 13 ms), `checkTwins`, `findOutages` and a backfill chunk load (about 0.1 s) were fine, and so was the P14a code alone (lag 10 s after the deploy).
- **The guard did not protect live data.** `backfill_guard` paused at a backlog age above 600 s, five times the 120 s freshness limit, and read a loader row that the slow pass refreshed once per cycle.
- **The fix.**
  - Both Q7 scans (24 h and last outage, `EXISTS` and `NOT EXISTS`) carry a constant `o.ts` bound of `Q7_LOOKBACK_MS` (48 h), so every history partition is pruned. The counts are identical; at 21M rows Q7 takes about 845 ms. The registry's longest `expected_step` is PT1H and its longest `staleness_limit` PT12H, pinned by `test/staleness-limit.test.ts`, so 48 h covers every window.
  - `backfill_guard` answers `backlog` above **60 s** (was 600 s, five times the 120 s freshness limit) and `loader_lag` for a loader row older than **150 s** (was 5 minutes; the health pass rewrites it every 60 to 90 s), in migration `20261111000001_backfill_guard_60s.sql`; the 3-file rule and the 30-chunk `unloaded` rule are unchanged. The Q7 bound is the fix; the guard is defence in depth (review R1).
  - `run.ts` raises the alert `health_slow` (`ms`) when the health block takes more than 10 s.
  - Evidence ([CI]): `health.int.test.ts` (about 300k backfilled rows in 2003 leave both counts unchanged; the scans without the bound agree over a sweep of `now` and outages, and a bound 2 h too tight fails it; `EXPLAIN` names no `obs_y...` partition), `roles.int.test.ts` (the guard at 59, 60 and 61 s, and `loader_lag` at 151 s), `test/staleness-limit.test.ts`.
- **Process lesson.** A migration that names a new database role, or a release that needs a new secret, needs that release's bootstrap **before** its deploy (CLAUDE.md Gotchas, `docs/runbooks/bootstrap.md`).
- **Not in this fix ([U], `docs/known-gaps.md`).** KG-353 (`findCoverage` grew from 0.5 s to 3 s), KG-354 (health still inside the load loop), KG-355 (job 7, Eijsden Q F216, `schema_drift` at chunk 2010-12-27; cross-reference KG-342).
- **The [agent-prod] criterion stays open** until a backfill night passes with live lag within the limits (KG-343): the owner starts the next night (`docs/runbooks/backfill.md` §3) and the per-hour lag query of §6 is the evidence.

### Nights 2 and 3 (2026-10-14/15 and 2026-10-15/16) and the queue fix (issue #29)

- **Night 2 did not run.** The owner scheduled it at 14:37Z with `systemd-run`, and a reboot at 17:01Z (issue #155) removed the transient timer: no journal entry, no chunk. With no backfill, live lag p95 was 16.7 to 29.1 s all night (`/api/v1/health`, every 30 minutes). Runbook §3 now says to check `systemctl list-timers` after a reboot.
- **Night 3 ran** from 22:01 to 05:03 UTC. Chunks rose from 2,072 to 6,083 and rows from 7.29M to 21.09M. 21 of the 41 jobs are done, 13 planned, 1 running. 5 more jobs failed `schema_drift` (KG-355). There was no `health_slow` and no `load_stalled`. NL-1's tier 1 stayed fresh (41/41), but **live freshness failed again**:

  | Hour (UTC) | Backfill batches | Chunk load p50 / max | Live p95 |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | 22h | 595 | 2 / 88 s | 631 s |
  | 23h | 63 | 57 / 72 s | 1,284 s |
  | 00h | 303 | 2 / 87 s | 2,037 s |
  | 01h | 1,996 | 2 / 12 s | 57 s |
  | 02h | 459 | 2 / 30 s | 760 s |
  | 03h | 253 | 8 / 21 s | 490 s |
  | 04h | 292 | 6 / 27 s | 377 s |

- **Cause.**
  - Backfill lines share the daily manifest with the live lines, and the loader reads a manifest in order (its cursor is a byte offset). So every unloaded chunk sits in front of the live lines written after it.
  - The guard let 30 chunks wait (`unloaded`). That number was sized for the runner's pace, not for load time: 30 chunks of 2 s are a minute, but 30 of about a minute each are half an hour. That is the lag measured (2,037 s, about 30 × 68 s).
  - The hour with the most chunks (01h) had the lowest lag.
  - Why a chunk sometimes takes a minute is not isolated (KG-356). There were 4 forced checkpoints since 10-01, and autovacuum ran on the yearly partitions in bursts after 01:30.
- **The fix.**
  - Migration `20261112000001_backfill_guard_unloaded.sql` answers `unloaded` for any chunk of an active job that is not in the ledger (it was more than 30). The runner looks again after 2 s (it was 15 s). It stays one chunk ahead of the loader, so at most one chunk waits in front of a live line.
  - A chunk the loader sets aside (quarantined or skipped) gets a ledger row with no counts and `reconciled` false, so the guard never waits for it forever. Its job fails `unreconciled`.
  - The job line of a `schema_drift` carries `drift`, the parser's fixed code.
  - The runbooks' `rwsc` and the unattended start call `rws_compose`, which adds the tunnel and owner overlays: no "orphan `rws-cloudflared-1`" warning, and no `--remove-orphans`.
  - Review round 1 (Q1, Q2): the guard counts the ledger by distinct chunk start, so a chunk fetched again after a `kill -9` counts once; a job is `done` only once its last chunk is in the ledger; and a run whose guard says `unloaded` for 10 minutes in a row stops `stuck` (exit 1) instead of waiting silently to the end of the window, for a chunk that never reaches the ledger (a damaged or recovered manifest line, KG-341).
  - Cost: at the usual 2 s load about 300 to 400 chunks an hour instead of up to 2,000 (fewer in a slow hour, where a load over 60 s also trips `backlog`), so the rest of NL-1 (14 jobs) takes about two nights.
  - Evidence ([CI]):
    - `resume.int.test.ts`: the guard at one unloaded chunk; for each way a line is set aside (a missing object, skipped; an object that does not inflate, quarantined; the tail's two-attempt quarantine) the chunk gets an unreconciled ledger row, nothing of the job is left unloaded and the job fails `unreconciled` (the test fails without the loader change); a chunk with two ledger rows counts once.
    - `pacer.test.ts`: the runner stays one chunk ahead of a loader that ticks every 10 s, with short sleeps only; a finished job waits for its last chunk; 10 minutes of `unloaded` in a row stop the run `stuck`, and a break starts the count again.
    - `run.test.ts` and `truncation.test.ts`: the drift code.
- **The [agent-prod] criterion stays open** (KG-343) until a night passes within the limits.

| 00h | 102 | 24 s | 33 s | 86 s | 97 s |
| 01h | 132 | 19 s | 28 s | 54 s | 74 s |
| 02h | 97 | 24 s | 37 s | 76 s | 87 s |

## 50. Amendment: fix #109, the Cloudflare Tunnel edge (2026-10-12)

What #109 built (ADR-0021, owner decisions of 2026-10-12): the public site can run behind a Cloudflare Tunnel on the current home host (KG-228), switched back to Caddy direct by one line. Direct mode is unchanged byte for byte (`deploy/tests/caddy-edge.test.sh` compares the adapted Caddy JSON with today's text; measured equal to main's). The domain moves to `waterradar.io` first, in direct mode and without code (`docs/runbooks/domain-change.md`); the tunnel follows (`docs/runbooks/edge-switch.md`).

**What was built.**
- **The switch.** `RWS_EDGE=direct|tunnel` in `rws.env` (default `direct`); `edge_mode()` and `rws_compose` in `deploy/bin/rws-lib.sh` refuse any other value before docker runs, add `deploy/compose.tunnel.yaml` from the release's own bundle in tunnel mode, and die if the overlay is missing or `/etc/rws/secrets/cf_tunnel_token` is empty. `smoke()` uses `http://` with `--resolve $RWS_DOMAIN:80:127.0.0.1` in tunnel mode. Deploys use `up -d` without `--wait`, so a `cloudflared` that cannot connect never rolls a release back; `rws-tick` restarts an unhealthy one.
- **The overlay.** Service `cloudflared` (`cloudflare/cloudflared:2026.9.3@sha256:…`, BOM row; 2026.10.0 was under the 7-day rule), uid 65532 with `group_add 61012`, read-only, `tmpfs /tmp`, `cap_drop: ALL`, `no-new-privileges`, 256m, 1 cpu, 128 pids, `GOMEMLIMIT` 230MiB, `--no-autoupdate --edge-ip-version 4`, metrics on `127.0.0.1:20241`, `tunnel run --token-file /run/secrets/cf_tunnel_token`, healthcheck `cloudflared tunnel ready` (no shell in the image). `caddy` gets `RWS_SITE_SCHEME=http`, `RWS_TRUSTED_PROXIES=172.30.41.10/32` and `ports: !override ["127.0.0.1:80:80/tcp"]`.
- **Caddy.** The site address is `{$RWS_SITE_SCHEME:https}://{$RWS_DOMAIN}`. `edge-https.caddy` (direct) and `edge-http.caddy` (tunnel) are imported at the top of `site.caddy` as `edge-{$RWS_SITE_SCHEME:https}.caddy` (Web Dockerfile, `.dockerignore` and the CI e2e mount follow); each defines the 421 catch-all (`:80, :443`, or `:80` alone) and the snippet `edge_site`, imported in the site block after the phase snippet: empty in direct mode, and in tunnel mode a 308 to `https://` for a request with `X-Forwarded-Proto: http` (review round 1, S6). Any other scheme value stops Caddy.
- **Host.** `bootstrap.sh`: the secret file `cf_tunnel_token` (gid 61012, group `rws-cftunnel`, created empty, never filled) and `RWS_EDGE=direct`, `RWS_WG_ENDPOINT=` in the template for a new host; `nftables.conf`: the set `cftunnel4` and one rule, TCP and UDP 7844 from `rws-tunnel` to it, no 443; `rws-wg-peer`: the optional `RWS_WG_ENDPOINT`.
- **verify-prod.** `--edge direct|cloudflare` (default `direct`, output unchanged). With `cloudflare`: the `Server` header may be `cloudflare` or absent; the owner listener passes on a refusal, failed handshake, timeout, certificate error or an edge answer that is neither 200 nor 401 and carries no `WWW-Authenticate`, counting only the owner site's exact headers (`OWNER_CACHE_CONTROL` `private, no-store` and `OWNER_ROBOTS` `noindex, nofollow`, exported by `scripts/lib/verify-owner-listener.ts` and held to `owner.caddy` by `test/caddy-owner.test.ts`; either suffices) as owner signs, through the pure `parseProbeHead`, so a Cloudflare error page (`Cache-Control: private, max-age=0, no-store, …`) passes. The new group `edge` runs: `edge headers` (no `NEL`, `Report-To`, `Set-Cookie`, `Speculation-Rules` on `/` and `/en/`), `edge html` (no `/cdn-cgi/`, `cloudflareinsights`, `rocket-loader`, `email-decode`, `challenge-platform`, `__cf_bm`, `beacon.min.js`), `edge tile range` (two `Range: bytes=0-1023` GETs of the current tile file: 206, exact `Content-Range`, 1024 bytes; n/a without a manifest), `edge not cached` (`/api/v1/health`, `/api/v1/meta`, `/status/capture.json`, a missing `/data/v1` file and a missing `/assets` file pass only with an absent `cf-cache-status`, `DYNAMIC` or `BYPASS`; `HIT`, `MISS`, `EXPIRED`, `STALE`, `UPDATING`, `REVALIDATED`, `NONE`, `UNKNOWN` or anything else fail; the 404 stays 404) and `edge runtime config cdn` (exactly `Cloudflare`, the name that selects the Cloudflare privacy text).
- **Privacy.** With `cdn` named the privacy page puts the CDN paragraph first with the stronger text (A§10, A§12.2); "no CDN" stays the committed default. The owner approves NL and EN (E5). After review round 1 (S4) the US / Data Privacy Framework / "`/assets` and `/data`" sentences appear only when `RWS_CDN_NAME` is exactly `Cloudflare` (message `privacy_cdn_cloudflare`); any other name gets a neutral text (`privacy_cdn_named`).
- **Other.** `check-bom` requires every compose `image:` to be an allowed variable or an installed row's pin; `scripts/record-frames.ts` records from `https://waterradar.io`.

**Where the build differs from the plan (stricter; the lead's decisions).**
- cloudflared's egress bridge is a network of its own (`tunnel`, `rws-tunnel`, not internal), separate from the internal link to Caddy (`tunnel_edge`, `rws-tunnel-edge`): the plan had one network for both.
- The trusted proxy is cloudflared's fixed /32 (172.30.41.10), not the plan's /24: a /24 holds the bridge gateway, which is the host, and a host or LAN request to the published port would be trusted with its `X-Forwarded-For`.
- Caddy publishes only `127.0.0.1:80` in tunnel mode, so no plain HTTP can be served on a public address even if a router forward stays open; R-097's "no inbound path" then holds structurally once the forwards are closed.
- The catch-all moved to per-scheme files: `:80, :443` kept a certificate-less `:443` listener in tunnel mode (measured with Caddy 2.11.4 `caddy adapt`), which the plan's "one `:80` server" needed to avoid.
- `RWS_CDN_NAME=Cloudflare` goes in with `RWS_EDGE=tunnel`, in the same deploy, and `edge-switch.md` checks the runtime config over loopback before the DNS switch: set earlier, the privacy page would name Cloudflare while the site is still direct; from the tunnel deploy on, Cloudflare sees no visitor's request until the DNS switch, so the disclosure still comes first (A§12.2). The owner approves the texts from the PR (E5).

**Evidence ([CI]).**
- `compose config -q` with `compose.tunnel.yaml` alone and with the owner overlay: `deploy/tests/e2e/run.sh`.
- Direct mode identical, tunnel mode one `:80` server with no TLS policy and no ACME: `deploy/tests/caddy-edge.test.sh` (13 cases after round 1, 14 after round 2, in the CI `deploy` job's offline loop; includes the `no-store` 308 for `X-Forwarded-Proto: http`; 14 cases after round 2).
- The overlay's networks, hardening keys, secret mount, no `TUNNEL_TOKEN`, the nft rule and the BOM pin: `test/compose-tunnel.test.ts`, `deploy/tests/hardening.sh` with `deploy/tests/hardening.test.sh`, `deploy/tests/rws-update.test.sh` (`RWS_EDGE` refusal, overlay, smoke), `deploy/tests/rws-wg-peer.test.sh` (`RWS_WG_ENDPOINT`) and `test/check-bom.test.ts` (an unpinned compose image fails).
- The stand-in run: `deploy/tests/e2e/tunnel.sh` with `tunnel-probe.mjs` in the `deploy` job after verify-prod (a container at cloudflared's address appends `X-Forwarded-For`; the limiter keys the appended address, a client prefix, `CF-Connecting-IP` and `X-Rws-Client` do not; `api`, `api-owner`, `caddy-owner` and `db` are unreachable; only TCP 7844 to Cloudflare's ranges leaves; the masked log; the token not in `docker inspect`), then `hardening.sh --ci` again.
- The privacy page names the CDN first in NL and EN, "no CDN" the default: the privacy e2e and `apps/web/test/pages-static.test.ts`.
- The new checks: `test/verify-edge.test.ts`.

**[U] and [owner] items** (also `docs/known-gaps.md`, KG-347 to KG-352): the real `cloudflared` (read-only start with `--token-file`, the `tunnel ready` healthcheck, QUIC or HTTP/2 on 7844) never runs in CI and is first proved at cutover; rollout step 1 (domain change); rollout step 2 (dashboard settings and cache rules, tunnel and token, `rws.env` lines, bootstrap re-run, deploy, DNS switch, close the router's 80/443 forwards, retire the LAN proxy, clear `RWS_TRUSTED_PROXIES`); `verify-prod.sh waterradar.io --edge cloudflare` after cutover; the KG-228 check; the privacy text (E5). Dashboard drift is caught only when `verify-prod --edge` runs (no Terraform).

**Gaps and risks:** KG-347 to KG-352 (KG-228 gains a pointer: fixed in tunnel mode); R-102 (home power or line outage), R-103 (Cloudflare's terms on uncached tile ranges), R-104 (Cloudflare as processor and silent dashboard drift), R-105 (token theft), R-106 (Cloudflare account compromise); R-097 updated; T-EDGE-1 new, T-CDN-1, T-API-3 and T-HOST-3 changed (threat model v4.56). D20 is widened by ADR-0021 (the whole public host may sit behind Cloudflare; the owner host never).

**Review round 1 (2026-10-12).** Two read-only reviewers on head e8202e6. Code review (Sonnet, xhigh): 1 blocker, 1 major, 4 minor, 5 nits. Security review (Fable, xhigh): 2 Medium, 7 Low, no Critical or High. Direct mode's adapted Caddy JSON was verified byte-identical to main in both phases. Each finding and its fix:
- **C1 (blocker).** `deploy/tests/e2e/Caddyfile.ci` had no trusted-proxy globals, so CI Caddy never read cloudflared's `X-Forwarded-For`. It now carries those of `deploy/web/Caddyfile`; `test/caddy-public.test.ts` holds the two equal but for the ACME lines.
- **C2 / S1 (major, Medium).** The owner listener check took any `Cache-Control` containing `private` as an owner sign, which a Cloudflare error page sends. It now matches only the owner site's exact headers, through `parseProbeHead`, with a test on a Cloudflare-style head.
- **S3 (Low).** Cache rule 3 is now "use `Cache-Control` if present, bypass if not" (our `/assets` 404 has none); `edge not cached` accepts only an absent `cf-cache-status`, `DYNAMIC` or `BYPASS` and probes a missing `/assets` file.
- **S6 (Low).** An origin guard in tunnel mode (`edge_site`, 308 on `X-Forwarded-Proto: http`) and the per-scheme files renamed `edge-https.caddy` and `edge-http.caddy`, imported at the top of `site.caddy`; direct mode still adapts byte for byte.
- **C4 / S5 (minor, Low).** Solved by dashboard settings, with direct mode left byte-identical (a log-filter change would alter its adapted JSON): runbook rows for IP Geolocation, Pseudo IPv4 and the Managed Transforms, a statement of which Cloudflare request headers reach the access log, and a `client_ip`-is-never-a-Cloudflare-range assertion in the KG-228 check; residuals in T-API-3 and T-WEB-4. C5: Browser Cache TTL "Respect Existing Headers".
- **C3.** T-REF-8 names `waterradar.io`. **C6.** `deploy-rollback.md` says a rollback past #109 in tunnel mode is refused and `RWS_EDGE=direct` comes first. **C7, C8.** `tunnel.sh` wording and a captured grep. **C9.** `RWS_WG_ENDPOINT`'s IPv4 form is range-checked per octet. **C10.** A missing `rws.env` reads as direct. **C11.** `hardening.sh` reads `RWS_EDGE` from `$RWS_ETC/rws.env`: with `tunnel` cloudflared must run and caddy may publish only `127.0.0.1:80/tcp`.
- **S2 (Medium).** The Cloudflare account as a root of trust: runbook prerequisite (hardware key, mailbox behind two-factor sign-in, one member, no API tokens or each rotated with the tunnel token, no Workers, Snippets or extra transform rules, the audit log read at each `edge` run), a row in `docs/security/secrets.md`, T-EDGE-1 and the new R-106.
- **S4 (Low).** Cloudflare's own sentences only for exactly `Cloudflare`; another name gets a neutral text.
- **S7 (Low).** `domain-change.md` §1a: DNSSEC before the proxied switch. **S8 (Low).** `RWS_WG_ENDPOINT` guidance (a dynamic-DNS provider name or a non-guessable label) and the residual in T-HOST-3 and T-WG-1.
- **S9 (recommendation).** Recorded in KG-352 (a scheduled `verify-prod.sh <domain> --site --edge cloudflare`, in the style of `contract-check.yml`), not built: scope out of #109, the owner decides.

The threat model stays at v4.56 with its changelog entry extended. A re-review of the fix diff follows, because the fixes add host code.

**Review round 2 (2026-10-12).** Code review: 3 minor and 6 nits (CR-1 to CR-9). Security review: 5 Low (SR-1 to SR-5). No Critical, High, Medium, blocker or major. Each fix:
- **SR-1.** `edge runtime config cdn` wants `cdn` to be exactly `Cloudflare`; `cloudflare`, `Cloudflare, Inc.` or another name FAIL.
- **SR-2 / CR-6.** The origin guard's 308 carries `Cache-Control: no-store` (tunnel mode only; direct mode still adapts byte for byte; `caddy-edge.test.sh` has 14 cases).

## 51. Amendment: fix #141 stage 3 B3, 41 FR-1 Rhine, Moselle and Saar tributaries and the LU-1 Gander and Mamer (2026-10-15)

What batch B3 of stage 3 of KG-250 (umbrella #127; after B1 and B2, PRs #146 and #151, which are merged) built: 45 rivers curated in `registry/rivers.yaml` the same way as in §41, §43, §46 and §48 (Wikidata QID, P403 mouth as the namesake check, the P402 relation or the relation that carries the QID in the extract of `geo.yml` run 38783923983). They cover the single-gauge FR-1 water bodies of Sandre zone A (Alsace, the Vosges, Lorraine) and the LU-1 Gander and Mamer, and two gaugeless natural connectors (owner, 2026-10-12). Their stations are placed on the river graph and get nearby measurements. ## 54. Amendment: roadmap 2 (all Dutch waters) (2026-10-16)

Roadmap 2 extends the map from the rivers that flow *into* the Netherlands to **all Dutch waters** (owner decision of 2026-10-03; issues #61 to #69; ADR-0022). It follows roadmap 1 (#13) and rebuilds nothing: it keeps roadmap 1's stack, data model, security invariants (all 11 of `CLAUDE.md`), audience rules (D22, ADR-0017), PR workflow and model rubric, and adds sources, registry rows, a water-body model and map layers. Until P15 merged, the issues were the plan; from this section on, **this section is the plan**, and P15 prepared the renumbering of the bodies of the issues #61 to #69 to match it (§54.2); the owner applies it on GitHub before the merge.

Roadmap 2 covers:
- **the rest of the Rijkswaterstaat network:** the lakes (IJsselmeer, Markermeer, Ketelmeer, the Randmeren, Volkerak-Zoommeer, Haringvliet, Hollandsch Diep, Grevelingen, Veerse Meer), the tidal delta (Rotterdam, Dordrecht, the Merwedes, Oude Maas, Hollandsche IJssel), the canals, the coast, the Wadden Sea, the Eastern and Western Scheldt and the offshore platforms;
- **sea level**, shown honestly: measured level, astronomical (predicted) tide and **surge** (measured − astronomical);
- **the smaller rivers that the 21 water boards measure** (Roer, Niers, Geul, Berkel, Oude IJssel, Dinkel, Regge, Dommel, Aa, Mark, Westerwoldse Aa, Kromme Rijn, Linge …), **one water board at a time, as permissions arrive**.

The IDs continue roadmap 1's: decisions **D24–D32** (§6.1), infrastructure **A9**, permission and notice requests **C14–C36**, build actions **Action D9–D10** and release tasks **E6–E7** (§6.2); ADR-0022 (A§13); water-board sources **NL-7…NL-26** (catalogue §2.8, §54.2). The non-code prerequisites are tracked in #62 until `docs/permissions.md` takes over the C rows.

### 54.1 Start gate

Roadmap 2 starts when **roadmap 1 is done: P0–P12 closed and the launch checklist signed (E4 in #14)**. P13 (#28, gated sources as permissions arrive) and P14 (#29, LATER: backfill in 2027) are open-ended by design: they keep running alongside roadmap 2, and neither roadmap waits for them.

**One exception: the water-board e-mails (C15–C36) may go out as soon as the owner likes.** Water boards answer slowly, nothing in roadmap 1 depends on them, and an early "yes" lets P21 start sooner.

**Early start of P15 (owner, 2026-10-16).** Roadmap 1's E4 is **not signed**: the site is in prelaunch (§44). The owner chose on 2026-10-16 to run P15 now. P15 writes documents, a generator and `off` registry rows only: no capture spec, no migration, no runtime dependency and no change of behaviour, so it does not touch the launch. **P16 to P20 still wait for the gate above**, and every date below still assumes that roadmap 1 launches on 2026-12-04.

### 54.3 Why the plan is shaped this way

- **Most of it is already open data.** The recorded NL-2 WFS snapshot (2026-09-29, in the repository) shows **247 live Rijkswaterstaat level locations** that roadmap 1 does not register. P15 makes the grouping exact; by name they are roughly:
  - about 40 on lakes and closed estuaries;
  - about 45 on the coast, the Wadden Sea and the Scheldt estuaries;
  - about 20 in the tidal delta;
  - about 25 more river points, including 9 on the Grensmaas;
  - **12 offshore platforms**, in cm MSL rather than NAP;
  - about 100 canal, lock and regulated-water gauges.

  There are also **92 more live discharge locations**. All of it is CC0 and served by the NL-1 adapter that already runs.

  **Exact counts: the generated inventory in catalogue §2.1 (P15).** Every figure of this kind in §54 (247 level locations, 92 discharge locations, about 250 more locations, the per-type numbers, about 40, 45, 20, 25, 12 and 100) is an estimate from the research of 2026-10-03; the generated block replaces them.
- **Forecast history is already there.** Since P1 (#16) the recorder has archived the forecast runs of **all 183 Rijkswaterstaat forecast locations**, the coast and the lakes included. Registering those series in P16 lets a replay load their forecast history from go-live.
- **The request budget is the bottleneck.** NL-1 asks one location per request, and roadmap 1 uses **373 of its own cap of 400 requests per hour**. About 250 more locations at sensible cadences need roughly 800–900. Rijkswaterstaat publishes no limit; the 400 is our own politeness rule. So Rijkswaterstaat is told first (C14), the owner sets the cap and cadences (D25), and CI keeps asserting the budget.
- **Sea level is mostly tide.** A coastal gauge swings 2–4 m a day, and what matters in a storm is the **surge**, the measured level minus the astronomical tide. Rijkswaterstaat publishes the astronomical tide up to the end of 2027 at 98 locations, plus measured and astronomical high and low waters (catalogue §2.1).
  - P18 computes the surge, labels it as derived, and never compares MSL with NAP.
  - Tidal water is never interpolated, in time or along the coast (D12, extended).
  - The astronomical tide lies in the future, and invariant 4 rejects future values in `obs`, so it gets a store of its own.
- **Lakes are not rivers.**
  - The IJsselmeer and Markermeer are held at seasonal target levels, and wind piles their water up against one shore while the other drops. So one gauge never silently stands for a whole lake (D27).
  - NL-4 already has seasonal classes for the IJsselmeer, the Grevelingen, the Veerse Meer and the Haringvliet.
  - Lakes become **water bodies** (polygons), not graph edges.
- **The delta is a network, not a tree.** The Noord, the Dordtsche Kil and the Spui connect the branches, and the tide reverses their flow. Roadmap 1's graph builder fails on any cycle, by design. P17 adds a declared **tidal zone** where cycles are allowed and no direction is asserted; everywhere else the cycle check stays.
- **Water boards need permission, one at a time.** The research of 2026-10-03 is summarised in catalogue §2.8.
  - Four boards state in writing that their data may be reused (De Dommel, Hunze en Aa's, Brabantse Delta, De Stichtse Rijnlanden), and none of them names a licence.
  - Vechtstromen forbids reuse without permission. Most of the others state nothing.
  - Few publish live levels in a machine-readable form: the HDSR Lizard API, Aa en Maas weir levels, Rijn en IJssel's Nexus layer, and the De Dommel, Rivierenland and Vallei en Veluwe ArcGIS layers without timestamps.
  - The umbrella organisations (Het Waterschapshuis, Unie van Waterschappen) have **no public live-data feed**. Their open map objects are CC-BY-SA, which is share-alike.

  So every board gets its own request, and the umbrella gets one question (C15). Each grant is a small PR in **P21**, in the audience the answer allows (D28): `public` with a permission record, `owner` if only personal use is allowed (D22), `off` otherwise. Until then the map keeps showing the German and Belgian gauges just upstream, and the Rijkswaterstaat points.
- **Flood and storm season.** Roadmap 2 runs from December to March, the Rhine and Meuse flood season and the North Sea storm season, on a site that is already public.
  - Every roadmap 2 deploy follows roadmap 1's rules: signed, pull-based, with rollback.
  - Recommendation: no roadmap 2 deploy while an official flood or storm-surge warning is active.
  - The first real storm surge becomes a fixture (Action D9).

**Audience of roadmap 2** (D22, ADR-0017; per source, never widened by a series):

| Audience | Sources | Basis |
|---|---|---|
| `public` | **NL-1, extended**: every D24 location (H, Q, MSL offshore), the astronomical tide and the high and low waters; NL-2 for discovery (stores nothing); NL-4 classes of the new series | Rijkswaterstaat CC0, unchanged |
| `off` → `public` or `owner` on a grant | **The water boards** (NL-7…NL-26; NL-5 keeps its ID; NL-6 stays `off` and is superseded) | Each board's answer to C16–C36 (D28); the CC-BY-SA of Het Waterschapshuis' map objects is share-alike and needs a reviewed decision before any use |
| `off` | Structure-internal Rijkswaterstaat gauges (D24); NL-3 (unchanged) | No use, or undocumented |

### P16 · Rijkswaterstaat: the rest of the network

**Window:** 2026-12-14 → 2027-01-15 (P16a 12-14 → 12-23; P16b 01-04 → 01-15) · **Lane:** data · **Depends on:** P15 (#63: the inventory, the water types, the structure-internal list); roadmap 1's NL-1 adapter and generator (P2b, #17); the forecast run model (P8, #23) · **PRs:** a capture + budget · b registry + loading (#64)

**Unblocks:** P17b (#65 snaps the new rows), P18 (#66 builds on the tide and the high and low waters). **Owner prerequisites (#62):** decisions **D24** (scope) and **D25** (request budget) answered; **C14** sent to Rijkswaterstaat **≥ 10 working days before the P16a deploy**, with no objection received; standing action Action D10.

**Goal.** Capture and load every D24 Rijkswaterstaat location within the D25 request budget:
- the lakes and closed estuaries, the tidal delta, the canals and regulated waters, the coast, the Wadden Sea and the Scheldt estuaries;
- the offshore platforms (cm MSL);
- the **astronomical tide** and the **measured and astronomical high and low waters**.

All of it is CC0 and goes through the NL-1 adapter that already runs. Registering the series also lets a replay load the forecast runs the recorder has archived since P1 for all 183 Rijkswaterstaat forecast locations. **Capture first:** P16a deploys the capture before P16b parses it (A§2 principle 1).

**Scope in**

*P16a: capture and budget*
- **`registry/seed/nl-1.csv`:**
  - every D24 location and quantity (H and Q) of the P15 inventory;
  - tiers per D25: `sea` every 10 min (the key coastal and delta gauges P15 proposes, about 30), `other` every 30 min (other tidal and river gauges), `slow` every 60 min (lakes, canals, regulated waters);
  - offshore platforms as a new kind with `Hoedanigheid` `MSL`;
  - structure-internal locations stay out of the seed.
- **`registry/capture.yaml`:**
  - `nl-1-obs-sea` and `nl-1-obs-slow`, offset from `nl-1-obs-key` and `nl-1-obs-other`;
  - `nl-1-astro`: `ProcesType` `astronomisch`, method F012 (F227 at Knock); monthly, at night; the window runs to the end of the published horizon, within 160,000 values per request; catalogue §2.1;
  - `nl-1-hwlw`: measured high and low water, `Groepering` `GETETM2` (`GETETMSL2` offshore); daily; a 3-day window;
  - `nl-1-hwlw-astro`: `GETETBRKD2` (`GETETBRKDMSL2` offshore); monthly.
  - Each spec keeps the NL-1 validity rules (JSON, `Succesvol`, `WaarnemingenLijst`, 204 allowed) and gets a `max_bytes` measured from a real payload.
- **Budget:**
  - `apps/server/test/capture/budget.test.ts` raises the RWS cap from 400 to the **D25 cap** (1,000, owner 2026-10-17) in any 60 minutes of a simulated week;
  - roadmap 1's specs alone stay ≤ 400;
  - at most two concurrent requests to the host (A§7.3);
  - `capture --dry-run` prints the busiest hour.
- **`verify-prod`:** `interval NL-1 <spec>` for each new spec, its cadence less 5 s.
- **The nightly contract check:** at most one more request (`nl-1-astro`), so it stays ≤ 9.

*P16b: registry and loading*
- **`scripts/gen-nl1-stations.ts`** (byte-for-byte generator) gains:
  - the new seed rows;
  - flags: `tidal: true` for coast, Wadden, Scheldt and tidal delta; `lake: true` for lakes and closed estuaries;
  - datum `MSL` for offshore rows (`TO_NAP` leaves MSL unconverted, so no NAP height is ever shown for them);
  - a curated `water_name` table: RWS metadata has no water name; never invent one, null otherwise;
  - structure-internal locations as `off` rows with a reason, so the loader knows them and stores nothing;
  - tier 1 for the key coastal gauges and the D27 lake reference gauges.
- **The NL-1 adapter** parses and normalises strictly:
  - the `astronomisch` series;
  - the high and low waters. The field that tells a high water from a low water is **[U]**: find it in the real payload and fail closed (drift) when it is missing.
  - New real fixtures recorded with `scripts/smoke-capture.ts` (opt-in), meeting the fixture standard: an astronomical payload, measured high and low water, astronomical high and low water, an offshore MSL gauge, a lake gauge, a tidal-delta gauge.
  - Caps for every new JSON shape (`boundedJson`), measured from the fixtures.
- **The astronomical tide is not an observation.** Invariant 4 rejects timestamps more than 15 min ahead in `obs`. It is stored outside `obs`:
  - **either** through the P8 run model as a run of kind `astronomical` (issued = `fetched_at`; the horizon is what Rijkswaterstaat published),
  - **or** in a table of its own.

  The plan picks one, with an ADR-lite line. Its readers get views in both families through `scripts/gen-views.ts` (`LATER`, a migration of its own), and only `apps/server/src/db/audience.ts` names them.
- **High and low waters** are stored so P18 can list each day's high and low waters with their times, measured and astronomical. They never enter the map snapshot as a station value.
- **Catch-up:** a seed to the data epoch for every new series (Rijkswaterstaat keeps decades), off-peak and within the D25 cap.
- **Forecast runs:** once the series are registered, a `replay` of the archived `nl-1-fc-*` lines loads their runs through the P8 model, back to go-live. The runbook `docs/runbooks/replay.md` gets the commands.
- **NL-4 classes:** the registry sync in `migrate` writes NL-4 rows for the new series by itself. Report how many new H series have classes.
- **Health:** tier-1 freshness and Q7 coverage for the new tiers. `/api/v1/health/sources` shows the astronomical horizon (the last stored instant per source), and the alert `astro_horizon` fires when it drops below 60 days ahead (the publication ends 2027-12-31).

**Scope out**
- Surge, classes, the crosswalk addendum → P18.
- Map display → P19.
- Graph, snapping and water bodies → P17.
- Water boards → P21.
- `OphalenLaatsteWaarnemingen` stays out of the core loop (catalogue §2.1).

**Deliverables**
- `registry/seed/nl-1.csv`, `registry/capture.yaml` (new specs), `budget.test.ts`, `verify-prod` checks, the contract-check spec list.
- `scripts/gen-nl1-stations.ts` and the regenerated `registry/stations/nl-1.yaml`.
- The NL-1 adapter extensions with real fixtures, goldens and properties.
- The astronomical-tide store (migration, generated views, `audience.ts`).
- The high- and low-water store.
- The catch-up seed; health and `astro_horizon`.
- Runbook updates (`replay.md`; a new `docs/runbooks/tide.md`); CLAUDE.md gotchas; `docs/threat-model.md` delta.

**Acceptance criteria**

*P16a: capture and budget*
- [ ] [CI] `budget.test.ts`: Rijkswaterstaat ≤ the D25 cap in any 60 minutes of a simulated week; roadmap 1's specs alone ≤ 400; at most two concurrent requests to the host.
- [ ] [CI] Every new spec takes its targets only from the registry seeds (invariant 1), and no structure-internal location of the P15 table is requested (test).
- [ ] [CI] `capture --dry-run` lists the new specs and prints the busiest hour (output in the PR).
- [ ] [agent-prod] After the deploy, `/status/capture.json` shows `nl-1-obs-sea`, `nl-1-obs-wide`, `nl-1-obs-slow`, `nl-1-hwlw`, `nl-1-astro` and `nl-1-hwlw-astro` fresh, and `interval NL-1 <spec>` passes for the three sub-daily ones (sea, wide, slow).
- [ ] [owner] C14 was sent ≥ 10 working days before the deploy, and Rijkswaterstaat did not object.

*P16a as built (2026-10-17, branch `claude/p16a-rws-capture-budget`)*
- **Specs and seeds.** Six NL-1 specs, none with a loader entry (CLAUDE.md "NL-1 roadmap-2 capture (P16a)"): `nl-1-obs-sea` (27 rows), `nl-1-obs-wide` (92, a tier of its own instead of "other (30 min)" in #64, so that roadmap 1's seven NL-1 specs stay byte-identical and the cut-back is removing specs), `nl-1-obs-slow` (207), `nl-1-hwlw` (83), `nl-1-astro` (79) and `nl-1-hwlw-astro` (79). `registry/seed/nl-1.csv` gains a `hoedanigheid` column and 326 rows; `registry/seed/nl-1-tide.csv` is new (astro 79, hwlw 83, hwlw-astro 79; the inventory's 79/139/89 count combinations that differ only in method).
- **The sea list** (27 rows: coast 18, Scheldt 6, delta 3) was curated by the build; the owner reviews it in the PR. With the three roadmap-1 key rows there are 30 ten-minute coastal and delta gauges. Six main tide gauges stay roadmap-1 `other` (hoekvanholland, hansweert, terneuzen, rilland.bath, antwerpen, moerdijk).
- **Budget (review round 1).** Busiest 60 minutes **946** (limit 1,000; 956 before round 1), roadmap 1 alone 373, at most 2 requests in flight in any modelled second. The astro window is `ahead: P400D` (owner, after seeing the 17 MB body). The tide specs got `space_ms: 179000` (a 180 s period, at most 20 requests an hour each) and a seconds field so that no spaced request meets the 10-minute NL-1 starts: `nl-1-hwlw` `30 0 0 * * *` (00:00:30 to 04:06:31 daily), `nl-1-astro` `30 0 20 1 * *` (20:00:30 to 23:54:30 on the 1st, `timeout: metadata`, 120 s, for the 17 MB body) and `nl-1-hwlw-astro` `30 30 4 2 * *` (04:30:30 to 08:24:30 on the 2nd; since #174 158 rows to about 12:24:30, "#174 as built" below). They never overlap each other; a first start, a catch-up or a retry can run all three at once, and that worst case (the busiest hour of every other RWS spec, 926, plus 3 × 20) is **986**, tested. The model projects every day-, month-, `L`-, `W`- and nth-weekday-restricted cron onto every day of the week, counts seconds at their minute and throws on a cron with no run in the week; every RWS-host spec must have a cron and no seed (tested).
- **Retry (every source).** For a spec with a cadence of at least 24 h, more than one row and no `expand`, the hourly retry after a transient failure re-runs only the variants that did not succeed (it skips `doneVariants`); one-row and expanding specs behave as before. This applies to every source's daily or weekly multi-row specs.
- **Build guards.** The NL-1 build throws on `groepering`/`method` for a Q row and on `ahead` unless the ProcesType is `astronomisch`. `test/nl1-seed.test.ts` fails if a P16a spec or a `CAPTURE_ONLY` id has a `LOAD_ADAPTERS['NL-1']` entry.
- **Growth.** Archive growth until P16b gives the observation specs a loader (measured on the committed fixtures, one request each, zstd -3 per object): sea 6,275 B raw / 894 B zstd × 3,888 requests a day = 24.4 MB / 3.5 MB; wide 11,298 / 940 B × 4,416 = 49.9 MB / 4.2 MB; slow 11,604 / 916 B × 4,968 = 57.7 MB / 4.6 MB; hwlw adds nothing while it answers 204 (no object is written; 83 requests a day). Together about 132 MB a day raw and 12.2 MB a day in the archive, about 4.0 GB and 365 MB a month. None of it is pruned before P16b, because the pruner deletes only payloads whose batch parsed `ok`, and a line of a spec with no loader entry writes no batch.
- **Contract check** runs 12 requests, not "≤ 9" (it already had 11): `nl-1-astro` is added, capture-only until P16b; its probe asks a 2-day window (`PROBE_PARAMS`, `ahead: P2D`), not the registry's 400 days, so the nightly body is small.
- **verify-prod** has `interval NL-1 <spec>` only for the three sub-daily specs (sea ≥ 595 s, wide ≥ 1795 s, slow ≥ 3595 s); `min_interval_s` spans 24 h, so hwlw, astro and hwlw-astro are judged by `freshness` (3 × cadence, 84 days for the monthly ones). Acceptance criterion 4 below therefore names `nl-1-obs-wide` and `nl-1-hwlw-astro` too for freshness.
- **Smoke.** One extra live request beyond the plan (7 in all, owner-approved) for the `GETETM2` question: hwlw at vlissingen answers 204 for a 3-day and a 31-day window, so whether measured extremes are published through `OphalenWaarnemingen` is unverified (KG-366); C14 asks. No `other:F227` exists at any live non-structure location.
- **`scripts/gen-nl1-stations.ts`** skips the tiers sea, wide and slow (registered in P16b); `registry/stations/nl-1.yaml` and `registry/thresholds/nl-4.csv` are unchanged.

*P16b: registry and loading*
- [ ] [CI] `gen-nl1-stations.ts` regenerates `registry/stations/nl-1.yaml` byte for byte. In it:
  - every D24 location appears once per quantity;

  - coast, Wadden, Scheldt and tidal-delta rows are `tidal: true`;
  - lake rows are `lake: true`;
  - offshore rows have datum `MSL`;
  - no row carries an invented water name or km.
- [ ] [CI] The new parser paths meet the fixture standard: real goldens for astronomical, measured high and low water, astronomical high and low water and MSL offshore; ≥ 90% line coverage of `adapters/nl-1/parse.ts` and `normalise.ts`; a fast-check property.
- [ ] [CI] Integration (PostgreSQL 18):
  - no astronomical value ever lands in `obs` (a future-timestamp test);

  - a replay with an unchanged parser writes nothing.
- [ ] [CI] A replay of archived `nl-1-fc-*` fixture lines loads forecast runs for at least one newly registered coastal series.
- [ ] [CI] NL-4 rows are synced for the new series, and the PR reports the coverage.
- [ ] [agent-prod] `verify-prod` checks:
  - `fresh NL-1 coast` and `fresh NL-1 lakes`: ≥ 90% of the new tier-1 gauges hold a value ≤ 45 min old at `meta.now`;
  - `health NL-1` is green;

*P16b as built (2026-10-17, branch `claude/p16b-rws-registry-loading`; issue #64, the last PR of it)*
- **Decisions Q1 to Q4 (owner, 2026-10-17) and what happened.**
  - **Q1, the high or low label: probe, else derive.** The probe of the type series (`Grootheid NVT`, `Typering GETETTPE`, `Groepering GETETBRKD2`, Vlissingen, 3 days) **answered 200 with 12 values** (`hoogwater` and `laagwater`, unit DIMSLS, method `other:F012`); the matching `GETETBRKD2` heights, labelled by strict alternation, agreed with RWS's labels 12 of 12. The plan said "stop and ask" on data; the owner chose **derive now, capture the type series later** (issue #174, KG-369). The loader therefore labels by strict alternation inside each time-ordered payload list and a break (from review round 1 also a value dropped between the first and last kept one, or extremes more than 10 h apart) is the retained drop `hwlw_unlabelled` (nothing stored for that series from that payload, KG-370). This deliberately deviates from the review prompt's "read from a field": no field exists in the `GETETBRKD2` payload.
  - **Q2, measured high and low water: probe a past month.** `GETETM2` at Vlissingen for 2025-09-01 to 2025-10-01, without and with `WaardeBepalingsMethode other:F010`: **204 and 204**. The extreme loader ships with the real 204 (it never reaches an adapter, so no golden) and a synthetic normal case (`nl-1-hwlw-vlissingen-nap-measured.synthetic.*`, built from the hwlw-astro structure with `Groepering` `GETETM2` and `ProcesType` `meting`); KG-366 stays open. P16b makes no capture change.
  - **Q3, lake references: two, at 10 minutes.** `krabbersgat.ijsselmeer` and `markermeer.midden` moved from tier `slow` to `sea` (sea 29, slow 205), both tier 1; the other lakes stay tier 2 until P18b (KG-372). Recordings: markermeer.midden H (200, 11,405 B) and, for the delta type, hellevoetsluis H (200, 6,236 B).
  - **Q4, live requests: at most 8, 7 used,** all on 2026-10-17 (the contact and info URL of the P16a metas, no X-API-KEY): markermeer.midden H, hellevoetsluis H, the two September 2025 `GETETM2` probes, scheveningen `nl-1-fc-3h-0` (200, 83,714 B, for D7), the `GETETTPE` probe and its matching `GETETBRKD2` heights (the last two not committed).
- **Build-time owner decisions.**
  - **Seed budget accepted.** The catch-up runs at `pace_ms` 85,000 (42 an hour, about two nights; live 956, live plus seeds 998 of 1,000). The P16a worst case, a restart that fires the three tide specs while a seed runs, reaches 1,038 an hour. The owner accepted it with a rule: approve the deploy between 06:00 and 22:00 UTC, pause a running P14a backfill, and do not restart capture in 00:00 to 05:00 UTC until the seed report says done (KG-377, R-108, `docs/runbooks/tide.md` §6). The worst-case test stays "live alone at most 1,000"; live plus seeds at most 1,000 is its own test.
  - **First release = tier 1.** The rule `first_release` = public, primary and tier 1 holds, so the 29 new `sea` rows and the new `epen.geul.cottessen` Q row are `first_release: true` (71 public rows; 41 before). The forecast-coverage denominator moves from 148 to 177 (the 29 new ones are all `other`).
  - **NL-4 stems.** Fourteen new stems get crosswalk rows (display classes, never warnings; typos kept as published, the `Verlagde waterstand` precedent): Licht vehoogd, Licht verhogd, Licht verhoogde waterstand, Licht verhoogde afvoer, Veroogd, Vorhoogde waterstand, Verhoogde instroom naar Veerse Meer: elevated; Hoog water: high; Extreem hoog water, Extreem hoog: extreme; Streefpeil, Strefpeil: normal (a zero-width marker, From = To at priority 10, that never holds a value; the order guard in `test/classification-pins.test.ts` skips zero-width bands). Verhoogde aanvoer and Verhoogd uitstroom uit Veerse Meer are **no_ref**: they are reversed-flow bands below Normaal at almen, genemuiden, markelo, zwartsluis.meppelerdiep and kats.zandkreekdam, which a one-directional scale cannot place.
- **Deviations from the plan.**
  - The label is **derived**, not read from a field (Q1 above).
  - `first_release` is **true** on the sea rows; the plan said every new row false.
  - **The debounce flush rule.** The plan flushed `bump_pending` "at the first cycle with no catch-up payload", which would flush after every paced request (85 s apart). The loader flushes when `now - since` is at least 1 h or `now - last` is at least 15 min, with one `bumpDays` per family.
  - **The tide views carry the obs history rule** (`lic_history_export OR ts >= now - history_window`), which the plan's "like `gaugeZero`" did not name.
  - **`NVT` is accepted as an extreme method** (and an empty one), beside F009, F010 and F029; astro and extreme_astro accept `other:F012` only.
  - **The astronomical horizon is the earliest series horizon** (review round 1, CR-4 and SR-3), not "the last stored instant per source": the earliest of the newest `astro` instants of the source's active, displayed primary series of its own audience, read with one primary-key probe per series (CR-1).
- **What the build found.** Registry: 429 rows at 391 stations (public 411 rows at 373 stations, 18 `off` structure rows); `tidal` 102 rows, `lake` 35; curated water names 44; the NAP H primary rows 300, MSL 12 (offshore only), TAW 2, NVT Q 97. NL-4: new public NAP H series with a class 164 of 232 (all public NAP H 225 of 300), new public Q 12 of 81 (`convert-nl4.ts` prints H 225/301, Q 27/99 over every tier); `nl-4-map.yaml` `none` 10 to 147. `registry/rivernet.yaml` lists 2,007 stations (+319), none placed (KG-378). Caps measured on the real bodies: astro Vlissingen NAP 17,003,443 B = 633,666 nodes, depth 6, 1 list, 57,600 values; hwlw-astro Goeree MSL 457,172 B = 17,072 nodes, 1,546 values. The plan's "about 100 days at 10 minutes is 60,000 values" was an arithmetic slip (100 days is 14,400); 60,000 is kept as the catch-up cap (about 416 days). `capture --dry-run` prints `998 (limit 1000)`. The old NL-2 recording drifts against the new registry (3 unregistered, 5 vanished; KG-379).

*#174 as built (2026-10-17, branch `claude/fix-174-getettpe-labels`; issue #174, stacked on the P16b branch of PR #176, so its PR targets that branch)*
- **Owner decisions (2026-10-17).**
  - **D-1, capture: fold into `nl-1-hwlw-astro`, no new spec.** The variants are `each: { typering: [GETETTPE, NVT] }` with the key `[code, hoedanigheid, typering]`: per location the type series first, the heights 180 s later. 158 rows a month (79 before), day 2, 04:30:30 to about 12:24:30 UTC, +79 requests a month. `capture --dry-run` is unchanged: `998 (limit 1000)` (live alone 956, burst 996, the P16b worst case with seeds 1,038). The type body is `Compartiment` OW, `Grootheid` NVT, the row's `Groepering`, `Typering` GETETTPE, `ProcesType` astronomisch, no `Hoedanigheid`, no method, and the same `Periode` as its heights (every body of a run is built with the run's `now`); the heights bodies are byte-identical. The builder throws on any other typering and on GETETTPE outside an astronomical extreme row.
  - **D-2, conflict: RWS's label wins.** The row is stored with RWS's label and counted `hwlw_type_conflict` (counted, not retained), one alert per payload.

  - **D-4, reviewers:** code review Sonnet high and security review Sonnet high, both read-only.
- **Deviations from the issue and the plan.**
  - **Folded into the spec instead of "a monthly spec on a day of its own".** A fourth tide spec would make the burst test 1,016 requests an hour, above 1,000. Variant names change from `vlissingen/NAP` to `vlissingen/NAP/NVT`; nothing persistent depends on them (`needsVariant: false`, no production lines of the spec yet).
  - **The missing-extreme spacing rule went from 10 h to 12 h** (`EXTREME_MAX_SPACING_MS`, both kinds). The real spacings of the astronomical extremes peak at 10.1 h (Hoek van Holland), 9.73 h (Vlaardingen), 9.4 h (Maassluis) and 8.0 h (Goeree lichteiland); under 10 h all 1,545 real Hoek van Holland rows would have lost their labels. A single missing extreme breaks alternation anyway, and a missing pair leaves at least 14.63, 15.0, 15.3 and 16.92 h, so 12 h still catches it.
  - **Item 3 (replay of archived `nl-1-hwlw-astro` lines) is not built:** the type window starts at the run, so a replay of earlier heights lines could only label instants that the run fetches again. Merge #174 before the first P16a/P16b deploy and there is no gap; if P16b goes live first, the past extremes between the two deploys that alternation could not label stay missing (KG-370).
  - **Item 4 (a measured type series, `GETETTPE` with `ProcesType` `meting`) is deferred** while `GETETM2` answers 204; its condition is on KG-366. No request was made.
  - **Stacked on P16b** (PR #176, not yet merged): the migration, the `tide` loader and the fixtures it builds on are that PR's.
  - **New deploy rule:** never deploy or restart capture on the 2nd of a month between 04:30 and 12:30 UTC (the run of about 7.9 h has no resume, KG-382). It joins the P16b rule (06:00 to 22:00 UTC, no restart in 00:00 to 05:00 UTC until the seed is done).
- **Live requests (5 of 6), 2026-10-17, through `scripts/smoke-capture.ts`, no X-API-KEY.**
  - **Vlissingen type series** (`vlissingen/NAP/GETETTPE`): 200, 1,546 labels (773 `hoogwater`, 773 `laagwater`). Committed.
  - **Goeree lichteiland MSL type series** (`goeree.lichteiland/MSL/GETETTPE`): 200, 1,545 labels. `GETETBRKDMSL2` has a type series too, so the 9 MSL rows get RWS labels (no KG needed). Against the committed Goeree heights, 1,544 instants are shared and all agree with the alternation label. Committed.
  - **Hoek van Holland heights** (`hoekvanholland/NAP/NVT`): 1,545 values, they alternate. Committed. **Maassluis and Vlaardingen heights** alternate too (kept in the ignored `.smoke/` only). So no agger double low water exists in RWS's astronomical extremes at the three Nieuwe Waterweg candidates; the agger case is tested synthetically, derived from a real body's structure (KG-380).
  - Only the words `hoogwater` and `laagwater` appeared; the question "stop and ask if other words" did not arise.
- **What was built.**
  - **Parser** (`adapters/nl-1/normalise.ts`): `normaliseTideType` returns `tideLabels` only; the drift codes are `tide_quantity`, `tide_typering` (new), `tide_unit` (DIMSLS), `tide_compartment`, `tide_process`, `tide_datum` (`Hoedanigheid` must be NVT) and `tide_grouping`; the datum comes from the grouping; `hwlw_type_unknown` (new, retained, counted per value, the word never stored) and the existing drops. `normaliseTide` keeps the rows of an `extreme_astro` series that does not alternate with `hilo: null`; measured `extreme` keeps its `hwlw_unlabelled` drop. `nl-1-hwlw-astro` dispatches on the first list's `Typering.Code`.
  - **Store** (`db/migrations/20261114000001_tide_label.sql`, `load/store.ts`): the table `tide_label`, `applyTideLabels` and `labelTide`, inside `commit(tx)`; RWS's label first, alternation as the fallback, neither means not stored and `hwlw_unlabelled`. Label rows join `n_rows`, `n_new`, `n_changed`. ADR-lite in ARCHITECTURE §6.
  - **Limit (KG-381):** a type payload that loads after its heights relabels nothing until the next heights fetch or a replay.

- *Review focus (#174), code:* the type body equals the probe shape and every heights body is unchanged; only `extreme_astro` emits null labels; `labelTide` runs inside the transaction and no null `hilo` reaches `applyTide`; the counts; a replay writes 0/0; the migration, its pins and goldens. *Security:* provider words are mapped to an enum and never stored, logged or alerted; SQL is parameterised; `tide_label` has no reader but the loader; no new egress, host, dependency or secret.

**Review focus**
- *Code review (P16a):* simulate the week yourself from the cron lines and the seed: the busiest 60 minutes stay within the D25 cap, roadmap 1's specs alone within 400, no minute starts more than two RWS requests; the astronomical and high/low-water requests fit the 160,000-value cap and send both `ProcesType` and `Hoedanigheid`; every target comes from the seed, no structure-internal location is requested, and `max_bytes` was measured, not guessed.
- *Code review (P16b):* byte-for-byte regeneration, flags per water type, MSL rows never get a NAP height, no invented water name or km; the high/low-water marker is read from a field that exists in the real payloads and a payload without it is drift, never a guess; MSL and NAP never mix in one series; timestamps keep their fixed `+01:00` and come out UTC; the astronomical tide never reaches `obs`, its views exist in both families and only `audience.ts` names them, and the new migration is pinned; the forecast replay really loads runs for a new coastal series; NL-4 coverage is reported; the catch-up respects the cap; health shows the astronomical horizon.
- *Security review:* invariant 1 (targets from registry seeds, no new egress host); politeness as a safety property (the budget test cannot be bypassed by a spec outside its simulation; backoff and the circuit breaker apply to the new specs; a 429 slows every NL-1 spec); parser hardening (every new JSON shape bounded; a hostile payload is drift or quarantine, never a partial write or a crash loop); invariant 4 (no future value reaches `obs`; the astronomical store cannot be read as observations by the at-T functions); invariant 2 and the view rule (generated, read-only views in the right family, no SQL concatenation); invariant 6 (the `X-API-KEY` never appears in a fixture, meta, log or manifest line); invariant 3 (names stay data).
