## 56. Amendment: P14f day-of-year climatology, empirical travel times and the storage review (2026-10-18)

What P14f (issue #29, group P14f) built, on the history that P14a and P14b backfill: our own **day-of-year (DOY) percentile climatology** as a new statistical classification basis (catalogue §4.7 item 8, which said "later: our own day-of-year percentiles"), **empirical travel-time ranges** per reach from cross-correlation (catalogue §3.7: "calibrate it from our own collected series by cross-correlation per edge and per flow class"), and the **storage review** that ADR-0004 asked for at about 50 GB (ADR-0023). The design is A§6 (`reference_value`, `reach`), A§9.1 and A§11.4; the classification is `docs/classification.md`. The runbooks are `docs/runbooks/climatology.md` and `docs/runbooks/travel-times.md`. It is "Part of #29": P14c to P14e are not all merged, so P14f is not the last group.

- **Decisions** (owner, 2026-10-18, AskUserQuestion; the plan's §1a).
  - **N = 10 complete UTC years.** A window of ±15 days pools 31 daily means per year, so 10 years give 310 daily means per day key. They are autocorrelated: the effective sample is of the order of 10 to 30 independent values, enough for an ordinal "unusual for the date", not for flood statistics. WMO's 30-year normal would exclude every series but the longest; catalogue §4.7 item 8 anticipated "1 to 3 years or a backfill"; the NL-1 backfill (from 1990) reaches 10, live-only series (since 2026-08) never do. Caveats are stated in `docs/classification.md` and KG-397.
  - **Order inside `statistical`: provider statistics first, our DOY set last.** Provider sets narrow first; the DOY set refines inside their interval and, where it disagrees, is outranked (collapses to the nearest edge). A D18 extension.
  - **Open upward.** At or below P10 is `low`; between P10 and P90 is `normal` (interval normal to extreme); at or above P90 is `elevated` (interval elevated to extreme). Climatology never yields `high` or `extreme` and never caps a lower-priority class: an NL-4 "Stormvloed" `high` still shows, an NL-4 low class between P10 and P90 collapses to normal. Priority stays operational, then statistical, then provider class, so at NL-1 stations with at least N years the DOY set ranks above NL-4: state changes there are expected and are in the golden diff.
  - **Travel times are shown as derived pairs.** The reviewed file feeds the next geo release as `reach.travel_time_h` with a `travel_time_source` starting `empirical` and as a `derived: true` pair in `travel_times`, so the upstream chain shows "indicative: 2–4 h (derived)". A derived pair never drives the map time shift (D-4 unchanged).
- **Defaults** (planner, §1b of the plan). Sonnet reviews (high, code and security) with Haiku posting; **owner-audience travel times left out** (the command reads only the public family); delivery through the reviewed repository file `registry/travel-empirical.yaml`, read by the geo build; the **climatology lives in the database only**, written by a one-shot command as `rws_migrator` through the `migrate` service; eligible series are primary level or discharge series (never a stage relative to a gauge zero), at stations that are not tidal or impounded, with `history_export` on; the kinds stored are `P10_DOY` and `P90_DOY` only (730 rows a series; P50 is computed and tested, not stored); a row is **valid from the run's start**; 365 day keys with no 29 February row; the storage ADR is a deferral with triggers.
- **Built.**
  - **Migration** `20261116000001_p14f_climatology.sql` (a partial index on `reference_value (season_from_md, series_id)` for the two kinds, and the CHECK `reference_value_doy_shape`: a DOY row has `season_from_md = season_to_md`, never 229, and `semantics = 'statistical'`). No new role, secret, grant, route, header or dependency.
  - **Configuration.** `registry/climatology.yaml` (`ClimatologyConfig`, strict Zod): `min_years` 10, `window_days` 15, `min_day_hours` 20, `min_year_share` 0.9, `percentiles` [10, 50, 90] and the `travel` block (`window_h` 336, `step_h` 168, `smooth_h` 6, `r_min` 0.5, `min_windows` 6, `max_lag_h` 96, `min_lag_h` 1). The pure functions take it as an argument; `docs/classification.md` prints N and the window from it.
  - **Core.** `packages/core/src/climatology.ts` (`doyClimatology`, Hyndman–Fan type 7, complete days and years, the pool of ±15 real dates, `utcMonthDay` with 29 February as 0228; a day key whose P10 is not below its P90 has no row; a repeated date throws), `packages/core/src/lag.ts` (`estimateLag`: windows, signals, interior lags, terciles of the upstream flow, class ranges and their envelope) and, in `crosswalk.ts` and `classify.ts`, the two roles `P10_DOY` (`<=` low) and `P90_DOY` (`>=` elevated) with source `*`, the DOY set candidate (sorted after provider sets, the label `DOY P10/P90 <first>–<last>`, `basis.source` the row's own source) and the generated section "Day-of-year climatology" of `docs/classification.md`.
  - **Server.** The role `climatology` (`apps/server/src/climatology/`: reads through `VIEWS[family]` in `READ ONLY` transactions, writes `reference_value` and the dirty log in one transaction per series under the loader lock), the loader guard (`load/refs.ts` leaves the two kinds out of the rows it compares, so no `refScope` payload closes them), the day read of the DOY rows for `readStates` (the forecast branch too) and `readHourStates` (frames and `/frames`; the UTC day key is part of the dedupe key), the exclusion of the two kinds from the static cache and from `series/{id}/recent.json`, and the coverage counts `climatology` and `by_climatology` (`Share`). The role `travel-times` (`apps/server/src/travel/`: `rws_publish`, public views only, one series-year per query, YAML on stdout, counts on stderr).
  - **Geo build.** `tools/geo/rivernet/place.ts` and `scripts/gen-rivernet.ts` read `registry/travel-empirical.yaml` (`TravelEmpirical` in `packages/contracts/src/rivers.ts`): a sourced pair always wins; an unknown or non-public station fails the build (`empirical_unknown_station`, `empirical_non_public_station`); `geo.yml` runs on a pull request that changes the file.
  - **Web.** The basis text for a DOY reference (`basis_climatology`), the agency text for the `*` roles on the Method page (`method_agency_own`), `method_form_doy`, `method_measure_series` and a reworded `travel_caption` (it said "flood peak", which an empirical lag is not).
  - **Fixtures** (real and public): `packages/core/test/fixtures/climatology/uckange-qmnj-1991-2000.raw` (Hub'Eau FR-2 `obs_elab` QmnJ at Uckange A850061001 on the Moselle, exactly ten complete UTC years, 3,653 records, cut from the P14b recording by `node scripts/trim-fixtures.ts --p14f`), and `packages/core/test/fixtures/travel/nl-1-backfill-{lobith,zaltbommel}-h-19950120.raw` (NL-1 hourly and 10-minute answers for 1995-01-20 to 1995-03-01, whole).
- **Criterion to proof** (issue #29; plan §4).
  - [CI] percentile classes only for at least N years: `packages/core/test/climatology.test.ts` (N−1 years gives none, N gives a set; properties) and the Uckange golden (1991 to 2000, 10 years, 365 rows, 15 keys stored; N = 11 gives `null`); the command's integration test (a 9-year series gets no rows and keeps its basis, a 10-year one gets 730 rows and a DOY basis in `/snapshot`).
  - [CI] they appear in the generated classification document: `test/classification-doc.test.ts` asserts the roles, N and the window; `node scripts/gen-classification.ts --check` in `pnpm check`.
  - [CI] the owner canary never in public output, present in owner output: the owner integration test seeds at least 10 synthetic years around the canary value on an owner series and finds DOY rows in the owner reference view, the owner `/snapshot` basis and the owner status coverage, and none in the public view, `/snapshot`, `/frames`, `status.json`, `recent.json` and `/api/v1/health/sources`; the travel command's test as `rws_publish` never reads an owner series.
  - The refScope guard (a DE-1 `refScope` payload leaves the DOY rows open); frames equal the snapshot (the hour state of a DOY series equals `/snapshot` at that hour's end); eligibility (a stage series, a tidal and an impounded station, and a source without `history_export` get no rows); determinism (properties and golden bytes for both cores); the travel UI stays indicative (`apps/web/test/eta-scan.test.ts` and the chain and Method fixtures with one empirical derived pair); the cold `/snapshot` p95 with the day read (`scripts/bench-q1.ts` seeds DOY rows for 300 series).
  - Golden states (`apps/server/test/classification/golden-states.golden.json`): 36 entries unchanged and 9 new `#doy` entries (synthetic P10 and P90 placed around recorded values).
- **Storage review (ADR-0023).** Decision: keep plain PostgreSQL, defer compression and Parquet, with triggers (the database at 40 GB, a measured dump restore over 2 hours, growth over 2 GB a month outside a backfill) and Parquet of closed yearly partitions preferred when one fires. The local restore benchmark (19.5 M rows, 1.8 GB: dump 14.5 s, single-job restore 22.3 s, extrapolated to 50 GB at 6.7 and 10.3 minutes before a 3 to 5 times slower VPS) is in its appendix and in A§11.4. The production measurement O1 was requested on issue #29 (comment 6251697447) and is not back (KG-403, R-109).
- **Live requests of the build** (all on 2026-10-18, contact `m@ikelwijkhuisen.nl`): 3 in all, the planned budget, all NL-1 `OphalenWaarnemingen` backfill chunks for 1995-01-20 … 1995-03-01 through `smoke-capture --backfill`: Tiel H (HTTP 204: no `other:F007` data that year), Zaltbommel H and Lobith H (both 200). The FR-2 recording the plan budgeted was not needed: the climatology fixture is cut from the P14b recording.
- **[U] items** (also in `docs/known-gaps.md`): KG-397 (the statistics are ordinal), KG-398 (the production run, and states before it), KG-399 (the travel file ships empty), KG-400 (no owner travel times), KG-401 (stage series not eligible), KG-402 (FR-2 aggregate twins as an input), KG-403 (the storage measurement is pending), KG-404 (no DOY band on the chart, P50 not stored, no per-class travel ranges), KG-405 (the cost of reading raw history is unmeasured in production), KG-406 (a changed parameter or a new year needs a run), and from review round 1 KG-407 (DOY rows carry no mark of the family they were computed for: an audience change closes the source's rows in the same change).
- **Reality differs from the plan and the issue.**
  - **The travel file ships empty** (`pairs: []`). The values exist only after `travel-times` has run in production on the backfilled history, so they come in a follow-up data PR (the runbook's §4, KG-399).
  - **Owner travel times are left out.** The command reads the public family only; the owner reaches variant keeps the public file's values (split parts stay null).
  - **Rollups are absent before `DATA_FLOOR`** (2026-08-01), so both commands aggregate raw `obs`, one series at a time (and `travel-times` one series-year per query, because of the 2 s statement timeout of `rws_publish`).
  - **Season was ignored for statistical references before P14f.** Only the NL-4 candidate called `inSeason`; a DOY set filters its own day key inside `classify` (UTC, not Europe/Amsterdam).
  - **The web read only travel pairs**, never `reach.travel_time_h`, so the file's ranges reach the site only as `derived` pairs of `travel_times`.
  - **Validity runs from the run's start.** Past states never change and the settled files stay true; a state from before the first production run stays non-DOY.
  - **The core travel golden is Lobith to Zaltbommel, not one reach.** Tiel to Zaltbommel answered 204 for 1995; the two recorded stations are not the ends of one reach and the golden runs with explicit relaxed parameters (window 240, step 72, three windows) and finds h [10, 20] over 11 windows; with the real parameters it finds nothing (40 days give about four windows, under `min_windows`). `lag.ts` adds one rule the plan did not state: a lag also needs 80 % of the window's hours paired (`MIN_PAIRED`).
  - **Step 0 found 10 candidate reaches**, all NL-1 to NL-1, with backfilled history at both ends that are neither tidal nor impounded (ijssel.2, ijssel.7, ijssel.8, ijssel.11, meuse.37, vechte.6, vechte.7, waal.2, waal.3, waal.6); with the same quantity at both ends and an interior lag of at least 1 h at most about 6 can qualify. Which of the 71 first-release NL-1 series are backfilled in production is not known from the repository.
  - **The climatology fixture is ten years of Uckange QmnJ** cut from the P14b recording by a committed rule (no new live request); QmnJ is a daily mean in l/s read by the test itself, not through an adapter. P14f does not depend on #183 beyond that recording: FR-2 aggregate twins as a climatology input are a follow-up (twins are in no view; KG-402).

## 57. Amendment: #184 stage 1, daily means and the method census (2026-10-18)

What stage 1 of issue #184 (KG-342) built, on the P14a/P14b NL-1 backfill (§49, §55). RWS sends a day's mean (`WaardeBewerkingsMethode` `GEM24H`, "Etmaalgemiddelde") as a second list under the **same** `WaardeBepalingsMethode`, and the normaliser keyed a list on code, quantity, datum and method only, so the daily mean merged into the 10-minute series: in the recorded Lith H chunk of 2003-01-29, 26 midnights were withheld as `conflict` (52 values) and 14 counted `duplicate`. Every loaded P14a chunk with such a list under the registered method lost midnight values. Stage 1 stops the merge and adds a read-only census that says what the replay must restore and which method groups stage 2 registers. Stage 2 (twin series per method, the contract key, attachment by the primary series, the NL-2 drift report) follows in its own PR, after the census is on #184.

- **Decisions (owner, 2026-10-18).** D1: instantaneous history under another method becomes a separate twin series per station, quantity and method, stored but shown nowhere (stage 2). D2: a daily mean (`WaardeBewerkingsMethode` other than `NVT`) is a retained drop, never merged, no series registered. D3: the GEM24H merge bug is stage 1 of #184. D4: history that is not in the archive (before each job's `data_from`, before the 1990 floor) is out of scope: KG-408.
- **Built.**
  - **Normaliser** (`apps/server/src/adapters/nl-1/normalise.ts`): a list whose `WaardeBewerkingsMethode` is not `NVT` and whose key, or whose `<code>/<Grootheid>/<Hoedanigheid>` combination, is registered counts the new code `processed` and never merges. An unregistered combination keeps its `unknown` or `datum` outcome. Forecast, tide and HW/LW paths are unchanged. `GAP`, `KNOWN_QUALITY` and `INSTANTANEOUS` are exported.
  - **`RETAINED`** (`load/pipeline.ts`) gains `processed`: a live payload alerts and keeps its object (`n_skipped`), a backfill payload counts it only.
  - **`loadNl1Backfill`** (`load/adapters.ts`): the body of the NL-1 backfill loader after the parse, exported so that the census runs the loader's own code.
  - **`backfill census --spec nl-1-backfill-obs`** (`backfill/census.ts`, `backfill/cli.ts`): archive and registry only, no database, no request, no write; NL-1 specs only (exit 64 otherwise). It prints orphan lines, one line per method group, per registered series and a totals line with `expect` (`docs/runbooks/backfill.md` §9). Every printed provider code passes a strict pattern or prints `"?"`.
  - **Docs:** catalogue §2.1 (GEM24H, the method table), `docs/runbooks/backfill.md` §9, `replay.md`, `schema-drift.md`, A§7 drop codes, threat model v4.66, KG-342 updated and KG-408.
- **The replay expectation, corrected.** The handoff plan (A3) expected `n_changed` = `requalified`. The store counts a changed row as `n_new` when it is new or already carries the backfill bit 512 (`inserted = old_series IS NULL OR (old_qc & 512) <> 0`, `load/store.ts`), and every backfilled row carries it. The stage-1 replay therefore shows **`n_new` = `restorable` + `requalified`** and **`n_changed` 0** (± `duplicate_lines_differing`), which the census prints as `totals.expect`. `apps/server/test/load/census-replay.int.test.ts` proves it: replay with the pre-fix loader, replay with the real one (equal to `expect`), a third replay (0/0).
- **Golden changes** (regenerated by `UPDATE_GOLDEN`, reviewed; `nl-1-backfill-golden.test.ts` literals and titles edited). Lith 2003-01-29: 5,724 stored becomes **5,750**, `conflict` 52 becomes 0, `duplicate` 14 becomes 0, `processed` 40, `unknown_quality` 10 and `outside_backfill` 1 unchanged (5,801 = 5,750 + 10 + 40 + 1). Lobith Q 2010-01-01: `unregistered_method` 251 becomes 241 plus `processed` 10, no rows. The two Lobith H goldens are unchanged. **§55's line** (5,724 stored, 52 `conflict`, 14 `duplicate`) is the P14b record and stays; this section supersedes it.
- **Method facts** (catalogue §2.1): the GEM24H value stamped `D 00:00+01:00` is the mean over `[D 00:00, D+1 00:00)` in fixed +01:00 (39 of 39 days within 0.6 cm on the Lith fixture, 24 of 39 for the previous day).
- **[owner] after merge and deploy** (also in the PR and on #184): (1) `rwsc run --rm --no-deps -T backfill backfill census --spec nl-1-backfill-obs > census-184.jsonl` outside 22:00–05:00 UTC, runner idle, loader caught up; attach the file to #184 (public NL-1 counts and codes only). (2) `replay --source NL-1 --spec nl-1-backfill-obs --from <totals.manifest_from> --to <today>`: the result equals `totals.expect`; `unreadable` > 0 in the census means the replay stops at that object, so fix it first. (3) The same replay again: `"n_new":0,"n_changed":0`. (4) If `orphan` > 0 (daily means stored as instantaneous rows before the fix, which a replay never deletes), O1 is decided then: a reviewed one-off cleanup in stage 2; with 0 nothing is done.
- **[U] items** (also in `docs/known-gaps.md`): GEM24H in live payloads (no live fixture has one; the rule covers it and a live `processed` alerts); the labelling rule over the whole archive (39 of 39 days on one chunk); the production census and replay numbers; O1. KG-342 stays open until stage 2; KG-408 (history not in the archive) is new.

## 58. Amendment: #205 Stage 0, the calm opening view (2026-10-23)

What issue #205 (Stage 0 of the calm map, built on P19a, §54) changed: the map opens on the Netherlands with its border gauges, far out it draws only the tier-1 stations, and the flow animation starts off. It adds no request, dependency, header or CSP change.

- **Decisions (owner).** 2026-10-22 (#205): open on the Netherlands plus the border gauges, not the whole basin; the flow animation is off by default and an opt-in; D10 is unchanged. 2026-10-23 (planning) Q1: the 12 MSL platforms (A12, D15, F3, J6, L9, K14, Europlatform, Goeree Lichteiland, Borssele Alpha, Hollandse Kust Noord Alpha, Hollandse Kust Zuid Alpha, Ameland Westgat; all tier 2 in `registry/stations/nl-1.yaml`) follow the tier rule and are drawn from z8 with their MSL label; D29's basemap choice stands (the cut stays; the world basemap's tiles overzoom), but "points at z0–6" no longer holds (KG-450). Q2: the south edge of the opening bounds is 50.2, not the issue's 50.6 (see item 3 below).
- **Built.**
  - **Tier filter** (`apps/web/src/features/map/stationLayer.ts`): `stationPoints()` carries `tier`. `TIER2_MINZOOM = 8`, equal to `BIN_MINZOOM` in `features/flow/reaches/bins.ts` (kept by hand, because that file is the lazy flow chunk). `stationFilter(layer, selected)` is `['step', ['zoom'], ['any', tier == 1, id == selected], 8, true]`, wrapped `['all', own, …]` on `stations-tidal` and `stations-msl`. It applies to `stations`, `stations-suspect`, `stations-owner`, `stations-trend-up`, `stations-trend-down`, `stations-surge-up`, `stations-surge-down`, `stations-tidal` and `stations-msl`; `stations-impounded` is unchanged (minzoom 8). `setSelectedStation(map, id)` sets the filters again with the selected id, so a tier-2 station chosen in the search stays drawn under its popup and leaves when the panel closes. An effect sets the filters again whenever the selection changes; no camera move.
  - **Opening view** (`StationsMap.tsx`): MapLibre's `bounds: [[3.2, 50.2], [7.4, 53.6]]` replaces centre [7.2, 50.6] at zoom 5.3. The `?s=` jump to z9 is unchanged.
  - **Zoom buttons** (`createMap.ts`): `NavigationControl({ showCompass: false })` top right, named from the existing `mapLocale()` keys `map_zoom_in` and `map_zoom_out` ("Inzoomen" / "Uitzoomen", "Zoom in" / "Zoom out"). The spike page shares `createMap` and has them too. `map.module.css` moves `.maplibregl-ctrl-top-right` left by `--drawer-w` from 48rem (beside the 26rem drawer, like bottom-right); `App.module.css` `.onMap .top` takes a right offset of `+ 3rem` (was 0.5rem), so the wrapped control row and the status lines stay out of the zoom column.
  - **Flow off** (`App.tsx`): the animation starts off for every visitor. The e2e build turns it on only when a spec sets `window.__rwsFlow`; production folds the check away (no `__rws` in the bundle).
  - **Legend:** one static note after `legend_honesty`, key `legend_tier` (NL "Uitgezoomd staan alleen de hoofdstations op de kaart", EN "Zoomed out, only the main stations are shown").
  - **E2E seed** (`apps/server/test/e2e/api.ts`): `tier` per test station (default 1); a new tier-2 station `nl.e2e.tier2` ("E2E tier two", 6.15 E 51.83 N, inside the Lobith fixture); `nl.e2e.platform` becomes tier 2, as in the registry.
- **Reality against the issue.**
  1. A zoom `step` nested in `all` is valid in a filter: filters compile through the style spec's `createExpression` (feature_filter, validate context `filter`), not `createPropertyExpression`, so the rule that paint and layout need a top-level `step` does not apply. GeoJSON tiles are 512 px, so the tile zoom is the floor of the map zoom: tier 2 appears at exactly z8.0.
  2. P19a (#207) was already in `main`: the tier filter also covers its `stations-surge-up`, `stations-surge-down` and `stations-msl`, and `stationPoints()` is pinned with `msl` too.
  3. The south edge is 50.2 (Q2): with 50.6 the fit at 1440x900 (about z7.07) puts Eijsden about 60 px above the map's bottom edge, under the collapsed timebar card, which covers about the bottom 100 px in the centre. Camera padding is no fix: `fitBoundsOptions.padding` persists in the transform and shifts every later zoom (the `?s=` effect avoids padding for that reason).
  4. Line references moved: the seed's hard-coded tier is at `api.ts:325`, the flow default at `App.tsx:108`.
  5. "On by default" was written only in PHASES (the P11a FlowToggle line); `FlowToggle.tsx`, `animation.ts` and threat-model T-WEB-6 never said it, and now say "off by default".
  6. `map.spec.ts` is the P3 spike page's spec (no app hook): the new specs are in `p10e.spec.ts`.
  7. From 48rem the zoom control would sit under the drawer: one CSS rule moves it beside it.
